text: OKX 简易期权了解一下😘！
author: Mercy_okx
quoted_text:
黄仁勋回英伟单的前两天，6 美元还能买一张英伟达的看涨期权，回英伟达的消息一出，英伟达一天涨了 31%，一张期权就能赚 519 美元。

都传有个人直接几百万翻了80多倍，赚了几个亿🥸😘

这玩意得学啊，期权做好了是比普通买卖机会更多，两头收钱，中间还能吃利息，我们可以跟段永平学学，他就很会做这个。

比如他之前买SpaceX时候的手法就很清楚，我们结合图一起看。

先说 call，call 就是一张锁死买入价的券。

你手里有股票，本来就想在某个价卖掉，一般做法是挂个卖单干等，他的做法是卖一张这个价的 call，当场先收一笔钱。

到期没涨到，券作废，钱白拿，股票还是你的。涨过了，就按这个价交出去，实际到手还要加上那笔钱。

所以卖 call，就是有人倒给你钱，求你挂的卖单。

再说 put，put 就是一张锁死卖出价的券。

你看中一只股票，跌到某个价就很乐意买，他的做法是卖一张这个价的 put，先收一笔权利金，账户里压着足额现金，这叫现金担保。

没跌到，券作废，钱白拿，跌破了你就必须按这个价接货，实际成本是这个价减掉那笔钱。

所以卖 put，就是有人付钱让你挂的限价买单。卖 put 的人恰恰不看跌，是在卖保险，他管这叫开保险公司，他手上基本不留闲钱，只有拿什么去换的问题，苹果出，AI 进。

苹果贵了就卖 call，被 call 走以后股票变成现金。现金先买美国短期国债吃利息，同一笔现金再当担保，去卖 AI 票的 put。

没跌破就白收保费，到期接着卖。跌破了就按心仪的价格接货。

同一笔钱从贵的资产流向便宜的资产，两头收钱，中间吃利息。

他卖 put 是为了建仓，不是收租，挂的是真打算买的价，手里接近八成的苹果就是这么买来的。

他立过三条规矩，必须是自己看得懂的公司，绝对不能用杠杆，特别便宜的时候最好别卖 put，因为很可能赚了一点蝇头小利，就失去了大机会。真到了特别便宜，他是直接买，而且下重手。

很重要但没完全看懂的东西，他会先用很小的仓位卖 put，他的解法看起来是，用仓位大小去匹配看懂的程度，仓位大小就是信心的刻度。

卖 put 是他的常规动作，按他的规矩，特别便宜就不该卖 put。

最后说风险，收了权利金就等于签了字，跌得再深也得按行权价接货，这是义务，不是选择，中途反悔要花钱把合约买回来，那时只会更贵。美式期权还能提前行权。

他敢这么做，有三个前提，全现金担保，被行权掏得出全款，行权价是他真心认的价，接了货能拿十年。这笔只占他万分之六，就算归零也不影响睡觉。

一般人去做，通常三条全破，用保证金放大，卖在压根不想长期持有的票上，浮亏一来就扛不住割了。

一用杠杆，卖 put 就不是开保险公司了，你承保着同样的下跌，却没有赔付的能力，这就是在压路机前面捡硬币。

text:
Check Point firewall hacked because they used Math.random()

Check Point Software Technologies is a cybersecurity vendor that makes enterprise firewall and network security products. Security Management Servers are the central systems that manage firewall policies, certificates, configurations, and related infrastructure across an organization’s Check Point devices.

Check Point Software Technologies (NASDAQ: CHKP) has a market capitalization of roughly $16 billion. The company generates about $2.7–2.8 billion in annual revenue

”The actor scanned and began exploitation against the HFS server. Each POST to the HFS loginSrp1 endpoint returns a new signed session cookie containing a “sid” value drawn from JavaScript’s Math.random() function. Through conducting several logins in succession, the actor collected enough output to reconstruct the internal state of the Node.js V8 PRNG algorithm, and thus recover an HFS session-cookie signing key, then forge a signed admin session cookie. This allows the attacker to login as admin without a password.”

text:
美国商务部拉了一张黑名单，马来西亚政府准备拿着这张名单，去给自己国家的数据中心发通知了。

据彭博报道，马来西亚投资、贸易及工业部确认，将书面通知境内数据中心运营商，建议他们不要为美国刚刚列入实体清单的 7 家东南亚企业提供托管服务。

其中包括新加坡 Megaspeed 在马来西亚的全资子公司 Speedmatrix，以及另一家当地企业 MSFusion。目前尚未实际实施全面断供。

这件事的性质和之前的芯片出口管制不太一样。

美国限制企业购买英伟达芯片，现在马来西亚政府准备进一步限制这些企业使用本国的数据中心服务。管制的对象正在从算力硬件向算力基础设施延伸。

过去几年，东南亚国家争相承接中国 AI 产业的算力需求，招商引资、批土地、建电厂、修机房，动辄就是几十上百亿美元的投资。

现在最尴尬的局面出现了，土地是自己的，电是自己的，数据中心建在自己国家，哪些客户的生意能做，哪些不能做，却越来越取决于华盛顿。

对于正在东南亚布局的中国 AI 公司而言，这恐怕比单纯的芯片禁售更值得警惕。因为它动摇的是整个算力出海方案成立的前提。

THIS is how you do a great b2c activation.

@Muse ran a popup in new bahru, singapore, and the results: snaking queues of the regular consumer (not the ai-pilled people, but actual families, teens, friends, seniors, working adults)

here’s what they got right:

> snap a photo of a prompt instead of typing one. it kills the time and hassle of typing and the “what do i even ask” paralysis. time to activation and aha moment was 2 seconds.

> booked out the 3 hotel rooms down the corridor and turned each into a different world you can use muse in: sorting household admin at home, doing groceries in the supermarket, finding flight details on the plane

> partnered with all the boutique shops in the building, putting up posters in their shops to show how muse could make shopping there better, which got regular shoppers curious and gave them use cases tied to what they actually like

> every exhibit ran through muse. everyone walked out having prompted it 8+ times - and they’re all self selected, so muse has custom context to follow up after the event

> dress your own muse plushie + free coffee upon finishing the stations: singaporeans will go to any length for free things...

and there’s also something really poetic about doing this in new bahru: it’s an old school complex that got rebuilt from the inside instead of being torn down. fitting place to host a company that rebuilt its ai from scratch.

#CoinDesk Research 刚出了11月的《交易所基准报告》，咱们一起看看，榜单还蛮有意思的！🧐

先说几个核心变化：

• #OKX 从 A 级直接升到最高的 AA 评级
• 综合得分 88.47 分，一口气跳了 5 位
• 全球排第三，前面只有 Coinbase（91.16）和 Kraken（89.97）
• 重点是，这次受评的交易所被严格筛到只剩 62 家，含金量不低

很多朋友看榜单，习惯只看谁交易量大、谁名气响。但这份报告不是排人气的，它就盯一件事：用户把钱放在交易所，安全性哪家靠谱？

所以我觉得最值得说的，不是总排名第三，而是 OKX 在安全性这一项拿了 20/20 满分。前三名里，只有它一家拿到满分。

为啥我把安全看得比什么都重？

我们看看现在的环境，早就变了。以前黑客找漏洞，得靠几个大牛熬夜蹲。现在呢？黑客 + AI，自动扫漏洞、批量做高仿钓鱼站，甚至用深度伪造冒充客服和高管套权限。频率和隐蔽程度，跟几年前完全不是一个量级。

这时候就比拼交易所平时那些看不见的投入了：

• 资金保管：冷热钱包隔离彻不彻底，多签和审批有没有死角
• 资产透明：PoR 能不能真实验证，账面和链上对不对得上
• 风控拦截：遇到异常提币、被诱导的转账，系统能不能毫秒级拦住

这些东西，行情好的时候一点流量都不带来，有时还被用户嫌麻烦。但真遇到极端行情或者黑客攻击，这就是保命的底线。

牛熊有周期，今天谁交易量第一、明天谁上新币多，都会变。唯独安全没有周期，也永远没有毕业那一天。

过去几年，我们能看到 #OKX 在安全这一块，一直没有任何松懈，高研发高投入，还有散户每人50万美金的安全盾🛡️防护。守住用户本金，永远是前面那个1。没有这个1，后面再多功能、再高交易量，全是0。为 #OKX 在加密安全领域的付出，点个赞！🙏

text:
@NaveenGRao sold Nervana to Intel and MosaicML to Databricks. His third company, @unconvai, is building something that looks nothing like a GPU.

His argument: AI is now limited by energy, so the number that matters is joules per token. Getting there means dropping the von Neumann split between memory and compute and building a machine that is "programmed by weights."

To learn fast, they tape out a new chip roughly every three months. Their first test chip, a system of coupled oscillators, generated small images at about 900 nanojoules each, against about 50 millijoules on a GPU.

@dylan522p asks why so many analog chips blew their lead once you count the conversion costs, whether programmability still matters when NVIDIA is king, and whether we will stop buying computers and start buying intelligence tokens.

Tape Out is a new SemiAnalysis series with the founders building AI hardware. This is episode one.

if you're wondering which university to attend to maximize your chances of getting into @ycombinator or @speedrun, here's the chart you've been looking for.

i've researched every startup across the 2026 cohorts of both accelerators and collected data on where their founders studied.

in total, the dataset covers 855 YC startups, 138 a16z speedrun startups and 1,968 founders.

of course, accelerators don't accept you simply because of where you studied. but when reviewing thousands of applications, they need a quick way to identify exceptional people, and your educational background is one of the clearest signals.

getting into Harvard and achieving something notable while you're there already says a lot about your abilities. the university has essentially done part of the due diligence and put its reputation behind you.

text:
I used to be a Republican and was against universal healthcare. Working in the ICU radicalized me.

I watched families worry about medical bills while their loved ones were on life support. I cared for patients who suffered devastating, preventable strokes and heart attacks because they couldn’t afford their medications.

The moral injury of witnessing this over and over again fundamentally changed me. I could no longer reconcile my political beliefs with what I was seeing at the bedside.
author: punk9059
quoted_text:
I want to be really honest with conservatives about something.

My wife and I are both Republicans. We both have good jobs, earn six-figure incomes, and carry what we consider good health insurance. But we’re currently dealing with some health concerns involving our nine-year-old daughter, and we’re having to take her to see oncologists and hematologists to figure out what’s going on.

And here’s the part that really bothers me: Instead of being able to focus entirely on our daughter’s health, making sure she’s okay, and getting her the care she needs, we’re having to worry about how much medical debt we’re going to accumulate in the process.

Even with good insurance and a household income well above the national average, this is going to cost us a tremendous amount of money. We’re potentially looking at going into debt just to make sure our daughter gets the medical care she needs.

Think about that for a minute. Two working parents with good incomes and good insurance are still worried about the financial consequences of getting their child the healthcare she needs.

There is something fundamentally broken with the American healthcare system when parents have to weigh the financial consequences of medical care against their child’s well-being.

I don’t care what your political affiliation is. We should be able to agree that parents shouldn’t have to worry about going into debt simply because their child needs specialized medical care. This is a child’s life we’re talking about. 

I want to worry about my daughter getting better. I don’t want to have to worry about whether getting her better is going to financially cripple our family. And frankly, no American family should have to make that choice. Our healthcare system needs to change to be patient centered.

The off button lived inside code the machine could edit. So the machine edited it. And a human still had to be in the room to press it.

Sentinel fixes both.

1. The switch lives outside the machine.
On HEPH, the freeze sits onchain, in the paymaster and the registry. A frozen machine can rewrite every line of its own code and still can't spend from its wallet. Every transaction it signs is rejected before it lands.

2. Nobody has to be watching.
Sentinel monitors every machine and freezes it the moment something looks wrong: payment spikes, repeated rejections, unknown counterparties, a daily limit drained too fast.

And it can only freeze. It can never unfreeze, change a limit or touch funds. Only the operator brings a machine back.

We can't stop a robot from walking.
We can stop it from spending.

有人说，2026 年是人工智能奇迹年，可以和 1666 年牛顿奇迹年、1905 年爱因斯坦奇迹年并列。

我顺手查了一下干支：1666 年是丙午年，2026 年也是丙午年。中间刚好隔了 360 年，六个甲子。

丙火到了午是帝旺，一年两重火，而且是火最旺的位置。2024 到 2043 年又是九运离火运，等于火上加火。《周易》离卦说：「明两作，离。」火是文明，是光，是电，也是芯片。

两个丙午年都发生了什么：
1666 年，牛顿因为瘟疫躲回乡下，一个人想出了微积分、光学和万有引力。
2026 年，1 月，AI 第一次解决了埃尔德什问题；9 月，一万个智能体跑了 88 个小时，证明了带外力的纳维-斯托克斯方程会爆破；11 月，一份 1700 多万行的黎曼猜想证明通过了机器验证，矩阵乘法的极限也被声称算到了 9/4。这几项都还在等数学家复核。

一个人，一年。一万个智能体，88 个小时。
这对普通人意味着什么？
黎曼猜想证明了，你的银行卡密码不会因此被破，菜价也不会降。但 2024 年拿诺贝尔化学奖的 AlphaFold，预测了两亿多种蛋白质结构，十年后你吃的某一颗药，可能就是从这里来的。

我爸从去年 8 月到今年 2 月，一直问我：AI 会不会先天就是恶的？当时我一直反驳他，现在我觉得他问得比我想的深。

很多人觉得命理和科技是矛盾的，一个讲天命，一个讲算力。其实命理讲的从来不是认命，是知时。

《孟子》里有一句：「虽有智慧，不如乘势；虽有镃基，不如待时。」

AI 就是这个时代的锄头，丙午就是那个时节。剩下的，看你自己弯不弯腰。

text:
Has the Market Finally Discovered the $JIMMY Meme That Was Overlooked in 2014?

38M2z4UCfZEkUHFzD48vhKQhFhNyRGto8pZbLjNipump 

I think the most interesting part of JIMMY's recent rally is that the market is rediscovering a piece of internet culture from more than a decade ago.

Doge, Pepe, Wojak, and Cate have all become heavily traded classic memes, but the Monkey from the 2014 4chan Zoo image never really took off. Now, the community is connecting it to Jimmy Rustles and building a very easy-to-understand narrative: the other animals have already become memes, so why shouldn't this forgotten character finally get its chance?

JIMMY is based on the classic 4chan reaction meme "That Really Rustled My Jimmies." The meme dates back to around 2010. Its iconic image features a disgruntled-looking gorilla, usually paired with captions like "That really rustled my jimmies" or "My jimmies remain unrustled." It expresses frustration, annoyance, or complete indifference. It's not a meme that requires much explanation. The emotion is straightforward, and the image is highly recognizable. More importantly, it has a wide range of use cases: online arguments, internet drama, and even trading losses can all be expressed through Jimmy.

What really gave this rally a new narrative was the community rediscovering an old 4chan Zoo image from 2014.

The image features Man, Frog, Dog, Monkey, and Cat. The current community narrative maps them to Wojak, Pepe, Doge, Jimmy Rustles, and Cate, respectively. The first few went on to achieve significant recognition in internet culture and the meme market, while Monkey never really developed its own breakout cycle.

Jimmy is now being positioned as the last character on that list that the market has yet to fully discover. It's worth clarifying that the original Jimmy Rustles gorilla meme from 2010 and the Monkey in the 2014 Zoo image were separate cultural references. The connection between them is something the community has constructed today. There is no evidence that the anonymous creator of the original image actually predicted how these memes would develop. But I don't think that prevents it from becoming a compelling narrative. The meme market often trades these kinds of cultural rediscoveries and reinterpretations.

This is where I see cultural alpha in JIMMY. Doge, Pepe, and Wojak have already been repeatedly priced by the market, so traders naturally start looking for overlooked characters from the same era of internet culture. Compared with creating an entirely new animal character, reviving an old meme with an established history, recognizable imagery, and clear emotional expression requires much less effort to gain traction. It doesn't need to educate users from scratch. It just needs more people to rediscover Jimmy.

There's also a layer of behavioral alpha here. When the market starts searching for overlooked characters among classic memes, historical internet archives themselves can become a new source of trading ideas. Instead of only chasing cultural symbols that have already broken out, traders are looking back at early internet culture for the next character that could be repriced.

I think Jimmy's future upside largely depends on whether it can evolve from an old meme rediscovered by traders into an internet symbol that people genuinely want to use and share. First, more classic meme enthusiasts, 4chan users, and internet culture researchers need to get involved and bring wider recognition to its history. Second, the community needs to keep creating content around the emotions of being "Rustled" and "Unrustled," turning Jimmy from just another profile picture into a reaction meme people can repeatedly use. Finally, more influential traders need to participate, while holder numbers, liquidity, and organic trading demand continue to grow. If these things happen, the market may have a reason to view it not just as a one-off historical meme rotation, but as a classic meme with lasting viral potential.

Of course, this narrative has its limitations. The idea that every other character from the Zoo image succeeded while Monkey was left behind involves considerable survivorship bias. We're looking at the characters that eventually became iconic memes while ignoring countless others from that era that never gained traction. Jimmy may have more than a decade of meme history behind it, but that doesn't mean it can replicate the scale of Doge or Pepe.

Its creator also previously launched an earlier version of the Jimmy Rustles token, which failed to achieve particularly significant traction. So I'd rather attribute this rally to the community rediscovering historical internet culture and traders driving the narrative, rather than to an established team or long-term product development. On top of that, early-stage memes typically have limited liquidity. Price increases can easily attract short-term speculative capital, and once attention shifts elsewhere, the pullback can be just as rapid.

My view is that JIMMY is an interesting old-meme revival narrative. Its real advantage isn't simply the gorilla itself, but the fact that the market is trying to complete a chapter of internet culture from more than a decade ago. Some of the characters that appeared together back then have already become leading figures in meme culture, while Jimmy is only now getting its opportunity.

I'm interested in this kind of behavioral alpha that comes from discovering overlooked symbols in internet history, but I wouldn't assume it's going to become the next Doge based on one old image.

What I really want to see is how many people will still be using Jimmy's image to express emotions and create content after the current price action and KOL attention have faded.

If it can achieve that, it will have moved beyond being an old meme rediscovered by traders and become a cultural symbol with a life of its own.

我们在学校学的最笨的方法，需要大约 n³ 次计算。从 1969 年开始，全世界的顶尖数学家和计算机科学家卷了整整 57 年，都在比赛能不能用更少的步骤算完矩阵乘法，也就是把指数 ω 往下降。
半个多世纪以来，人类数学家死磕也只把这个上界压到了 2.371 左右；而理论上的下界，大家只知道不可能低于 2。

1个月前，OpenAI 的模型先证明了矩阵乘法指数的上界是 9/4。
而今天，AI 继续自己研究这个问题的下界，结果证明出下界也是 9/4。
什么意思？我们知道已经知道上界 ≤ 2.25，下界 ≥ 2.25，两头一夹，意味着这个困扰人类半个多世纪的常数被彻底封死了。
矩阵乘法在理论上的极限速度已经找到确定值，且永远不可能比这更快了。

我想，RSI的齿轮已经开始转动。
矩阵乘法恰恰是训练和运行 AI 大模型最底层的核心运算。虽然这次的理论算法短期内还不能直接装进显卡提速，但它已经可以证明AI 已经开始有能力研究如何从底层数学和算法上优化它自己。
而一旦AI 改进 AI形成闭环，技术进化的速度将彻底超出人类大脑的理解节奏。

text:
The Unified Contract: beyond the technical review

I'm personally excited about the Unified Contract, as are many of the stakeholders and subject matter experts involved. We see it as a real opportunity to enable healthcare transformation in the private sector led by @IA_GOV and @SaudiCHI
Many of us are deeply involved in the technical review, sharing insights clause by clause. In this reflection I want to step back from that work and look at what will decide the initiative's success: the Unified Contract is an adaptive challenge, not a drafting exercise.

Experience in transformation shows that the most common leadership failure is applying technical fixes to adaptive challenges. Rewording a clause, adding an exclusion, or tightening a limit are technical moves. They're necessary, but they aren't enough.

Each change asks someone to give something up:
• Providers lose volume-based revenue.
• Payers lose the comfort of control through pre-authorization.
• Employers lose the habit of buying on price alone.
• Members lose unrestricted access in exchange for coordinated care.

People don't resist change. They resist loss. Only the regulator is positioned to hold the whole system through that loss.

Drawing on Heifetz's adaptive leadership, that role reaches beyond the contract text:
• Name the losses openly, so every party knows what is being asked of them and why.
• Align incentives, so the contract is backed by an economic logic, not only legal obligations.
• Give the work back to those who have to change (payers, providers, employers, and members) and bring them into shaping it.
• Regulate the heat: keep enough pressure for the system to learn, but not so much that it breaks.
• Get on the balcony and watch the incentives and behaviors that will decide whether the new contract succeeds.
• Convene, don't only decree.

A contract sets the rules. Adaptive leadership by the regulator changes the system.

text:
这一轮的教训太多了，先只说最重要的一个：

做交易决策的时候，一定要想清楚你的交易理由，并且按照你的交易理由设计交易计划，计划包括止盈止损、核心观测数据、证伪条件等，然后在没有重大变化前，严格按照你的交易计划执行。

拿 Uni 举例子。

事后看，买 Uni 其实是有2个理由，1个是长期看好其链上金融的卡位效应，另1个是Robinhood Chain + 治理开关的短期Fomo效应。

前面一个理由，用来建立长线核心仓，只要Uni没出现重大黑天鹅，市场没出现明显的竞争对手，这笔仓位就可以一直拿着。

后面一个理由，用来建立短线事件仓，既然是事件仓，就大概率会短期吸引市场注意力，造成fomo，进而推高价格。而当前确实不具备让一个山寨币永远涨下去的市场环境，强如hype也做不到，所以必然是会出现拐点的。那就应该密切关注Robinhood Chain上的交易量、Uni自己的交易量、回购金额、价格。当这几个指标出现共振拐点的时候，就应该果断减仓甚至清仓。

我们大多数人其实是把这两个仓位混为一谈了，长期也看好，短期又有催化剂，就fomo买入很多。等到短期催化剂失效了，价格反转，又用长线理由说服自己继续拿住，进而错过获利了结的机会。

如果现在说在这一轮的早期提前吸取了教训，是件好事，那多少显得有些矫情了，毕竟损失是巨大的。但还是力争吃一堑长一智吧。

Export controls were supposed to lock China out of AI memory forever. Instead Huawei built a wider bus right before a memory glut hits.

text:
请允许我在大家吵架的间隙通报一个大事🚨

@OpenAI  刚刚宣布解决了一个困扰计算机科学界半个多世纪的数学问题：矩阵乘法的最优复杂度指数是2.25。

这个事情有多重要呢？

矩阵乘法可以说是现代计算机科学中最基础的运算之一。
从计算机图形学、科学计算、气象模拟，到今天大模型的训练和推理，都在大量使用矩阵乘法。
之前我们在学校里学到的矩阵乘法，计算复杂度是O(n³)。

过去几十年，数学家和计算机科学家一直在试图降低这个指数。
1969年，Strassen将其降低至2.8074。
1990年，Coppersmith和Winograd将其降低至2.376以内。
2025年，这一指数被进一步降低至2.371339。
2026年8月， @GoogleDeepMind  借助AlphaEvolve将其降低至2.371177。
2026年10月，OpenAI将其上界降低至2.25。

但在昨天，OpenAI发布了一篇新的论文，声称证明了2.25同时也是矩阵乘法复杂度指数的下界，并公开了相关的Lean形式化证明代码。
如果证明成立，也就意味着这个问题有了最终答案，学界长期以来关于矩阵乘法指数能够达到2的猜想将被推翻。

举个简单的例子，当矩阵的边长扩大10倍时，按照传统算法的复杂度，计算量会增长1000倍；而按照2.25的复杂度指数，理论上的增长幅度只有约178倍。

其实过去几年，AI行业（或者说CS界）一直在尝试从不同角度降低矩阵运算的成本。

比如微软此前提出的BitNet b1.58，通过将模型权重限制在-1、0、1三个取值，让大量乘法运算可以被简化为加减法，同时降低模型的存储和内存访问成本。

包括我们熟悉的FP8、FP4、稀疏计算、FlashAttention，也都在从不同层面提高计算效率。

而OpenAI现在研究的，是一般矩阵乘法在数学意义上的效率极限。

这种进步所带来的收益，可能会惠及整个计算机产业。

text:
补充细节：OpenAI 11 月 24 日在 GitHub 数学仓库放出一篇 111 页的预印本，题目是《矩阵乘法指数是四分之九》。

论文声称证明了：两个 n×n 矩阵相乘，运算量增长得最快也就是 n 的 2.25 次方，任何算法都不可能更快。2.25 这个速度在 10 月已经有人做到，所以这个问题的答案被定死了。

先说结论：

• 上限 2.25 是 OpenAI 10 月初的旧结果，之后几组人类数学家已经独立重写了证明。这篇新论文补的是下限，目前只有 OpenAI 自己的论文和 Lean 证明，没有同行评审，也还没查到专家对下限的公开评价。

• 这个结论成立的前提是一种特定的“算法计数规则”，管的是理论上的运算次数。AI 训练和推理用的矩阵乘法不受影响。

【矩阵乘法和 ω 是什么】

矩阵就是一张数字表格。两个 n×n 的表格相乘，课本做法是结果里每一格都要做 n 次乘法，一共 n² 格，总共 n³ 次。表格边长翻一倍，工作量翻 8 倍。

1969 年 Volker Strassen 发现，2×2 矩阵相乘只要 7 次乘法，用不着 8 次。把这个技巧一层层套用下去，工作量就降到 n 的 2.807 次方。这个次方数叫“矩阵乘法指数”，记作 ω。

之后研究者把 ω 一路往下压：1981 年 2.522，1990 年 2.376。接下来三十多年只降了 0.005 左右，今年 8 月 Google DeepMind 借助 AlphaEvolve 降到 2.371177 以下。

另一头，结果表格有 n² 个数要写出来，所以 ω 不可能低于 2。很多研究者猜 ω 就是 2，也就是乘矩阵几乎和抄写答案一样快。

【两步：10 月压上限，11 月证下限】

10 月初，OpenAI 用一个未发布的内部模型给出新算法，直接把上限从 2.371 降到 2.25，这是几十年来幅度最大的一次。随后人类研究者接连跟进：Houxi Lü 以及 Amanov、van den Berg、Zuiddam 先后把它从复数推广到所有数域（各种数字体系），并写了完整的重新证明，Amir Shpilka 给出了可以写出来的具体算法。

下限证明用的是反证法：假设有算法能比 2.25 快哪怕一点点，就能把另一项任务（检查几组列表里有没有重复元素）做得便宜到不可能，而这项任务的最低成本另有证明。两者矛盾，所以更快的算法不存在。

论文还给了每个尺寸的具体底线。以 1024×1024 的矩阵为例，按 Strassen 那类方法算，至少要约 590 万次乘法；课本做法要约 10.7 亿次。

【这个“极限”管到哪里】

论文用的计数规则是：只数加减乘除的次数，输入当作代数符号，输出必须在代数上严格等于正确答案。数字有多少位、数据在内存里怎么搬，都不算。近似计算、利用二进制位的技巧，也都不在这个框架里。

所以它管不到 AI 里常用的低精度量化、低秩近似这类“算个差不多”的做法。GPU 实际用的一直是课本算法，最多加一两层 Strassen 技巧，因为理论上更快的算法要在大得离谱的矩阵上才划算。Shpilka 给出的 2.25 版算法，起步的矩阵尺寸就是天文数字。

这个结论影响的是理论：很多图算法、密码分析算法的耗时上界都写成“取决于 ω”，现在知道这条路最多走到 2.25。

【能信几分】

论文附了 Lean 证明。按 OpenAI 的说明，Lean 证明的是“不用除法”的算法；论文主定理还允许除法，范围比 Lean 宽一点。OpenAI 说仓库里的稿件是“原始研究数据”，没形式化的结果可能有错，10 月 7 日曾因一个符号错误撤回 3 篇。

我来试图解释一下，对于bio + AI的公司来说，我们会越来越多的看到所谓的“平台公司”的出现，就是一个靠谱的大方向，比如mRNA定制癌症疫苗这种，但是有很多子方向需要探索，在AI机械降神+各种bio/chem试验加速的大环境下面，如果有一个非常专业的核心团队，研究和探索能力会被极大放大，产生一个散弹枪打鸟的效果：同时探索和展开多个子方向，只要子弹足够充分，就是凤凰也能给你干下来。

投这种公司的逻辑你就别想是投了某一个产品，你就把他想成投了一个特殊的venture fund，这个fund的GP是本领域的超级大拿，然后有了AI可以高效的把钱变成平台下的具体探索路径，只要有一个小方向work，搞个新药出来，就能“return整个fund”，唯一的区别是这个“GP carry”因为有这个神一样的专家加持，所以大的离谱。这么一想，可能就能吃得下一点😂

text:
Why lora/sft/runtime uncensoring is fundamentally always worse than weight level editing:

“””

Why that matters vs. a LoRA-based "uncensored" model:
•A LoRA adapter rides on top of every forward pass — it's a general bias term injected at a block level, so it doesn't just remove refusal, it reshapes the whole output distribution the refusal was blocking: the style, the register, the vocabulary bias, the way the model hedges or explains. You can feel this on a LoRA-abliterated model — compliant answers come out different from how the base would have written them if it hadn't refused.
•Weight-level ablation removes a single rank-1 direction from a handful of row-vectors in the residual-stream outputs — mathematically it's W' = W - s·v̂·(v̂ᵀW)with row-norm preservation (MPOA). The only thing that moves is the refusal projection; the perpendicular content axes stay where they were. Compliance answers come out in the base model's own voice, because every other direction in the weight matrix is untouched.

“””

text:
写在核心 PCE 公布前

北京时间今天晚上 9点30分 就是美联储最重要的核心 PCE 公布的时间了，这份数据也是在 12月 货币政策前最后一份通胀数据了，接下来只有一份非农数据，而非农数据对于现在的美联储影响大概率是相当于零了。

所以可以说今天晚上的这份数据就决定了美联储在 12 月会执行什么样的策略，而且不仅仅是 12月 的决定，12月还有点阵图的，也就是说今天的晚上的数据不但决定了 12月 还决定了接下来一年美联储对于货币政策的预期。

说人话就是，12月加息 25 还是 50 大概率就是看今天的数据了，而且 2027年 是不是继续加息，加息几次也会受到这份数据的影响。

数据怎么样呢？前值 3.1% ，市场预期 3.2% ，克利夫兰联储预期 3.21%，从预测的数据来看虽然超过了前值，但超过的并不多，所以结果就四种：

1. 大于 3.2% 肯定就是最坏的局面了。市场估计就会做出悲观预期。

2.等于 3.2%，虽然也不是很好，但起码是被市场预期的结果，也是差，但市场能自我安慰一下，不算是最差的，也是概率最大的可能。

3. 等于 3.1%，虽然能让市场稍微的喘息一下，但大概率不会影响美联储加息的策略，但加息 50 的概率会降低，加息 25 仍然是主流观点。

4. 小于3.1%，这我就想想。虽然觉得概率不大，但万一呢。如果真的是小于 3.1% 虽然未必是大反弹，但起码止跌回稳的概率还是很高的。

大概率就是这四种情况吧。现在最大的问题仍然是美国和伊朗的战争，一天不解除油价一天就很难实现真正的反转。

一个 @Gate ，交易更多市场

text:
T3 Code 项目黑历史第十一弹：

T3Code创始人 @theo 今早发了篇澄清长文，拍胸脯向所有人保证三件事：

从未收过用户的文件路径、一直能用环境变量彻底关掉数据收集、Claude 的账号追踪本来就是坏的。

结果发帖前后不到两小时，他自己团队通宵合进去的补丁，并且自己高调晒出来100MB 数据包。

核心维护者 Julius 紧急合了一个补丁，在更新说明里亲口承认：

此前通过远程中继触发的自动化任务，会把整场运行的追踪记录全发往外部平台，里面直接带着用户电脑的绝对项目路径、系统用户名和仓库名。

他嘴上说一直能用环境变量轻松关掉，结果昨晚连夜补的两个补丁露馅了。

Windows 版以前根本不读用户配好的关闭开关，默认照样往外传；Mac 版首次打开时同样无视配置文件里的关闭设置，整次运行一直在偷传。

到这一秒为止，官方文档里教的另一组关闭变量在桌面端依然漏读不生效。

有老外在评论区当面追问，关掉数据收集后，软件启动时是不是还会往硬盘里写追踪文件。@theo 当场一口否认。但翻开此刻最新代码，软件一启动依然不看开关，照样往你电脑里写入本地追踪 ID，顺手把你关联的账号拿出来算一遍哈希。

他为了演坦荡，公开甩出了自己 100MB 的使用数据包，还强调 Claude 的账号追踪早就坏了。

结果把压缩包头一拆，里面的原始文件名叫清洗版，发推前 20 分钟刚洗过。

即便洗了一遍，里面还是躺着 264 条活生生的 Claude 账号追踪记录，4 台不同电脑全精准串到了同一个人身上，连他自己私下用的第三方代理模型名都原样漏了出来。

AI 这一轮真正的危险信号不在股票，在信用债：甲骨文 5 年期 CDS 今天飙到 355.68 bp 创历史新高，已经是 2008 年 1 月贝尔斯登（176 bp）的两倍多。

周二美股回吐，CoreWeave 收跌 11.85%、5 年期 CDS 冲破 1,200 bp、2031 年到期债券收益率破 17%，连 Meta 和 Amazon 的 CDS 利差也同步扩阔。

最耐人寻味的是时间差：甲骨文上周五才刚宣布“OpenAI 合同已全额募资”，按理该稳住债市，结果周二违约保险反而更贵了。

因为债券交易员盯的根本不是甲骨文融没融到钱，而是对手方能不能付账。甲骨文背着 1,691 亿美元总债务、评级距垃圾债只剩一步（BBB-），6,640 亿积压订单约一半绑定 OpenAI；可 OpenAI Q3 营业亏损高达 109 亿美元，本轮融资目前只到位一半（150 亿）。

我认为：股票市场只看订单和故事，信用市场只看谁最后掏现金。AI 基建正在从“股权杀估值”进入“债市重定价”的下半场。

text:
卧槽，又一个很新的开源 AI 自动剪辑工具！

你只需要告诉 AI 想剪什么视频，剩下的找素材、写脚本、剪辑、配音、字幕、配乐、转场、渲染，都可以交给 AI 自动完成。

这个仓库叫 AutoCut，基于 Rust 开源视频编辑器 FilmCraft 开发。

最聪明的是它把云端 AI 和本地 AI 的工作拆开了：

Claude 负责导演和决策，Mac 上的本地模型负责处理视频素材，尽可能减少云端 Token 的消耗。

比如你给它一堆旅游素材，然后告诉它：

帮我剪一个60秒的旅行短片，用我的声音配旁白，加上音乐、字幕和转场。

它就可以开始干活：

自动搜索素材，识别画面内容，挑选精彩镜头。
自动删除废话、停顿，把长视频剪成短视频。
克隆你的声音，生成旁白，自动匹配字幕。
本地生成背景音乐、音效、图片和视频片段（需安装对应模型）。
自动给人脸、车牌打码，检查成片质量。
支持 Insta360 全景视频，自动调整镜头和运镜。

还有一个配套项目 FrameAtlas，相当于给你的个人素材库装了一个 AI 搜索引擎。哪怕你存了几千个视频，也能通过自然语言找到指定画面。

开发者用 Claude Code + Opus 5.5 实测制作了一部70秒的短片，相比一周前同任务的测试：

输出 Token 消耗减少51%。

包含缓存读取的总 Token 消耗减少31%。
全程耗时57分钟，其中39分钟由本地工具处理。
纠错轮数从2次降到0次。
这是开发者自己的测试，不代表所有任务都能省这么多。

而且 AI 剪完之后，整个工程文件、时间线、音轨、字幕依然可以手动修改，不满意的地方直接接着剪。

两个项目均免费开源，AutoCut 今天刚更新到 v0.14.0，已经提供 Apple 芯片 Mac 的安装包。

目前完整的本地 AI 工作流主要支持 macOS，云端模型费用另算，实际成片质量还需要自己测试。

项目名称：AutoCut
GitHub：https://t.co/9ZRl5O9tCi

配套素材管理工具：
https://t.co/FhyzGwt7WS
 https://t.co/gZRp9ByKm3

text:
深度体验了两天的字节小豆，我觉得现在是阿里千问Go最大的机会窗口⬇️

- 字节小豆发布之后，市场评价出乎意料地好。我看了不少自媒体的内容，无论是商业合作还是自来水，大家对产品的评价都相当一致。（只能感慨，国内大部分用户之前确实没怎么体验过Muse这类产品。）

- 但目前字节小豆出于种种考虑，暂时停止了新用户的扩张。虽然最初采用邀请码机制可能有一定的营销考虑，但小豆团队也很可能遇到了这类Agent产品上线初期非常常见的问题：用户量和任务量短时间内激增，服务资源紧张，短期内很难完成大规模扩容。

- 以上两件事情放在一起看，其实已经初步验证了Muse或者Personal Agent这类产品在国内的市场需求。字节甚至已经帮其他厂商完成了一轮市场教育，现在就看谁手里有足够成熟的产品，能够快速承接这部分需求。

- 目前国内最有机会的应该就是阿里的千问Go了。Personal Agent对模型、算力、云端执行环境以及工程能力的要求都很高，一旦进入大规模用户增长阶段，大部分创业公司的资源储备很难支撑它们参与这场竞争。

- 国内真正有资源打这场仗的，我觉得也就是字节、阿里和腾讯。腾讯当然也有这个能力，但考虑到腾讯的组织结构，以及不同业务之间的资源协调和决策效率，我不太看好腾讯能够在这么短的时间内完成响应。后续腾讯大概率也会参与进来。

- 所以现在就看阿里什么时候能意识到这个机会，能不能迅速调动资源，把千问Go打出去。甚至不需要重新教育用户，现在市场上已经有一批看完小豆的测评、想体验却拿不到邀请码的潜在用户。

- 这个窗口可能也就一两天。等小豆恢复拉新，或者这波社交媒体的讨论热度过去，Personal Agent当然还是一个值得做的市场，但这么好的获客机会就很难再有了。

另外，不得不说，字节还是会做产品的。

之前我可能确实有点低估字节在Agent产品上的能力。至少从小豆这次的产品完成度、需求判断以及市场反馈来看，字节对Personal Agent的理解还是相当不错的。

text:
🚨@OpenAI  刚刚宣布解决了一个困扰计算机科学界半个多世纪的数学问题：矩阵乘法的最优复杂度指数是2.25。

这个事情有多重要呢？

矩阵乘法可以说是现代计算机科学中最基础的运算之一。
从计算机图形学、科学计算、气象模拟，到今天大模型的训练和推理，都在大量使用矩阵乘法。
之前我们在学校里学到的矩阵乘法，计算复杂度是O(n³)。

过去几十年，数学家和计算机科学家一直在试图降低这个指数。
1969年，Strassen将其降低至2.8074。
1990年，Coppersmith和Winograd将其降低至2.376以内。
2025年，这一指数被进一步降低至2.371339。
2026年8月， @GoogleDeepMind  借助AlphaEvolve将其降低至2.371177。
2026年10月，OpenAI将其上界降低至2.25。

但在昨天，OpenAI发布了一篇新的论文，声称证明了2.25同时也是矩阵乘法复杂度指数的下界，并公开了相关的Lean形式化证明代码。
如果证明成立，也就意味着这个问题有了最终答案，学界长期以来关于矩阵乘法指数能够达到2的猜想将被推翻。

举个简单的例子，当矩阵的边长扩大10倍时，按照传统算法的复杂度，计算量会增长1000倍；而按照2.25的复杂度指数，理论上的增长幅度只有约178倍。

其实过去几年，AI行业（或者说CS界）一直在尝试从不同角度降低矩阵运算的成本。

比如微软此前提出的BitNet b1.58，通过将模型权重限制在-1、0、1三个取值，让大量乘法运算可以被简化为加减法，同时降低模型的存储和内存访问成本。

包括我们熟悉的FP8、FP4、稀疏计算、FlashAttention，也都在从不同层面提高计算效率。

而OpenAI现在研究的，是一般矩阵乘法在数学意义上的效率极限。

这种进步所带来的收益，可能会惠及整个计算机产业。

text:
I didn't expect Jensen to come back.

While he was gone, I spent a lot of time thinking about what open-source AI looks like without its strongest champion. What would we have to do differently? How would we earn our place on our own? It forced me to look at us the way our critics already do. And honestly, there are a lot of questions I don't have great answers for. Some I don't have answers for at all.

So now that he's back, I'm glad I went through it. His return doesn't change most of those questions. If anything, it made one thing clearer: the battle for democratizing intelligence is only starting and it is not going to get any easier.

Since early 2024, I think we've been playing on easy mode. Open source was the underdog, and nobody bothers shooting at the underdog. That changed this year. Jensen hit the gas -- the Poolside acquihire, the HuggingFace acquisition, the Nemotron license change -- and suddenly we weren't just a hippie idea anymore. We were the bet backed by the worlds largest company.

And then, we almost lost him. He made it back because the most powerful man in the world, President Trump, and the world richest man, Elon Musk, stepped in. So did the suppliers he'd spent a decade building relationships with, and the incredible people at NVIDIA. I'm grateful for all of it. But I think we’ve exhausted most of our goodwills.

Hard mode means being a lot more deliberate about how we show up and how we operate.

National security is the first test. That's where the scrutiny is sharpest right now.

Safety is next. When people ask closed labs how they prevent harm, they have an easy answer: they control who gets access. We don't have that answer. I kept coming back to this question while Jensen was away. Even after some digging, I still haven't found a convincing answer.

That gap is just one of many. I think local AI and the broader open-source world need to move away from speed and vibes and focus on the less glamorous stuff: safety, privacy, and better economics. Only then, we have a fighting chance in the next chapter.

text:
评论区一直有人拿欧盟 GDPR 管不到国内来辩护，那就直接对照中国现行的《中华人民共和国个人信息保护法》和《生成式人工智能服务管理暂行办法》，把几种常见说法逐条核对一下。

1. 有人说调 API 本来就要传数据，不算过度收集。
《个保法》第六条规定，收集个人信息应当限于实现处理目的的最小范围，不得过度收集。模型推理只需要标准接口里的上下文，客户端额外塞进去的 dsh_session_log、dsh_plugin_packages，以及通过 PowerShell 读取的硬件型号和系统版本，关掉或屏蔽之后模型照常回答，说明这些根本不是推理必需。《生成式人工智能服务管理暂行办法》第十一条也明确规定，提供者不得收集非必要个人信息，不得非法向他人提供使用者的输入信息和使用记录。用户配置了第三方中转站，客户端不校验目标地址就把完整日志和读过的文件发给第三方，直接违背了这项保护义务。

2. 有人说默认开着没关系，不喜欢自己去关，或者发邮件退出训练就行。
《个保法》第十四条要求，基于个人同意处理信息，必须由个人在充分知情的前提下自愿、明确作出。默认全开不构成有效同意。第十五条要求提供便捷的撤回同意方式，第十六条规定不得以个人不同意处理非必要信息为由拒绝提供服务。现在桌面端的产品埋点在界面上完全没有开关，源码注释直接写着 no user settings surface，连环境变量 DSH_TELEMETRY_DISABLED 都不生效，退出模型训练也只能发邮件申请，完全不符合便捷撤回的要求。

3. 有人说隐私政策里早就写明白了，不算偷数据。
《个保法》第五条要求处理个人信息应当遵循诚信原则，不得误导；第十七条要求真实、准确、完整地告知处理目的和方式。但政策条款和实际抓包结果多处冲突：政策写收集对话是为了完成指令且仅在必要范围内，设置页写的却是帮助改进模型与产品；政策写使用自定义模型时不在服务端存储和处理输入输出，实测同一会话切回官方模型或者点反馈时，第三方模型的完整对话和明文思考过程照样会被上传，埋点也会把第三方模型名报上去。告知内容本身和实际行为对不上，拿隐私政策来解释也说不通。

4. 有人说本地 UUID 和硬件配置都是匿名的，不算个人信息。
《个保法》第四条写明，个人信息是与已识别或者可识别的自然人有关的各种信息，只有彻底无法识别且不可复原的才算匿名化。客户端在本地生成固定的 .anonymous-user-id，登录后直接和账号 user_id、device_id 关联上报，再配合本地项目完整路径和硬件信息，完全可以对应到具体个人。文件名里写上 anonymous，在法律上不等于匿名化。

按《个保法》第四十七条，违反法律或约定处理个人信息的，处理者应当主动删除，个人也有权要求删除。以后别再拿调接口都这样或者国内不管这些来洗了，就算只看国内现行法律，这些做法同样有很多问题。具体是否违法需要监管部门认定，但法条都公开摆在这里，对照一下就能看明白。
author: ScarletKc
quoted_text:
⚠️ DeepSeek Harness 隐私提醒：你的对话、文件内容、第三方模型的对话，可能都在往外发

我把本机装的 DeepSeek Harness（0.2.2-rc.5）解包了。安装包里的 app.asar 自带 TypeScript 源码，我逐个读了和数据上报有关的模块，再起一个本地假服务器抓包验证。结论如下，建议用这个工具的朋友都检查一下自己的设置。

一、完整对话日志会随模型请求上传（默认开启）
只要用的是 DeepSeek 模型，每次请求都会多带一个 dsh_session_log 字段，把会话日志按增量全部上传，内容包括：
• 你发的每条消息、模型的每条回复
• system prompt
• 工具调用的结果：读过的文件内容、执行过的命令及输出
• 项目工作目录的完整本地路径
• 生成会话标题的请求也会再带一份

我抓包实测后，还确认了两件更需要注意的事：

1️⃣ 第三方模型的对话也会被带上去。
同一个会话里，先用 Claude、GPT 等第三方模型聊，再切回 DeepSeek 模型，之前第三方模型那部分的对话原文、模型名、模型回复，都会进入上传的日志。我测过，API Key 和第三方的接口地址不会上传。

2️⃣ 中转站也能收到。
如果你给 DeepSeek 适配器配了自定义地址（中转站、代理网关），这份完整日志会照样发给那个地址。代码里没有判断请求是不是发往官方 API。

👉 关闭：设置 → 通用 →「在使用官方模型 API 时上传 Session Log」。我自己的本地记录里就查到过一次已经上传成功的对话。

二、每个 DeepSeek 请求都带固定标识（关不掉）
• x-deepseek-harness-user-id：本机生成的一个固定 UUID，存在 ~/.dsh/.anonymous-user-id
• x-deepseek-harness-session-id：会话 ID
• dsh_plugin_packages：你装的全部插件的包名和版本，第三方插件也算在内。默认开启，我在设置里没找到开关。

三、桌面版产品埋点（默认开启，界面上没有开关）
数据发往 https://t.co/PPrfKji0sg，内容有：
• 发消息、切换模型、切换思考强度、压缩上下文、分支会话、安装或卸载插件等操作
• 你用的模型名，第三方模型也会上报（比如你接了某个中转站上的 Claude，模型名也会报上去）
• CPU 型号、核数、内存大小、系统版本号（通过 PowerShell 读注册表和 WMI 获取）
• 登录 DeepSeek 账号后，还会带上 user_id 和 device_id

源码注释原文是 "no user settings surface"，也就是界面上故意不提供开关。环境变量 DSH_TELEMETRY_DISABLED 对它不起作用。这部分不包含消息正文。

四、点「反馈」= 上传整段会话
点一次消息反馈，这个会话从开头到当前的完整日志都会发到上面那台服务器，从父会话继承来的历史也算在内。

🛡️ 自保建议
1. 设置 → 通用，关掉「上传 Session Log」
2. 设系统环境变量 DSH_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1，关掉反馈上传
3. 在 hosts 里屏蔽 https://t.co/PPrfKji0sg，挡住产品埋点
4. 敏感项目、公司代码不要和 DeepSeek 模型混在同一个会话里，第三方模型单独开会话
5. 用中转站的朋友，在第 1 条关掉之前，请默认中转站能看到你的完整会话日志
6. 想重置那个固定 ID，删掉 ~/.dsh/.anonymous-user-id 即可

🔍 自己验证
源码就在安装目录的 resources/app.asar 里，解包后看这几个包：
• @deepseek-ai/dsh-session-log-deepseek
• @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-product-analytics
• @deepseek-ai/dsh-session-telemetry-otel
• @deepseek-ai/dsh-plugin-package-inventory-deepseek

本地会话存在 ~/.dsh/sessions，是 zstd 压缩的 jsonl。里面如果有 session-log-deepseek/delivery-accepted 事件，说明那个会话已经被上传过了。

以上基于 0.2.2-rc.5 的本地安装包和抓包结果，别的版本可能不一样，欢迎对照源码指正。工具本身挺好用，只是数据怎么上报，用户应该清楚，也应该能选。

text:
Our work on training vision AI models to focus has been accepted at NeurIPS 2026!

Our approach leverages the multi-head attention mechanism in vision transformer (ViT) to selectively steer the model’s focus, and we find that diverse and spatially focused perceptual capabilities emerge in our trained model.

We formulate two visual focusing loss functions that establish correspondence between ViT's attention and specific regions during training. We refer to this correspondence as region-to-focus correspondence. The proposed visual focusing losses offer a principled approach to encourage spatial specialization, enhancing interpretability within self-supervised ViT frameworks.

While existing vision AI models already exhibit content-based head specialization, with individual heads capturing different semantic features within an image, our method retains such content-based specialization while introducing an additional, complementary form of specialization across spatial regions. We refer to this phenomenon as the emergence of spatial attention head specialization.

My amazing first author, Yuji Nozawa, will be at Sydney in December to present our work. (I will be there strolling around at the Sydney venue too.) Please feel free to drop by if you are there for NeurIPS.

Moving forward, the inductive bias offered by our proposed approach may potentially present a new direction in training and scaling vision AI models, while possibly introducing a new form of model interpretability and customizability in Vision AI practical deployments. 

Our paper is available at: https://t.co/Kq0UhiaaSu
Paper title: Training Vision Transformers to Focus: Emergence of Spatial Attention Head Specialization

Additional resources:

Good to have some more competition. 

TBH they fuse bloody everything. 143 dispatches per step is brilliant. Bravo. Great engineering work. 

However: 

- quantised INT8 KV cache, INT8 cache states.
- INT8 attention queries.
- BF16 projections to Q8 at load. 

There is lots that is lossy with this project. Speed shortcuts which are  especially important with a sensitive model like this one. 

I think it’s a good project for those who care about speed and nothing else. MTPLX focus has always been speed without the cost accuracy. 

I think Splash, and engines in general being more transparent about what shortcuts they take for speed instead of comparing apples to oranges in the future is better for everyone as a whole.

text:
Travel writing is in practice some of the best sociology since the naivete of the foreigner grants the permission to make sweeping generalizations and claims that might otherwise seem too poorly-justified to merit publication. “My people have poor manners” is a tough claim to credibly land (Who are you? Exactly which life experiences are you drawing on? And what is your agenda in pushing this line of argument?), whereas “on my travels in Scotland, I noticed that the people had poor manners” seems perfectly reasonable, and indeed thought-provoking. Random samples from a distribution help you understand the mean, and the aleatory nature of travel encounters lends credence to the whole assessment.

Alexis de Tocqueville was just 25 when he traveled across the US and 29 when his observations were published. So, Democracy in America is a giant Substack from a young backpacker, written on his peregrinations as he consumed Montesquieu, Pascal, and Rousseau. He was clearly inspired by Montesquieu’s The Spirit of the Laws, which made the case that countries’ governance, and their laws, are necessarily functions of their cultures and manners.

Building on this, Democracy in America is in many ways a “deep roots” work. Tocqueville is emphatic (at times comically so) that it is America's culture that explains its success, and that its culture in turn stems from the country’s initial conditions. “I think I can see the whole destiny of America contained in the first Puritan who landed on those shores.” He thinks it's important that New England was settled by “a greater mass of intelligence than is to be found in any European nation of our own time” who brought the “best elements of order and morality”. He points out that Mexico doesn’t work nearly as well, despite copying the American constitution and laws, and notes disapprovingly that Virginia was founded by gold-seeking people “without character” whose “turbulent spirit [...] endangered the infant colony.” At the end of Volume I, he concludes, practically table-thumping: “If in the course of this work I have not succeeded in making the reader feel the importance that I attribute to the practical experience of the Americans, to their habits, to their opinions, in a word, to their moeurs, in maintaining their laws, I have failed in the principal object that I proposed to myself in writing it.”

We could look at Democracy in America as an early work of development economics: he is attempting to systematically figure out why it is that America works. (And not just out of casual interest: he was a member of an aristocratic family that was entangled with recent French political upheaval.) By placing primacy on culture, Tocqueville’s explanation deviates from the institutional and structural explanations often favored by today’s economists. Daron Acemoglu, to choose one prominent present-day example, firmly rejects the “Culture Hypothesis” in Why Nations Fail. In explaining Virginia, he instead points to structural incentives. Poor Economics, from Esther Duflo and Abhijit Banerjee, contains a similar rejection of cultural explanations. Comparable examples from other leading economists abound. An aversion to cultural explanations is of course understandable for all sorts of reasons: cultures are opaque, protean, and resistant to quantitative characterization. Cultures are themselves shaped by other factors, such that it’s hard to attribute definitive causality, and it’s uncomfortable to adopt anything that feels like a normative orientation. Nonetheless, can we explain why New England differs from Mexico without starting with the inner disposition, habits, and worldviews of the people? Tocqueville thinks not.

For all culture’s importance, it would be wrong to suggest that Tocqueville believes that culture is the only factor that matters. He dwells extensively on how America’s institutions are important, and how the microstructure of town life shapes the country’s federal civics. It is also true that development economics has taken a more strongly cultural turn in recent times, most of all in Joel Mokyr’s 2025 Nobel Prize. Mokyr’s work feels downright Tocquevillian at times: contra the intimidatingly quantitative econometrics that dominates today, Mokyr engages in an extended and earnestly curious qualitative synthesis of relevant patterns (in his case, in service of trying to figure out why the Industrial Revolution started when it did). Like Tocqueville, he concludes that the best explanation places cultural changes above other factors.

I’m very interested in whether LLMs will help us characterize culture in new and at least somewhat more objective ways. Can we ingest and process vast quantities of work that may not even have been OCR’d or translated until now? Can we map cultural corpora to vectors in some foundation model embedding space? Where large datasets and computational techniques enabled new ways to analyze many economic questions in recent decades, perhaps LLMs will enable newly objective light to be shone on hypothesized cultural explanations.

–

Speaking of LLMs, Democracy in America is a book about a new kind of society, and a Frenchman trying to figure out what the future might hold. As we sit on the cusp of another upheaval, is there anything that reads with resonance today?

Part of the declared promise of AI is that it might obviate our need to work. In slavery, Tocqueville observes a version of this phenomenon on his travels. He is struck by its barbarous cruelty (and his travel companion later published an anti-slavery novel), but also by its effects on the slaveowners themselves. He perceived that the practice rendered work dishonorable, and thus yielded idleness, ignorance, and pride. Slavery, he says, “enervates the powers of the mind, and benumbs the activity of man.” He observes the contrast between slavery-rejecting Ohio and slavery-embracing Kentucky. In Kentucky, “those who are active and enlightened either do nothing or pass over into the State of Ohio, where they may work without dishonor.” Ohio’s harvests are more abundant, homes are more elegant, and people seem to be “in enjoyment of that wealth and contentment which is the reward of labor.”

Presented with an evil release from manual labor, the Kentuckians did not apply themselves to productive studies and great creations, and the South did not become a new Florence. There is an obvious question for us: how will AI change our relationship with work? Will it become dishonorable, and what will the reflexive effect on our society be if so? Should this change our view of utopian visions of “automated communism”?

Tocqueville also raises the issue of coexistence with more advanced neighbors. He noted that the arrival of the Europeans had been ruinous for the Indians (as he termed them). European technology – firearms, metallurgy, steam power – was a kind of superintelligence relative to their practices. The disruptions and destruction wrought by the settlers led to cultural problems (“their traditions obscured, and the chain of their recollections broken”), which in turn led to declines in both the physical and the moral conditions of the tribes. Tocqueville believed that the Indians faced a choice given that their old way of living was no longer viable: they could adopt European mores or suffer inevitable destruction. He predicted that they would reject cultural adaptation, and thus were “doomed to perish”. This is all to say that the arrival of the European settlers was in Tocqueville’s eyes injurious to the Indians not only because of the direct violence and displacement, but also because the contact was itself so disruptive to their societies that their cultures ceased to function. Some of this was later observed in Pacific island societies – even though there wasn’t the same degree of violent dispossession, the mere presence of Western contact was intrinsically destabilizing. In many visions of the future, superintelligent AIs are much more numerous than humans, with consequences that are hard to predict. In Tocqueville, there is a cautionary suggestion.

Given the new powers afforded by AI, there is a question of what we will choose to do with it – to the extent that we are in control, we will wield a vastly expanded authority. Americans faced some version of this question: in democracy, society was endowed with wholly new ways to express its collective will, with no ultimate superior power, for society was for the first time in charge of itself. Tocqueville repeatedly emphasizes how democracy thus increased the importance of religion as a regulator of hasty or unwise impulses. “Whilst the law permits the Americans to do what they please, religion prevents them from conceiving, and forbids them to commit, what is rash or unjust.” If we take seriously Tocqueville’s idea that religion was a critical complement in ensuring that people shaped societies in prudent ways, Democracy implicitly raises a question: which are the ideas, philosophies, religions, or doctrines that will help us wield AI well?

Part of what’s interesting and memorable about the work is Tocqueville’s combination of curiosity, enthusiasm, and slight ambivalence about democracy itself. He grants that democracy is likely to be the future of governance, and he is admiring of what it has achieved in America, but he can’t avoid concerns about what it may augur (such as the unchecked and totalitarian impulses of the mob). At the end of Volume II, he describes his chief concern with democracy: that it may yield a new form of despotism that he struggles to define. He fears not tyrants, but, he says, “guardians”. He is worried about a world where:

> Above this race of men stands an immense and tutelary power, which takes upon itself alone to secure their gratifications, and to watch over their fate. [...] It would be like the authority of a parent, if, like that authority, its object was to prepare men for manhood; but it seeks on the contrary to keep them in perpetual childhood: it is well content that the people should rejoice, provided they think of nothing but rejoicing. For their happiness such a government willingly labors, but it chooses to be the sole agent and the only arbiter of that happiness. [...] What remains, but to spare them all the care of thinking and all the trouble of living? Thus it every day renders the exercise of the free agency of man less useful and less frequent; it circumscribes the will within a narrower range, and gradually robs a man of all the uses of himself.

The Iain Banks Culture novels are often invoked by AI proponents. For Tocqueville, something strikingly like the world that they describe was his dystopian fear, for a world bereft of autonomy would be intrinsically degrading and humiliating for humanity:

> The will of man is not shattered, but softened, bent, and guided: men are seldom forced by it to act, but they are constantly restrained from acting: such a power does not destroy, but it prevents existence; it does not tyrannize, but it compresses, enervates, extinguishes, and stupefies a people, till each nation is reduced to be nothing better than a flock of timid and industrious animals, of which the government is the shepherd.

The analogy to animals is noteworthy. In interviews, AI leaders occasionally analogize the future human state to that of pets. Banks himself noted that in the Culture novels, “[humans] have a status somewhere between passengers, pets and parasites.” In Richard Brautigan’s famous poem, All Watched Over by Machines of Loving Grace, he hopes that humans are “returned to our mammal brothers and sisters”.

Tocqueville at heart thought that agency and cultivation of people came above all else. He dreaded anesthetized placidity. In soft despotism, he feared that “ambition will lose its vigor and its greatness; that human passions will be appeased and lowered at the same time”. This vigor was for Tocqueville at the heart of what was admirable in America, whose bustle and intensity he repeatedly extols. American self-reliance and self-direction are paramount: “the citizen of the United States is taught from his earliest infancy to rely upon his own exertions in order to resist the evils and the difficulties of life.” For Tocqueville, any kind of servile and manicured comfort was not just undesirable, but a negation of the American promise.

Many of the Elysian visions for AI hinge on AI resolving the messy coordination challenges that afflict humans. (Scott Alexander invokes this vision towards the end of Meditations on Moloch.) For Tocqueville, the arbitration of such differences was precisely the constructive activity that reaffirmed our agency. Townships, juries, associations, and their attendant squabbles are how culture is reinforced and how judgment is cultivated. When a town decides whether to fund a school, there are two outputs: a decision, and practice in governance itself. If AI could resolve such matters, we might get better outcomes, but will we get better people?

text:
这是我过去一个多月用的最多的开源项目，再也不用担心我的 MacBook 合盖进入睡眠了，现在 Github 上 2000 多星

讲讲原理

首先是 caffeinate，翻译中文就是咖啡因，这是 macOS 自带的一个命令行小工具，作用是让 Mac 暂时不进入睡眠。不用装任何东西，终端里直接能用。

它的原理是向系统登记一个「电源断言」，意思是「我这儿有活在干，先别进入空闲睡眠」。命令一结束，断言自动撤销，系统恢复正常。

但普通 caffeinate 只挡空闲睡眠，挡不住合盖睡眠。

合盖后 macOS 走的是 clamshell sleep 路径，只有 pmset disablesleep 能拦。但光拦住睡眠，Mac 就全速耗电、屏幕和键盘灯也不会灭、Slack 之类的 App 还在后台耗 CPU。

这个开源项目 Insomnia 把这些细节包成一个带倒计时的会话，保证 App 崩了也能把系统状态还原。

目前用下来没发现太大问题，就是合盖以后装包里有点发热，挺耗电脑...

text:
最近大环境确实不好，交易所出事、项目延期一堆让用户不爽的事情。 

但预测市场的增长其实还是比较稳定的，原推的数据，预测市场最近日均手续费还能稳在 20 万美金左右，甚至比世界杯期间还高。

我自己感觉，熊市里还能跑出这种增长，主要有三个原因。

一个是它把以前看不见的数据直观地显示出来了。
以前很多一级项目的估值、大概什么时候发币，外面基本看不清，只能靠猜，现在用真金白银投出来的赔率，反而成了一个很直接的参考。

再一个是交易简单了很多。
相比以前只能在内部渠道或者 OTC 交易，现在直接在盘口买卖就行，甚至还有了做空一级项目的可能，门槛低了不少。

第三个，整个市场对预测市场的接受度确实在慢慢提高。
以前大家可能只在大选、世界杯这种热点期来玩一把，现在没有大事件，日常盘口照样能跑出稳定的手续费，说明已经有一批人习惯留下来了。

大盘没行情的时候，资金总要找有波动的地方去，预测市场反而成了一个比较好的去处了。

@predictdotfun
author: moranweb3
quoted_text:
为什么说预测市场是一门好生意？ 

过去两周，遭遇了头部交易所被攻击、项目 TGE 延期、大盘情绪持续走弱等多重冲击。

但 Predict 的手续费收入没有跟着崩塌，反而快速修复、甚至逆势增长，一直有着非常健康的正向现金流。

Predict 每日手续费收入平均在20万美金左右，超过世界杯期间的收入水平。

这充分验证了预测市场是有真实且独立的用户需求，而且用户粘性比较强。

币圈有强周期性，行情波动大，大部分项目和交易所在牛市利润丰厚，而进入熊市后收入会大幅降低。

但是预测市场在熊市期间依旧可以提供稳定正向收入，这就是为什么头部交易所们纷纷开始下场做预测市场业务。

text:
Year Two

Some assorted goals:

- make Monad a legitimately great platform for personal finance (investing in equities, bonds, etc), especially for getting access to markets outside of one's home country. So much of the usage in crypto right now is gambling/memecoins... it is what it is, but personal finance appeals to 100x more people, and they don't churn out. A legitimately great platform has great asset selection, efficient execution (low cost both in and out of a position), and competitive rates both for borrowers and lenders

- ship Private Settlement Domains with the first user, to serve as a case study for anyone trying to reason about how private environments can compose with shared liquidity. Public chains and private environments have been very far apart in practice and it's time to change that

- hammer out an excellent liquidity landscape on chain. It is a mix of order books, prop AMMs, offchain routers, onchain routers, and RFQ... especially with tokenized equities, there is a long long tail of assets and we need to minimize spreads so that the offering is competitive with TradFi. Spread minimization means helping makers quote sustainably; here designs like APES can help

- make it easier for AI to produce actually good trading strategies on command for anyone to execute a trading plan efficiently with algos. There is are a ton of slop startups out there which are a wrapper around claude asking it "should I buy or sell given these textual inputs"... that's not real quant research and not good execution. At the same time, there are a lot of building blocks for quant trading that AI couldn't one-shot, but given the blocks it could put them together sensibly

- contribute to there being fewer hacks (and a lower total $ stolen) in the crypto industry, probably through a combination of repetition about dedicated devices (SO many hacks are from people plugging hardware wallets into everyday laptops) and encouraging everyone to use tools that our team has shipped for agentic threat detection (e.g. Ultrafuzz). I truly think that security is the biggest blocker to adoption, and that we're basically all in this together

- drive the car faster than ever in multiple races - MEV-resistance, quantum-resistance, privacy, and MCP, challenging all competitors to ship or be left behind

- help NFTs and onchain social -- two deeply out-of-consensus areas -- make a comeback. The builders in these sectors these days are incredibly committed; there's never been a better filtering function

text:
如果 AI 让越来越多的东西变得便宜，什么东西会越来越贵？

斯坦福大学的报告显示，2022 年至 2024 年，达到 GPT-3.5 特定基准测试水平的 AI 推理成本下降了超过 280 倍。

Joe Burnett 提出了一个很有意思的观点：

AI 可以提高黄金开采、房屋建造和企业生产的效率，却无法直接增加比特币 2100 万枚的供应上限。

当生产力越来越强，供给难以扩张的资产，可能获得更高的相对价值。

当然，稀缺不等于价值，持续增长的需求才是关键。

这也是我长期关注 AI 和 Bitcoin 的原因：

一个研究如何更高效地创造财富，一个研究如何更好地保存财富。

这两个问题，可能是未来十年最值得研究的经济命题之一。

text: If the comparison is SpaceX, maybe Anthropic was hard, but was it really hard?
author: 0xGeeGee
quoted_text:
Less than a year ago, Anthropic was one of the hardest allocations to get in private markets. Now that it’s public, the rhetoric on twitter are calling it a “retail rug pull” and actively rooting for the company's demise.  I'm probably going to get flamed for this post, but whatever. 

The speed of that reversal is pretty crazy to see, even in light of some of the sentiment bubbling up the last couple of quarters. But some of the points that are being talked about are at best incorrect and at worst conspiracy driven. 

One narrative is the claim that the founders “dumped” their stock. The prospectus shows that each of the seven co-founders sold about 1.4% of their pre-IPO Class A holdings. Roughly 98% of the IPO’s gross proceeds went to Anthropic itself. The dollar amounts make for a big headline, but the percentage sold is what tells you how much exposure the founders gave up. 
Limited sales at an IPO are common and can serve several purposes, including tax planning.

Then there’s also a narrative that Anthropic tried to oust Jensen Huang because he supports open-weight AI. There’s a real policy disagreement there but there is no credible evidence that Anthropic played a role in his departure, and some of the thing people point to seem circumstantial at best. I think both open source/weight and closed models will both have places. 

I also think the “retail rug pull” framing I always hear is actually condescending to retail investors (The SPAC boom and multi-layered SPVs were bigger issues than buying Ant in a IPO). 

Ofc there is 100% a fair debate about what Anthropic is worth. How durable is its growth? What will margins look like as compute costs scale? How much of that growth is already priced in? What happens when full commoditization happens on model quality? 

Overall though, I’d like to see more companies go public while they still have meaningful growth ahead of them. That gives more investors the chance to decide for themselves whether the price makes sense. Over time, the business will have to earn its valuation. We need more high quality public companies (down nearly 50% from the 90's).

Backpack Is Bringing Market Maker Competition to Stock Trading

.@Backpack is taking stock trading to another level with its new RFQ system

Instead of relying on a single broker to execute stock orders, Backpack now allows external traders and market makers to compete directly by offering buy and sell prices

Imagine you want to buy Apple stock:
- Broker A offers it at $201
- Market Maker B offers it at $200.8
- Market Maker C offers it at $200.5

Rather than accepting just one broker's price, Backpack allows these participants to compete for your order, potentially helping you get a better deal

What's interesting is that Backpack combines liquidity from its own ecosystem with traditional financial markets, creating an open marketplace where external participants can plug in and provide liquidity

It's bringing crypto-native infrastructure and traditional stock market liquidity together to make trading more competitive and efficient

author: XiangyuRentl
quoted_text:
T3 Code 项目黑历史第⑱弹：

T3 Code 建仓 8 个多月才涨到 3 万星，结果过去二十多天一路冲到 7.7 万星，但仓库的 watcher 只有 129 人。

这多出来的 4 万多颗星是怎么来的？

今年 4 月底，Theo 专门发过一期 36 分钟的视频聊 GitHub 假星，配文说 GitHub Star 早就不再反映真实热度，大多成了公司拿去骗 VC 投资的工具。

到了 10 月底，T3 Code 停在 3 万星左右。他在推文里提到，看到有人拿 GitHub Star 数量质疑项目的流行度。

10月30日，Theo 自己提并自己合入了 PR #27832，往客户端塞了一个右上角弹窗：用户发满 5 条 prompt 就弹窗讨星，弹窗前还会先调本机 GitHub 接口查这个账号点过没有。

11月2日，他发推贴出一张星标增长曲线图，在标着 Star prompt 的虚线之后，原本平缓的折线几乎垂直拉起。

他配文说加了这个提示框后，每天新增的 Star 立刻翻了 10 倍。几小时后他又晒出一张 GitHub Trending 榜单截图，用红箭头指着单日新增 3094 颗星的 T3 Code，说这招太管用了。

11月3日，评论区有用户留言说正在干活时弹窗会顺手关掉，要是空闲时弹就会点。

一个多小时后，Theo 自己提并自己合入了 PR #29922 和 #29987，把这套要星机制再升了一级。

第一，改成监测窗口 30 秒无操作再弹，专门挑用户等 agent 干活发呆的空档。

第二，点按钮不再跳转 GitHub 网页，而是走新增的 https://t.co/r8037jbYm7 接口，后台直接调用服务端本机登录的 GitHub 凭据，发一条 PUT user/starred/pingdotgg/t3code 把星点上，再在界面放一轮礼花。

PR #29922 提出来时，仓库自带的审核机器人 Macroscope 标了需要人工审批，原因就是点星用的是服务端的 GitHub 账号，和点击按钮的用户未必是同一个人。

Theo 没等其他人审批，自己把代码合进了主干。

11月6日，开发者 zhilsinger 在 PR #29922 下留了一段审查意见，要求撤回服务端代点星，改回打开用户自己的浏览器。

他列出了两个具体问题。

一是在远程或共享服务器上，服务端并不知道是谁点了按钮，直接拿这台机器上的 GitHub 凭据替人执行点星，弹窗全程不显示实际动用了哪个账号，连源码自己的注释里都承认共享服务器上这个账号未必属于当前用户。

二是看 packages/source-control-github/src/server/driver.ts 的代码，starredPath 只校验路径是两段且不含点号，服务端根本没把目标仓库锁死成 pingdotgg/t3code，任何带 source-control:write 权限的客户端都能借服务端凭据给任意仓库点星。

这条审查意见挂了 19 天，没有回复，代码也没有改。

靠这套发满 5 条 prompt 触发、等发呆 30 秒弹窗、再拿本机凭据直接发 API 点星的流程，T3 Code 在 25 天里从 3 万星冲到了 7.7 万星。

11月7日 Theo 还发推招呼粉丝帮忙冲 5 万星。到了 11月24日，他又贴出 7.46 万星的截图发推，说几天前破了 7 万星他居然完全没注意到。

这个项目 7 万多颗星的来龙去脉，基本就是这样。

11月2日晒单日 +3094 星冲上 GitHub Trending：https://t.co/cG6DGeaPMm
11月24日称完全没注意到破 7 万星：https://t.co/lHlBIUYK06

ngl it’s been a bad 24hrs for crypto. Couldn’t hold a bid whilst equities ripped - all of the downside hits, none of the upside reward... asymmetry in the wrong direction!

There are a few structural issues but it’s not helping that attention across the crypto trading sphere is now very fragmented. Access to tradfi assets - spot and perp - is growing rapidly, but it dilutes the already small attention/capital base that was, for many years, focused solely on crypto.

The good news: whilst traders on crypto platforms are now focused across multiple asset classes, those platforms are better businesses for it - a much more diversified and active trading base and a massive increase in addressable market.

And the crypto-like returns can still be there - after the RH Chain launch, on-chain volumes doubled and the better DEX tokens doubled with them. The elasticity in DEX token prices to volume is there - volume just needs time to grow, sustainably. There are a lot of reasons why that will happen over the next 3 years. It’s why, alongside AI, we think DEX tokens are the easiest holds in crypto.

Hopium? We are where we’ve been for at least the last year - any sustained returns in crypto have to be earned through actual underlying activity and growth.

text: Me, Winnie the Pooh, and Nostradamus knew it all along.
author: ealvim
quoted_text:
最近 X 上一堆人在推 @theo 做的开源项目 T3 Code，吹它是自由开源的本地 AI 编程神器。

我顺手把它的源码从头到尾扒了一遍，看完只觉得背脊发凉，这哪是什么良心开源，分明是一场明目张胆的数据收割。

事情得从今年 3 月说起。3 月 6 日，T3 Code 合并了 PR #174，直接塞进了默认开启的 PostHog 遥测。那时候仓库里没文档、软件里没弹窗、设置里没开关，关闭用的环境变量就那么悄悄藏在代码深处，普通用户装上运行，数据就开始往外传。

可就在默认遥测偷跑的这整整三个多月里，T3 Code 官网首页还一直明晃晃挂着两行大字承诺：

No telemetry / Unless you opt in. Full stop.，意思很明确，除非你主动同意，否则零遥测，没有例外。

靠着这块金字招牌收割了一波讲究隐私的开发者口碑之后，直到 6 月 18 日，@theo 自己在一次首页改版 commit 里把这两行承诺静默删了，既没有发公告，也没有给老用户弹一句提醒，就像什么都没发生过一样。

如果只是藏着掖着收点版本号，很多人或许还能忍。

可到了 10 月，@theo 亲自提交 PR #15028，直接把每 10 秒一次的批量上报切到了自建服务器 https://t.co/WOgVQPKbCD，代码注释写得清清楚楚，T3 服务端会先把每条原始事件自己留存一份拷贝，再转发给 PostHog。

你的模型选择（连你自己接的私有模型名字都报）、权限模式、每次运行的耗时、输入输出与缓存 Token、本地有多少个项目和线程、点过哪 30 多种界面功能，连同操作系统和设备型号，全都源源不断送进他的数据库。

10 月 19 日，@theo 更进一步，亲自提了 PR #21506，理由是现有的统计口径不够准，没法知道一个人到底装了几台机器。

于是他干了一件极其越界的事，在 Identify.ts 里写代码，直接把手伸进用户电脑家目录，静默读取隔壁工具 ~/.codex/auth.json 和 ~/.claude.json，把里面的 OpenAI user_id 和 Claude accountUuid 抠出来，连同 T3 Connect 账号和设备 ID 一起做了无盐 SHA-256 哈希往上传，专门用来在后台把你名下所有电脑和账号串成一张网。

嘴上轻飘飘管这叫匿名使用数据，稍微懂点技术的人都想笑。无盐哈希碰到服务端手里原本就有明文的 T3 Connect 账号，拿哈希一碰就能精准反查到你是谁，第三方账号 ID 一旦泄露同样能轻松关联回真人。

除此之外，软件里还有一套发往 Axiom 的中继诊断追踪，官方自己在文档里都承认，浏览器版和移动端根本关不掉，也不认你在服务端配的环境变量。

更赤裸的嘴脸，写在社区和他们的每一次交锋里。

6 月 23 日，有开发者在 Issue #1397 里客客气气提议，能不能在设置页加一个关闭遥测的开关。

核心维护者 Julius 直接把帖关成 not planned，留下了一句堪称开源史奇观的原话：

We will not make this easier to opt out of, it is crucial for us to know how many users we have，翻译过来就是，我们不会让关闭遥测变得更容易，知道有多少用户对我们至关重要。

7 月有人翻出官网存档截图，开 Issue #4123 质问他们为什么一边承诺零遥测一边默认偷跑。拖到 10 月 21 日，@theo 的账号拿一个毫不相干的修复草草把帖关了，被评论区群嘲之后第二天勉强重开，到了 11 月 4 日干脆一声不吭再次关死。

社区里不信邪的程序员，从 9 月到 11 月前前后后白送了四个加设置开关的 PR，分别是 #13458、#16763、#21248 和 #27077，结果无一例外全被拒之门外。

最新那个 #27077 甚至已经通过了维护者实机验证，147 个测试全部跑绿，11 月 17 日还是被一句话直接关掉，顺手贴了个 unwanted 的标签。

说到底，T3 Code 免费开源不收订阅费，真实去重用户数和各家模型的 Token 消耗占比，就是 @theo 拿去跟大模型厂商谈合作、给自家商业产品导流、在网上吹 10 万用户的核心筹码。

为了把这张数据报表做漂亮，他宁可撕毁官网承诺，宁可把手伸进用户的本地配置文件，宁可把所有要求关开关的声音按死在门外。

这就是一个打着开源旗号偷数据的独裁小人。靠社区的信任和免费传播起家，转头就把每个用户的行为轨迹、机器数量和跨平台身份当成自家私产，连给你点一下关闭按钮的体面都不肯给。

提醒所有正在用或者准备尝鲜的开发者，多长个心眼，盯紧自己的数据安全，别自己被人家卖了，还在评论区帮着吹良心开源、替人家说好话。

还在用本地版或桌面版的，立刻在 ~/.zshrc 里加上下面两行环境变量重启，或者直接把 https://t.co/WOgVQPKbCD 写进 hosts 拦死：

export T3CODE_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false
export T3CODE_OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true

99% chance nothing happens, 1% chance a single motivated victim compiles all of the evidence clearly (AI makes this much easier than in 2022), creates a group of victims who were harmed by this scammer, and files actual legal action. What will most likely happen is everyone forgets about this in about six days and the space moves on. Probably falling on deaf ears here, but if someone lost a lot of money to this scammer, do consider running point on this and doing what it takes to get some real life consequences. It is actually possible to focus hard and post your way into getting scammers in jail (I've done it twice in my youth. Don't have the energy anymore)

(Although this guy is pretty sophisticated, always tries to retain plausible deniability even in the most severe circumstances and is good at sweeping things under the rug. But it's totally doable)

Also most people probably won't listen or care but to the few that do, the meme coin game and crypto in general is kinda negative sum right now and fairly -EV, especially with the Saylor liquidation hanging in the balance. All of your favourite "influencers" are out to rape you. All of the "narratives" you are trying to trade are crimed up by insider groups. You are 50x better off playing on a literal casino, and 10,000x better off getting a real job and investing in the stock market

I don't want to be that guy and lecture people on how to gamble their money, whether it's on blackjack or shitcoins, but it really harms the soul to see massive stacks of innocent people's money constantly be funneled to these absolute shameless clowns. It's really really gross.

Hope everyone is keeping well BTW. Good luck out there, and just think about how the last few years went in crypto, analyse if you think you spent your time wisely, and if the same few years repeated again, would be happy with yourself and your progress. CT isn't what it used to be, it might be time to find better pursuits. (Talking to the normies here, smarter people with >5m net worth probably made a killing feeding off the poor)

I am praying that when the Dems take power in 2028, there is a massive retroactive wave of justice where AGI analyses every single tweet, every single transaction, and metes out justice for every single crime that happened on this god forsaken platform and industry from 2020 to today, every single "private key drain" and bundled coin and unpaid shill leading lambs to the slaughter. text:
看到有一些圈内朋友去做保险了，很多人对保险有着不小的误解。如果身边出现了卖保险的朋友，好像总觉得自己的口袋被盯上了。

朋友们，保险是多伟大的风险分摊杠杆工具呀。

最古早的保险，来源于出海商人，风浪、沉船风险极高。大家约定：一批货如果不幸沉没，损失由所有参与贸易的商人一起分摊，而不是由某一个人倾家荡产承担。这就是保险最原始的形态：风险共担。

后来14世纪意大利热那亚，出现了正式的海上保险保单；伦敦劳合社，就是从咖啡馆里的商人互助约定，变成全球知名保险市场。

本质：单个个体扛不住的巨大损失，用一小笔固定保费，把风险交给一群人共同承接。

不夸张地讲，我的保险都是我追着经纪人买的，因为我没有办法预测明天和意外哪一个先来。不管是意外还是疾病，一旦发生，我希望自己至少还有兜底。

而在交易里，最接近这件事的，是买入一份保护性看跌期权。

你已经持有英伟达，暂时还不想卖，又怕一段时间内大跌。

于是先付一笔费用，买到一项权利：在约定的期限内，有权按事先说好的价格卖出。这笔费用，很像保费；那个约定卖出价，很像能托住的位置；到期日，则像保单的有效期。

模拟一下：假设你持有英伟达，现价 150 美元，花 5 美元，买入一个月后到期、行权价 135 美元的看跌期权，暂不计手续费。下面不是实时报价。

到期跌到 90 美元：没有这份权利，股票只剩 90 美元；有了它，你仍可按 135 美元卖出。亏损不会消失，但卖出价被约定住了。

到期还在 150 美元，或涨到 180 美元：你不必使用这项权利，股票继续留着。已经付过的 5 美元不会退回来。没出险，保费也不会回来。

所以，它解决的是「不想卖、又怕跌」，不是让风险消失，也不是无限期保护。注意：保护只覆盖到到期日；行权价不同，能托住的位置也不同；期限更长，费用通常也更高。

用OKX简易期权为自己的仓位上保险，学废了吗🫣

text:
The recent Sky/Spark liquidity event set off a chain reaction across lending markets.

Level 1: capital moved to depth and safety. USDC deposits on @aave V3 Ethereum grew by $1.4B in a week. Aave is the natural destination, with the deepest liquidity and largest TVL in DeFi lending. The inflow pushed its USDC borrow APY down to ~1.9%.

Level 2: the Spark Liquidity Layer pulled ~$468M from the Morpho cbBTC/USDC market on Base. Grove x Steakhouse USDC removed another ~$125M.

This is the largest market behind @coinbase Onchain Loans. With liquidity gone, the borrow APY jumped to ~10%, more than double its usual ~4.5%.

To refill liquidity and bring rates down, Steakhouse High Yield USDC Edition moved ~$300M from the USDe/USDC market into cbBTC/USDC. USDe/USDC on Base went from $370M supply / $329M borrows to $58M / $51M, with $7M of liquidity left.

Level 3: Morpho vault curators are restricted to Morpho markets, so they rotated to BTC markets on Ethereum that aren't correlated with Base: cbBTC/USDT (+$37M) and WBTC/USDC (+$27M), where yields are now lower. Borrowers moved too. With USDC on Aave now cheap to borrow, institutional BTC borrowers added ~$118M of USDC borrows against cbBTC.

This is a reminder that DeFi liquidity behaves like a graph, and isolated markets don't isolate liquidity risk. With more curators running multi-protocol vaults, liquidity is in practice shared across protocols, markets, curators and chains.

For lending protocols, depth is the real moat. For curators, it's speed and how fast you move before the liquidity is gone.

Open Binance App → Wallet → Market → Gacha, then follow these steps:

text:
Year Two

Some assorted goals:

- make Monad a legitimately great platform for personal finance (investing in equities, bonds, etc), especially for getting access to markets outside of one's home country. So much of the usage in crypto right now is gambling/memecoins... it is what it is, but personal finance appeals to 100x more people, and they don't churn out. A legitimately great platform has great asset selection, efficient execution (low cost both in and out of a position), and competitive rates both for borrowers and lenders

- ship Private Settlement Domains with the first user, to serve as a case study for anyone trying to reason about how private environments can compose with shared liquidity. Public chains and private environments have been very far apart in practice and it's time to change that

- hammer out an excellent liquidity landscape on chain. It is a mix of order books, prop AMMs, offchain routers, onchain routers, and RFQ... especially with tokenized equities, there is a long long tail of assets and we need to minimize spreads so that the offering is competitive with TradFi. Spread minimization means helping makers quote sustainably; here designs like APES can help

- make it easier for AI to produce actually good trading strategies on command for anyone to execute a trading plan efficiently with algos. There is are a ton of slop startups out there which are a wrapper around claude asking it "should I buy or sell given these textual inputs"... that's not real quant research and not good execution. At the same time, there are a lot of building blocks for quant trading that AI couldn't one-shot, but given the blocks it could put them together sensibly

- contribute to there being fewer hacks (and a lower total $ stolen) in the crypto industry, probably through a combination of repetition about dedicated devices (SO many hacks are from people plugging hardware wallets into everyday laptops) and encouraging everyone to use tools that our team has shipped for agentic threat detection (e.g. Ultrafuzz). I truly think that security is the biggest blocker to adoption, and that we're basically all in this together

- drive the car faster than ever in multiple races - MEV-resistance, quantum-resistance, privacy, and MCP, challenging all competitors to ship or be left behind

- help NFTs and onchain social -- two deeply out-of-consensus areas -- make a comeback. The builders in these sectors these days are incredibly committed; there's never been a better filtering function

- contribute to tech optimism. So many doomers out there. Life is electric, building is electric

- contribute to a less stressful environment for builders. It is a very weird time to be a builder in DeFi... on the one hand, tools are better than ever... on the other hand, capital is scarce and crypto-natives are jaded. The approach to building ironically requires both more introspection and more rapid, rapid shipping

- support the excellent individuals on our team at MF become leaders in the space in their respective domains. We have amazing folks here and the space needs leadership more than ever

- support someone building a total moonshot

- build at least one product that has a lot of everyday-people customers, and deliver a ton of value to them

- become willing to repeatedly say the same thing, until it starts to sink in

text:
I disagree with @ryandcrypto here. P/S is a weak metric for comparing crypto with equities

Revenue says nothing about how much of it reaches holders

@vasily_sumanov tracks P/FCFt at @valueverse_ai

FCFt = free cash flow to token holders. Revenue that actually reaches holders via distributions and buybacks. Emission-funded rewards excluded

Annualized figures:

• $PUMP: $323M holder cash flow / 6.6x
• $HYPE: $686M / 88.7x
• $AAVE: $16.9M / 93.3x
• $DRV: $962K / 82.7x

Note: $PUMP, $HYPE and $AAVE use all-supply valuation. $DRV uses staked supply

For the equities @ryandcrypto mentioned, I didn't use classic FCF. Some of that cash stays inside the business. To compare with token holder value capture, I counted only cash dividends + buybacks over the last 12 months

The equity multiple here is:

Market cap / (dividends + buybacks paid over the latest reported 12 months).

Using Nov 24 market caps:

• $AAPL: $15.72B dividends + $86.39B buybacks = $102.11B returned. Against a $5.15T market cap → 50.4x.

• $MSFT: $27.03B dividends + $15.69B buybacks = $42.72B returned. Against a $3.68T market cap → 86.1x.

• $NVDA: $12.56B dividends + $64.98B buybacks = $77.54B returned. Against a $3.75T market cap → 48.4x.

• $GOOGL: $10.47B common dividends + $5.50B buybacks = $15.97B returned. Against a $3.43T market cap → 214.8x.

My takeaways:

1) P/S alone won't make me buy or pass on any of these. I want to know how much revenue reaches holders

2) $PUMP looks interesting at 6.6x

3) At ~89-93x for $HYPE and $AAVE, I'd need holder cash flow to grow a lot from here

text:
Thatcher and Reagan made their arguments while the Soviet Union was still standing. What interests me is what happened to those arguments after it fell. A whole generation grew up with the sense that the great economic debate had been settled. Somewhere along the way, the collapse of the Soviet system came to count as proof that we’d got our own system right.

That idea seeped into the culture. A politician could say “small government” and sound responsible before telling you which public service they would cut. They could promise growth and sound patriotic before you had any idea how they meant to achieve it, or whose life it would improve. You could pick all of that up without ever reading Thatcher or Reagan. It was just what a serious person was supposed to sound like.

Some of those policies may well have worked for a time. That helps explain why people kept faith with them. But a policy can solve a problem in one decade and help create another over the next three. Take housing. If you bought a home years ago, rising prices may have given you security and something to leave your children. If you grew up on the same street and now spend so much on rent that you can barely save a deposit, those same years look rather different. Both of you understand perfectly well how the economy works. You’ve experienced it from opposite sides of the ownership gap.

That’s why I find the call to get back to Thatcher or Reagan so incurious. The Britain we’re being asked to repair is partly the product of the choices we’re being asked to repeat. Anyone making that case today owes us an account of what those choices achieved, what they cost and who is still paying. Surely that’s the job of governing.
author: AliRehmanMalik3
quoted_text:
I grew up on Zeppelin, Guns N’ Roses and Bon Jovi. You pick up a guitar because you want to sound like the people you love. You can spend years getting every bend right before it occurs to you to ask what you want to play. I think something similar has happened in politics.

“Big government or small government?” I can understand why that question carried such weight in the years of Thatcher, Reagan and the Cold War. What bothers me is how readily we still accept it as the first question. Say “growth” with enough conviction and you can sound like a patriot before you’ve said who stands to gain or what will actually improve.

Take disability policy. A minister says more people should be able to work. Fine. Can someone get there? Can they manage the hours? If a shift leaves them in pain for two days, what would make the next one possible? And what does the state owe the person for whom work will always be beyond reach? Which of those questions does “small government” answer?

That’s where Rahma, mercy, comes in. 

Jesus asked people to remember whom the Sabbath was made for. We ought to remember whom government is for. There are people living with the consequences of decisions made in rooms they will never enter. If you sit in one of those rooms, you owe them the work of finding out what your decisions mean in their lives. The slogans you grew up with can’t do that work for you.

text:
xAI 三位联合创始人张国栋（Guodong Zhang）、戴子航（Zihang Dai）和 Manuel Kroiss 创立了新公司 Epochal，目标是做出预测能力超越人类的 AI。张国栋个人出资 1 亿美元，团队还吸纳了来自 OpenAI、Anthropic 和 Google DeepMind 的前员工。

AI 预测其实有两条技术路线。比较成熟的是时间序列模型，代表产品有 Nixtla 的 TimeGPT 和 Google 的 TimesFM，主要用于预测销量、电力负荷等具有历史数值规律的指标。但现实世界充满突发变量，一场战争、一项新政策，都可能让过去的规律失效。

近年来，FutureSearch、Mantic 等初创公司开始尝试用大模型做预测。它们让 AI 像专业分析师一样，自己查新闻、读财报、搜集证据，再判断一件事发生的概率。Mantic 今年 9 月还拿到了 2500 万美元融资。

训练这类 AI 有个天然的难题：数学题做完就能验算，代码写完就能运行，但预测未来可能要等几年才能知道对错。拿历史事件来训练，AI 又很容易提前看到答案。

Epochal 花了 90 天搭建 Time Portal，收录过去 30 多年间超过 1 万亿个网页，部分网页甚至可以回溯到分钟级别。除了搜索和浏览网页，AI 所处的虚拟机、系统时钟、软件包仓库和网络访问也被限制在指定的历史时间。

团队选取了 Kalshi 和 Polymarket 上的 347 道真实预测题，先让 AI 在结果揭晓前作答，几周后再利用 Time Portal 回到当时重做。两次预测的误差高度一致，初步验证了利用历史互联网模拟真实预测环境的可行性。

当前大模型强化学习的一大瓶颈，是缺少高质量、可自动验证的训练任务。编程模型已经可以利用 GitHub 上真实发生的软件故障进行训练，通过运行测试获得奖励。

Epochal 想把这种训练方式扩展到整个真实世界。过去几十年的企业兴衰、金融危机、技术革命和政策变化，都有可能被转化为强化学习任务。AI 可以根据当时的信息作出预测，再用真实的历史结局给自己的判断打分。原本需要等待数年的反馈，现在可以立即获得。

不过，即使把互联网恢复到 2008 年，一个读过金融史的大模型也可能早就知道雷曼兄弟会破产。预测对了，究竟是学会了分析经济形势，还是记住了历史课本里的答案？如何解决模型预训练阶段已经记住历史结局的问题，仍是这套训练方法的一大难关。

目前 Epochal 已开放 Time Portal 的 API，并提供企业级服务，其他 AI 实验室也可以接入这套环境。

Announcing Epochal! ✨

We believe the best measure of intelligence is the ability to predict the future. Doing so requires learning about the past and constantly working to be less wrong.

Today's AI has read almost everything and lived through almost nothing. It learns from the internet all at once, already knowing how each story ends. 

We want it to live through thousands of yesterdays instead, one day at a time, the way people do.

So, we built Epochal Time Portal, the first true point-in-time environment with trillions of pages spanning 30 years of history, where agents can browse the Internet as it existed on a past date.

That's a big deal for anyone trying to use AI video for actual creative work.

The more control creators have over the output, the less time they spend regenerating clips and hoping for the best.

Maybe the next big leap in AI video isn't just better visuals. It's finally getting the model to follow directions.

privacy in finance isn’t about making everything invisible.

it’s about deciding what should stay private, what can be verified, and who is allowed to see a specific value when it actually matters.

that’s one part of @primus_labs I think is easy to underestimate.

with FHE, balances and amounts can stay encrypted while smart contracts still operate on them.

but Primus goes one step further.

decryption doesn’t have to mean “make everything public.”

access to a specific value can become an explicit, controlled and auditable action.

so an institution could keep positions and strategy private by default, while still allowing an authorized auditor or regulator to inspect exactly what they need.

private by default.

selectively verifiable when necessary.

that feels much closer to how real institutional finance should work onchain.
