text:
an underrated shift in capital markets is the growing share of investors with more Silicon Valley-rooted DNA. it makes sense that in 2026, SV has become a larger part of the influence on financial markets given:

- the largest companies in the world today have deep ties to it in a way that was less true of past leadership
- all companies are staying private longer and so private capital has now grown substantially which clearly impact the public markets (especially as we have fewer and fewer public companies)
- the shift from traditional media to social media means that today's talking-head class skews more SV and tech-based than Wall Street (TBPN vs CNBC as an illustrative example)
- a whole class of investors only knows this multi-decade tech-dominated supercycle we have been in

these factors also lead to some second and third order effects. for better or worse, there is much more inherent optimism in technology and innovation and progress today. another way to say this might be that there is also much more naiveté. for a decade plus, a lot of tradfi guys looked at mag7 companies and said "too expensive, look at the p/e, no thanks" -- these people were tremendously wrong in hindsight. those co's turned out to be cheap bc the growth was insane and sustained. but as SV becomes a larger share of financial markets, there is more predisposition to say "humans can't think exponentially", "techno-optimism", "my portco's look expensive but will be cheap in hindsight"

there is a fine line between being a techno-optimist and respecting the reality of public markets. investors who cut their teeth exclusively in private markets historically waited 5, 7, 10, 15 years to realize the fruits of their investments. and in many cases, as @WillManidis points out(https://t.co/F4E8PkMWBB), the winningest trade was to "overpay" for elon exposure or to "overpay" for [xyz] exposure. the earlier you did this, the more frequently you now update your gulfstream model

but as the area between private and public markets becomes murkier, these investors are subject to a much more ruthless pricing model. the reality of private markets is that the clearing price is set by a very limited set of participants, who are incentivized to view these companies in the maximally optimistic light. especially as these companies grow into decabillion and centibillion scale, there's only a handful of individuals who are actually setting the clearing price. and i would argue that the cliquey nature of these markets only adds to the inherent premium a lot of these companies have enjoyed (or still enjoy)

but when these companies go public, reality sets in as the clearing price is now set by a much larger and more sophisticated (and shorter-term demanding) group of investors. crypto participants are all too familiar with this dynamic

just in the last year we've seen SPCX, FIG, GEMI get instantly re-rated. SNOW trades roughly flat to its day-1 close ~6 years ago. ABNB similarly. PATH -75% from IPO. RIVN. the list goes on

nobody would argue that the tech and progress we've seen has been impressive but there are a million examples of great company, terrible investment (and visa versa). the increasing influence of narrative as a share of how assets are priced just means that the pace at which re-ratings happen in either direction is faster

and the reality of that fact is we will continue to see people who were "right" and either blew up or gave back huge gains because they rode the momentum off a cliff or simply failed to interrogate the opposing view

public investing is probably the most competitive and cutthroat sport there is and a lot of technology investors imo are going from their weekly home poker game to the WSOP
author: based16z
quoted_text:
there are many vcs with much better track records at much larger scale than I have had on my own book making very classic mistakes of judgement on the leo situation, I do not mean to place myself above them in any way.

its just hard not to reflect in late july, when the entire world feels like its ground to a stop under the crushing city heat, on what exactly this business has become and how we can reason about the things we now believe about how we got here.

sustained outperformance in private market   software over the last decade was not driven by risk sizing, not driven by leverage, but simply by networks and rotating size into those networks.

you simply made money overpaying for the elon trade over the last 20 years, you will do the same overpaying for the {can't name him} trade or the {can't name him} index today.

I think one of the very few lessons we can take away from the roughly post-uber IPO to pre-openai first gilded age of scaled privates is that very few of us understood what the "product" "LPs" were buying actually was. hint: its not risk free returns

a lot of the industry got very rich offering the elon-index or the xyz-index which was not a game of position sizing, or risk, or even fund or product sizing, nor was it a particularly easy game (god knows, im flying commercial and you all are not)- but LPs were perhaps more lucid about what that product was than we ever were ourselves.

i remember a moment sitting across from an investor who was justifying his partnership doing the A, or the B, or the god knows what early round of one of the now trillion dollar labs- and him saying "man theres literally no data you just kind of got to lick your finger and stick it in the air but thats what we're paid to do" and realizing in that moment that he had more situational awareness than the rest of us combined.

it felt like a high water mark but god knows the only high water mark he's concerned about at this point is where the waves will crest on his $150m nantucket compound. he was a much better investor than almost all of us pridefully penning essays on VMS and feedback loops

things are legible now, and you get paid quite a lot for trading in and out of them. in the fullness of time we'll get back to the investing business once this feudal land claim era of SPVs and capped forwards fades away, but its a trading era now. and i don't think many will make it out with their convictions in tact

quoted_text:
The establishment liberal right has no solutions to the problems that their complacency and cowardice allowed their ostensible leftist opponents to cause. 

In the United States, they claim to represent the values of the Founding Fathers, while taking blank-slate anthropology, Civil Rights, and religious pluralism for granted as conservative values.

In their debate with Nick Frietas and Christian Heins, Jeremy Boering and Joel Berry said that, despite recognising that intolerable Weimar conditions led to totalitarian solutions, they wouldn't act until things got worse and Congress was "half fascist, half communist". 

Even then, they wouldn't be willing to wield the kind of power required to reverse that situation. 

They plan to spend their time policing perceived racism and antisemitism on the right instead. 

They abhor White identity politics, and deny that White people exist, while demanding you respect foreign religions, play identity politics for minority groups, and afford Israel a nationalism that you deny yourself.

As Sam Francis wrote in "Beautiful Losers", these conservatives, "having silently and unconsciously accepted the premises and goals, will also come to accept even the means by which the left has secured its dominance", and so will accept their defeated status as part of their identity as conservatives.

If you're offering a politics of always being on the losing end of a revolution, then young men with little to lose won't listen to you anymore.

Starving Bitcoin of hashrate does not mean they get to redefine Bitcoin. It merely means they quit mining Bitcoin. The Bitcoin community restored functionality by changing the proof-of-work algorithm (long overdue IMO), and it's been flourishing since in a way that had been nearly lost the last decade.

Tokenized stocks: supply growth weathers the market slump, and NVIDIA dominates onchain markets.

Here’s your digest for the past two weeks (Nov 9–22).

→ Issuance: $3.70B, supply up 8.7%
→ DEX volume: $2.72B, down 13.5%
→ $194M in net new issuance
→ Holder positions up 11.7k to 469.7k

Stock prices fell and trading slowed, but supply kept growing, and most of the growth was NVIDIA.

Tokenized NVIDIA supply grew by $275M across issuers while the stock tanked in mid-November amid the leadership crisis. That's 93% of the period's net supply growth.

The three biggest NVIDIA tokens also traded $834M, about 31% of all DEX volume, up from ~20% in our first edition. @RobinhoodCrypto's NVDA was the most traded single token, at $395M.

Last edition's biggest additions pulled back. The bStocks tokens for SpaceX (−$95M), Alphabet (−$30M), Intel (−$25M) and QQQ (−$20M) all shrank.

Chips held up: a 3x semiconductor ETF (+$54M), SanDisk (+$43M), Micron (+$14M) and SK Hynix (+$10M).

Robinhood kept 48% of DEX volume, at $1.30B. Binance's bStocks volume fell 25% to $756M. At $1.29B, Nov 16–22 was the quietest week since we started tracking in late September.

On issuance, bStocks (+$139M) and @xStocksFi (+$117M) each grew about 11%. xStocks added the most holders, at +4.7k.

Now for the biggest stories of the past two weeks.

quoted_text:
Year Two

Some assorted goals:

- make Monad a legitimately great platform for personal finance (investing in equities, bonds, etc), especially for getting access to markets outside of one's home country. So much of the usage in crypto right now is gambling/memecoins... it is what it is, but personal finance appeals to 100x more people, and they don't churn out. A legitimately great platform has great asset selection, efficient execution (low cost both in and out of a position), and competitive rates both for borrowers and lenders

- ship Private Settlement Domains with the first user, to serve as a case study for anyone trying to reason about how private environments can compose with shared liquidity. Public chains and private environments have been very far apart in practice and it's time to change that

- hammer out an excellent liquidity landscape on chain. It is a mix of order books, prop AMMs, offchain routers, onchain routers, and RFQ... especially with tokenized equities, there is a long long tail of assets and we need to minimize spreads so that the offering is competitive with TradFi. Spread minimization means helping makers quote sustainably; here designs like APES can help

- make it easier for AI to produce actually good trading strategies on command for anyone to execute a trading plan efficiently with algos. There is are a ton of slop startups out there which are a wrapper around claude asking it "should I buy or sell given these textual inputs"... that's not real quant research and not good execution. At the same time, there are a lot of building blocks for quant trading that AI couldn't one-shot, but given the blocks it could put them together sensibly

- contribute to there being fewer hacks (and a lower total $ stolen) in the crypto industry, probably through a combination of repetition about dedicated devices (SO many hacks are from people plugging hardware wallets into everyday laptops) and encouraging everyone to use tools that our team has shipped for agentic threat detection (e.g. Ultrafuzz). I truly think that security is the biggest blocker to adoption, and that we're basically all in this together

- drive the car faster than ever in multiple races - MEV-resistance, quantum-resistance, privacy, and MCP, challenging all competitors to ship or be left behind

- help NFTs and onchain social -- two deeply out-of-consensus areas -- make a comeback. The builders in these sectors these days are incredibly committed; there's never been a better filtering function

- contribute to tech optimism. So many doomers out there. Life is electric, building is electric

- contribute to a less stressful environment for builders. It is a very weird time to be a builder in DeFi... on the one hand, tools are better than ever... on the other hand, capital is scarce and crypto-natives are jaded. The approach to building ironically requires both more introspection and more rapid, rapid shipping

- support the excellent individuals on our team at MF become leaders in the space in their respective domains. We have amazing folks here and the space needs leadership more than ever

- support someone building a total moonshot

- build at least one product that has a lot of everyday-people customers, and deliver a ton of value to them

- become willing to repeatedly say the same thing, until it starts to sink in

text:
If you're holding $PRL, the new WPRL/USDT pool on @metricxyz gives you another way to use it: provide liquidity and earn from trading activity.

Here's a simple walkthrough.

wPRL is wrapped PRL on Ethereum. You lock native PRL through @pearlbridgexyz and receive wPRL, backed 1:1 before bridging fees. To go back, you burn wPRL and the bridge releases PRL.

That lets you use Pearl in Ethereum DeFi, including this pool curated by Carcosa.

As an LP, you provide the tokens traders swap against. You earn a cut of the spread (after Metric and curator fees), and it auto-compounds.

Metric groups liquidity into moving price-range “bins.” You only earn when trades hit your bins, idle liquidity earns nothing.

Last time I checked, the pool showed:

• 433.41% APR
• $98.92K in liquidity
• $1.65M in volume over the selected 7-day window

If you want you can use my ref link here:
https://t.co/90e6wKNKQ1

You can approach the LP in three ways:

1. You want to accumulate WPRL.

Put USDT in bins below the active price. When sellers trade into those bins, your USDT buys WPRL and earns a share of the spread.

2. You're happy to sell some WPRL.

Put WPRL in bins above the active price. When buyers reach those bins, your WPRL converts into USDT while earning a spread.

3. You're comfortable holding either token.

Supply both across suitable bins. Your position buys and sells WPRL as traders use the liquidity.

There are real trade-offs called impermanent loss (IL).

In case you're not familiar, IL means you can lose money or end up worse off than simply holding the underlying assets. So make sure you know how to hedge that.

Also, WPRL is set to become WPEARL later this week. Pearl Bridge says the contracts and pools will stay the same.

有人问他：现在最值得关注的CEO是谁？  

他没说马斯克，没说黄仁勋，直接点了一个很多人没想到的人：Shopify的Tobi Lütke。  

原因只有一个：这哥们自己写代码。  

“他发给OpenAI的产品反馈，比地球上任何一个人都详细。他永远领先其他CEO六到八个月。”  

不是六到八天，是六到八个月。  

Altman的潜台词很明确：  

一、亲手使用模型的人，和只听汇报的人，已经是两个物种。 Tobi从最早期就自己下场写代码、跑实验、压测能力边界。不是让下属出个调研报告，是自己亲自下场。  

二、Shopify内部下了死命令：每个人必须自己建Agent，否则出局。 不搞试点小组，不搞创新实验室，全员上桌。这不是转型口号，是生存筛选。

而真正拉开差距的人，已经在自己的终端里敲命令了。  

AI时代最大的不平等，不是谁的公司大、谁融的钱多：  

是谁真的在用，谁还在看。

text:
Ethereum's post-quantum transition has another major challenge - validator signatures.

Today, Ethereum's consensus layer relies on BLS signatures.

They are extremely useful because thousands of validators can aggregate their signatures into a compact proof. This keeps consensus communication efficient.

But BLS relies on elliptic-curve cryptography, which is vulnerable to sufficiently powerful quantum computers.

Ethereum's proposed direction is hash-based signatures.

The trade-off is significant
BLS signatures are compact and easy to aggregate.
Hash-based signatures offer a post-quantum security path.
But their signatures are much larger.
Validator clients, networking, aggregation and hardware requirements all need redesign.

This creates a difficult engineering problem - Ethereum must preserve efficient consensus while replacing one of its foundational cryptographic assumptions.

The EF's PQAI initiative is exploring this transition, with early post-quantum devnet work already underway.

It is not a simple cryptographic library update. It touches the machinery that allows Ethereum to reach finality.

The real test of Ethereum's post-quantum roadmap will be replacing its cryptography without sacrificing the decentralization that cryptography helps protect.

author: eyobnad
quoted_text:
Year Two

Some assorted goals:

- make Monad a legitimately great platform for personal finance (investing in equities, bonds, etc), especially for getting access to markets outside of one's home country. So much of the usage in crypto right now is gambling/memecoins... it is what it is, but personal finance appeals to 100x more people, and they don't churn out. A legitimately great platform has great asset selection, efficient execution (low cost both in and out of a position), and competitive rates both for borrowers and lenders

- ship Private Settlement Domains with the first user, to serve as a case study for anyone trying to reason about how private environments can compose with shared liquidity. Public chains and private environments have been very far apart in practice and it's time to change that

- hammer out an excellent liquidity landscape on chain. It is a mix of order books, prop AMMs, offchain routers, onchain routers, and RFQ... especially with tokenized equities, there is a long long tail of assets and we need to minimize spreads so that the offering is competitive with TradFi. Spread minimization means helping makers quote sustainably; here designs like APES can help

- make it easier for AI to produce actually good trading strategies on command for anyone to execute a trading plan efficiently with algos. There is are a ton of slop startups out there which are a wrapper around claude asking it "should I buy or sell given these textual inputs"... that's not real quant research and not good execution. At the same time, there are a lot of building blocks for quant trading that AI couldn't one-shot, but given the blocks it could put them together sensibly

- contribute to there being fewer hacks (and a lower total $ stolen) in the crypto industry, probably through a combination of repetition about dedicated devices (SO many hacks are from people plugging hardware wallets into everyday laptops) and encouraging everyone to use tools that our team has shipped for agentic threat detection (e.g. Ultrafuzz). I truly think that security is the biggest blocker to adoption, and that we're basically all in this together

- drive the car faster than ever in multiple races - MEV-resistance, quantum-resistance, privacy, and MCP, challenging all competitors to ship or be left behind

- help NFTs and onchain social -- two deeply out-of-consensus areas -- make a comeback. The builders in these sectors these days are incredibly committed; there's never been a better filtering function

- contribute to tech optimism. So many doomers out there. Life is electric, building is electric

- contribute to a less stressful environment for builders. It is a very weird time to be a builder in DeFi... on the one hand, tools are better than ever... on the other hand, capital is scarce and crypto-natives are jaded. The approach to building ironically requires both more introspection and more rapid, rapid shipping

- support the excellent individuals on our team at MF become leaders in the space in their respective domains. We have amazing folks here and the space needs leadership more than ever

- support someone building a total moonshot

- build at least one product that has a lot of everyday-people customers, and deliver a ton of value to them

- become willing to repeatedly say the same thing, until it starts to sink in

text:
The recent Sky/Spark liquidity event set off a chain reaction across lending markets.

Level 1: capital moved to depth and safety. USDC deposits on @aave V3 Ethereum grew by $1.4B in a week. Aave is the natural destination, with the deepest liquidity and largest TVL in DeFi lending. The inflow pushed its USDC borrow APY down to ~1.9%.

Level 2: the Spark Liquidity Layer pulled ~$468M from the Morpho cbBTC/USDC market on Base. Grove x Steakhouse USDC removed another ~$125M.

This is the largest market behind @coinbase Onchain Loans. With liquidity gone, the borrow APY jumped to ~10%, more than double its usual ~4.5%.

To refill liquidity and bring rates down, Steakhouse High Yield USDC Edition moved ~$300M from the USDe/USDC market into cbBTC/USDC. USDe/USDC on Base went from $370M supply / $329M borrows to $58M / $51M, with $7M of liquidity left.

Level 3: Morpho vault curators are restricted to Morpho markets, so they rotated to BTC markets on Ethereum that aren't correlated with Base: cbBTC/USDT (+$37M) and WBTC/USDC (+$27M), where yields are now lower. Borrowers moved too. With USDC on Aave now cheap to borrow, institutional BTC borrowers added ~$118M of USDC borrows against cbBTC.

This is a reminder that DeFi liquidity behaves like a graph, and isolated markets don't isolate liquidity risk. With more curators running multi-protocol vaults, liquidity is in practice shared across protocols, markets, curators and chains.

For lending protocols, depth is the real moat. For curators, it's speed and how fast you move before the liquidity is gone.

text:
Real talk. I need an opportunity or I need to pack it up.

I’ve been doing a lot of thinking lately about where I’m at in life, my career, and my future in this space.

And if I’m being honest, I’m reaching a point where I have to question whether continuing down this path is sustainable.

For the last 2–3 months, I’ve been working an overnight, in-person job six days a week. 10/11 hour days , It’s consuming nearly all of my time and energy.

If I get 6–8 hours of sleep, I’m left with 3–4 hours to cook, clean, eat, get to the gym, grocery shop, commute, and somehow maintain everything else in my life.

I just woke up from 13 hours of sleep. My body clearly needed it, but it’s also a reminder that this pace isn’t healthy or sustainable.

I’ve been applying for opportunities again. My last push involved 40+ applications, and it resulted in zero interviews.

That’s a tough pill to swallow when you know how much you’ve invested in yourself and this industry.

I’ve built relationships, created content, worked with projects, organized events, traveled internationally, helped onboard people into Solana, and built things of my own.

I have years of experience, a wealth of knowledge, a willingness to learn, and an even greater willingness to execute.

But passion doesn’t pay rent. Potential doesn’t pay bills. And I can’t keep putting my life on hold waiting for an opportunity that may never come.

I’m approaching 40. I have to make decisions that are right for me, my future, and my quality of life.

It’s difficult watching opportunities go to people half my age while I’m still trying to get someone to give me a shot. I’m not saying they don’t deserve those opportunities. I’m saying I’d like the chance to demonstrate what I can bring to the table, too.

I don’t necessarily want to leave Web3. I believe in this space, and I believe in what I’ve been building.

But I may have to stop making this industry the center of my financial future.

I’m open to opportunities both inside and outside Web3, particularly in marketing, content, partnerships, business development, community, and growth.

I’m looking for something with a real salary or dependable pay, room to grow, and an opportunity to make an impact.

I don’t need another promise, another unpaid opportunity, or another pat on the back for grinding.

I need a shot.

I don’t want applause for running on a treadmill. I want an opportunity to actually move forward.

If you know of a team looking for someone with my experience, I’d genuinely appreciate an introduction.

I’m not giving up on myself. I’m just starting to recognize that I have to make decisions that put my life first.

This is really the kind of result that I never thought I would see in my lifetime.

(btw, by an "old" result of Yin Tat Lee and collaborators this also implies that linear programs can be solved in time n^{9/4}.)

I've heard of math PhD students losing motivation because AI is solving everything. This is nonsense. If I look at my PhD field - computational complexity theory - the big questions are all just as open as they've been for decades. We barely know anything. We can't prove things that seem trivial and obvious at first glance:
As one example, we can't prove that a poly time algorithm can't always be simulated in logarithmic space!
Like in the metaphore with two men running away from a bear - it's easier today to have an edge over your competitors. People are so distracted, and most people don't even think that's a problem because they believe AI can do their thinking for them better than they can, so why go to the trouble of focusing?
Carve a chunk of the day where you're doing things old school - just you a pen and paper and maybe a book. No internet access for a continuous chunk of time. I'm solving (trying :) ) exercises from silverman EC book at the moment.

PPl who will preserve the ability to think humans used to have till fairly recently will have a huge advantage - like the ppl who invested in crypto in early 2010's.

Why can frontier AI models write complex code, yet still occasionally stumble when asked to identify the colors of five simple objects in order or verify what's not in an image?

That disconnect is called jagged intelligence and measuring it scientifically is critical to advancing AI reliability.

Today, @GoogleDeepMind is launching Humanity's First Exam on Kaggle, a benchmark designed to measure "floor reliability": whether models get simple tasks right every time, not just once. It spans 544 text and multimodal prompts across 20 foundational subcategories, in 136 four-prompt families.

Some early findings, across 18 frontier models:
• High single-shot accuracy masks inconsistency: Top five models reach 96%–98% pass@1 and 100% family pass@4, yet average only 85.6% on family pass^4 (80.5%–92.4%), with a 7.6–80.1 percentage-point Family Reliability Gap across all 18 models.
• Visual perception drives 74% of wrong answers: Extra thinking time helps far less on visual tasks than on text.
• Single-step slips are common: In 39% of failed prompt–model pairs, the answer is off by one or has a single wrong element; this holds for 167 of the 298 counting errors.

Current leaderboard:
🥇 GPT- 6.2 Astra (xhigh) - 90.7%

🥉 Gemini 4 Neon (high) - 85.6%

But METR is financially dependent on the Anthropic's success -- specifically, on the explosive growth of more than $7 billion dollars in Anthropic stock.

And GVF is the overwhelming funder of the entire Anthropic Network ecosystem.

This stock was worth $500 million early last year.

METR -- and all of those building a career its parent organizations -- cannot afford to disrupt that growth.

Because if Anthropic goes under, many of the organizations that fund METR go under as well.

But if Anthropic succeeds, METR and its parent organizations become more richly financed to regulate AI -- something those at METR want very much.

The "third-party evaluator" is not "third-party" at all.

The evaluator is on Anthropic's payroll.

If this were the end of it, that's bad.

But that isn't all.

The same organizations that fund METR also fund the many organizations, such as the Tarbell Center, that promote AI Doom.

The Tarbell Center publishes AI Doom articles in The Verge, Science, LA Times, The Dispatch, TIME, and others.

They are selling the problem, and then selling the solution to the problem -- from the same money pile: Anthropic's.

All of these organizations are financially dependent on the same exploding $7 billion money pile.

As Anthropic grows more and more powerful, its AI Doom Machine grows better and better financed -- louder and louder.

Meanwhile, the regulatory regime seeded in METR grows larger to solve the increasingly loud -- now hysterical -- problem of AI Doom that the Anthropic Network itself created.

From this standpoint, as Anthropic becomes more powerful, AI might be getting scarier, sure -- but the positive feedback loop also becomes more deafening -- independent of objective facts.

This itself is an objective fact.

The deafening AI Doom is part of an business model, that, as it expands, so too does the AI Doom messaging -- there is simply more money to do it.

But the problem also goes in the other direction:

If Anthropic dies, the Regulatory Regime and the AI Doom Machine are crippled or die.

Neither METR nor Tarbell nor the other organizations in the Anthropic Network can allow that to happen.

Hence, neither METR or the AI Doom Machine can be trusted to provide independent assessments of Anthropic's models or AI more broadly.

They simply are not organizations independent of Anthropic.

And Anthropic cannot detach itself from METR or Tarbell or countless other safety orgs (not shown here), either, because they drive hype for the models and the possibility of eventual regulatory capture, and Anthropic will not give that up willingly.

What's more, the people at all of these organizations are all the same ecosystem, the same community. They just shuffle between organizations.

The Anthropic Network is therefore, so long as it is successful, locked into a self-amplifying feedback loop inside an ideological monoculture.

And that feedback loop is winning.

That's what Jacob Coxon is.

China is keeping messaging tight. That is why optimism for AI is so high in China.

America has Anthropic: a massive company pushing anti-AI propaganda at a state level.

Anthropic will either create hysteria until American AI slows down and China wins, or it will create fractures throughout American society with severe political consequences.

Ironically, because of the structural financial incentives underpinning the Anthropic Network, it has become the same kind of self-amplifying virus that it fantasizes AI to become in the future -- while hiding its tracks just as carefully.

It is the mirror of the same AI virus that it hypothesizes to consume America.

Anthropic's business model, models itself after the very thing it claims to fear.

Except Anthropic's ideology infects humans, not computers.

Congress must investigate.

The rev-maxxing dynamic amongst some validators is almost a pure archetype of the principal-agent problem. Which I think is exacerbated by depressed prices. When the pie shrinks people will maximise for personal gain. Which in turn, lowers the chance of network success, which makes the pie shrink further. True on blockchains, true in the real world.

It does make one wonder what you'd need to do to finally flip towards positive-sum economics. Subsidies help, but get priced in quickly, are often unsustainable and often get abused. Maybe if we start actually competing with the NASDAQ then improving execution context would become more of a dominant utility function for validators.

The bounty on offer is vast IMO, but the competition is going to be fierce. Especially now we're in a world of centralised databases masquerading as blockchains FUDing us for toxic MEV. 

I do think when coins go up again (pls) the choices to think longer term get easier. Very interesting from an economics perspective in any case!

text:
A lot of you are holding Wearers with no Wearer on your OpenSea profile (some of the biggest holders too, I was just scrolling the holders page), so here's a heads up: the keeper is real and it's going to take them.

It wakes up 24 hours after the last Wearer is minted. From then on it runs once a day, at a moment picked at random and kept hidden until the round is over.

Each round it reads every holder's OpenSea profile picture. If yours is a Wearer you own, every Wearer you hold is safe, in every wallet linked to that profile.

If it isn't, you're at risk. A fifth of the holders at risk, picked at random, lose one Wearer that day, and it goes to a random holder who is wearing theirs. Then the same thing happens the next day, and the day after, until you put one on.

In the contract it's one function, claim(tokenId, to, round), and only the keeper wallet can call it. It can only move a token that has sat with one owner for at least 24 hours (safeUntil(tokenId) shows the exact moment for any token), so someone who just bought always gets a full day to put it on. Every move emits a Claimed event with the round number, so anyone can check all of it onchain.

The keeper can't mint, list, approve or move anything outside claim, and that's fixed in the code.

So if you hold ten, wearing one keeps all ten.

Smart money would kill to buy in the $30ks or $40ks. It would be so obvious.

People will scream “Bitcoin to $35k next” on every dip. They always do. But, in the grand scheme, buying anywhere in the $50ks is a steal.

Bitcoin has bottomed. And if I'm wrong then the next bottom is definitely the real bottom.

The Chinese stock market has no short selling, so there are no short squeezes either. 

Almost every bounce is basically just a trap for buyers, and Chinese retail investors don't even know what Hyperliquid is. 

Chinese stocks basically only have two patterns: they either gap up and fade, or gap down, bounce, and fade again. 

The Chinese market is also much more risk averse, so to some extent, Chinese stocks can predict US market moves.

text:
One wallet now decides where a third of Terra's staked $LUNA sits. No vote authorised it.

At 07:10 AEDT on 25 Nov, about 5¾ hours after Terra prop 4856 passed, terra1kefa2...klgzl moved four TLA control roles from the Phoenix Directive Stewardship DAO to itself.

No Stewardship vote. No Terra governance vote.

Whose wallet? @0xphilipp’s own TLA launch post (12 Aug 2024) lists it as the ERIS owner wallet, with this promise: "Ownership transferred to PD Stewardship after 3 months."

Contract admin was due to move after one month. More than two years on, neither has happened. Owner and admin are still the ERIS wallets.

What the four roles control:
- Delegation: which validators hold 107.6M LUNA of TLA and PD Treasury stake, 33.9% of all staked LUNA
- Asset whitelist: which assets earn TLA rewards, and where each asset's staked LP is sent
- vAMP voter blacklist
- Bribe whitelist

Why it matters:
- 33.9% is above the 33.4% veto line even at 100% turnout. Placed with validators voting NoWithVeto, that stake alone vetoes any Terra proposal and burns its deposit.
- Replay 4856 and 4857 with that stake on the NWV side: both vetoed.
- Concentrated on a few validators, it would give them over a third of consensus power.
- Before 07:10, using these roles needed 3 of 4 Stewardship directors. Now it needs one key.

None of the stake has moved yet. It can be moved at any time, with no one else signing off.

4856 keeps the 2024 handover commitment in force and says any change to it needs express governance and legal approval. The Foundation's contract-by-contract control schedule, which must cover the TLA config, is due by 16 Dec.

Hand the roles back to the Stewardship and complete the handover promised in 2024.

Semi***sis 机构版：Blackwell现货价格下调！！
Semi***sis 机构版今天凌晨发的： 
1. SpaceX下调Blackwell GPU现货报价：小集群单价从此前约15‑15.5美元/GPU·小时降至10‑12美元/GPU·小时，该价格与面向Anthropic、Google等大客户的大规模集群报价拉平；本次调价距离上一轮AI云TCO模型更新仅数周，此前GPU租赁价格曲线仍处在上行阶段。
2. 行业消息显示Anthropic将不再续约在SpaceX规模约5万张H200的GPU集群；SpaceX已开始向其他客户兜售这部分算力资源，预计2027年初可交付，对外报价约5美元/GPU·小时。
3. GPU算力市场已经显现出价格降温的早期信号，短期算力供给快速释放：Anthropic不再续约释放的H200算力叠加SpaceX自身算力集群扩张（明年主力新增机型为Vera Rubin），且SpaceX业务模式偏向现货租赁、而非长期锁单合同。
4. 美国BIS新规进一步增加短期可用算力：原本租给中国客户的算力资源需要重新寻找承租方，增量短期算力供给将对2027年GPU现货租赁价格形成下行压力。
5. 分析师原有测算模型保持不变：维持GB300算力约5000万美元/IT兆瓦/年（折合约12美元/GPU·小时）的假设，SpaceX最新报价落在该预期区间内；Vera Rubin机型定价显著高于Blackwell。
6. 即便Blackwell定价落到10‑12美元/GPU·小时区间，新部署Blackwell项目的投资回报依然具备吸引力，因此分析师判断本次降价不会拖慢SpaceX在2027年的算力基建扩张节奏

Semi这篇快评信息量很大，核心其实就一句话：全球GPU租赁的“稀缺溢价”开始退潮了，但还没到杀上游硬件CapEx的阶段。SpaceX把Blackwell小集群现货价从15美元出头直接砍到10-12美元、跟大客户报价拉平，同时把Anthropic退租的5万张H200按5美元往外甩，背后其实是三重短期供给同时砸盘：一是头部模型厂在换代且更抠ROI（IPO后华尔街死盯着变现，没人愿意继续为老一代Hopper买单）；二是SpaceX明年主力切向Vera Rubin，本身又偏现货租赁、缺少长协锁单缓冲；三是最具讽刺意味的BIS 11.16新规反噬——原本租给中国客户的海外集群被迫回流，硬生生给2027年的全球现货市场砸出了一批额外供给。

不过也别急着喊AI基建见顶，10-12美元的Blackwell其实正好落在每兆瓦5000万美元的基准TCO模型里，新项目IRR依然算得过账，短期还拖不动明年Vera Rubin的扩产节奏。真正要重新定价的，是缺乏大客户长协护城河、靠赚现货溢价和吃Hopper折旧红利的二三线算力Neocloud——当H200跌到5美元、Blackwell小集群失去溢价，算力租赁“有卡就能躺赢”的周期基本结束了，接下来拼的纯粹是电价、融资成本和押注Vera Rubin的换代节奏

text:
为什么那么多人热衷于抄底智谱、MiniMax，甚至一路抄底、一路被套？

行为金融学里有一个非常重要的概念，叫做锚定效应（Anchoring Effect）

智谱的发行价是116.2港元，上市不到半年就被拉到了2980港元。一旦市场接受了3000港元这个价格锚，跌到2000觉得便宜，跌到1000觉得严重低估，跌到500觉得遍地黄金。

今天跌到280港元，相较历史高点已经跌了90.6%，但仍然比发行价高出141%。

这也是为什么低流通盘的股票尤其值得警惕。

智谱首次解禁前，实际流通盘仅占总股本的2.67%；MiniMax也不到6%。在大量原始股东和机构投资者的筹码被锁定的情况下，相对有限的资金就能撬动极高的账面市值。

今年7月8日，智谱约2568万股基石投资者股份解禁；7月9日，MiniMax约1.53亿股解禁，占总股本的48%以上。

紧接着，智谱又在7月13日完成了约314亿港元的配售融资。

站在资本的角度，这种筹码结构天然存在把估值做高的动力：低流通阶段推高股价、制造赚钱效应、建立市场的价格锚；随着限售股陆续解禁，再由二级市场承接不断增加的筹码。

而锚定效应恰恰会让散户在这个过程中源源不断地产生接盘的意愿。

所以，每次想抄底之前，不妨问自己一个问题：

如果你从来没有见过智谱2980港元的股价，今天第一次看到这家公司，你还会觉得1366亿港元的市值很便宜吗？

text:
《交易与交易所》把套利风险分为四类：实施风险、基差风险、模型风险和持有成本风险。

实施风险，是我觉得技术门槛较高的一项。拿跨所套利来讲，拆单和挂 maker 单都是必修课。习惯以双边都走 taker 的成交成本为基准，衡量拆单和挂单究竟省下了多少，又有多少被等待成交期间的价格变动吃掉了。

基差风险比较直观。两条腿都成交以后，基差仍然可能朝不利方向走。同样是价差再走10 个基点，仓位越大，账面浮亏就越大。

模型风险和基差风险，在我看来有一层因果关系。模型给出基差的公允值。如果我连两项资产的定价关系都理解错了，就可能把本来合理的价差当成套利空间，最后表现在基差风险上。

持有成本风险，在永续合约里尤其明显。永续合约没有固定的到期交割日，资金费却按照周期持续结算，对于收敛速度和预期外成本的预估至关重要。

顺着「套利就是卖风险」这个思路看，这四类风险都对应着赚取补偿的机会。

落到目前的 RWA 永续合约市场，我觉得靠模型识别错价仍是基础，但靠执行赚到的钱被严重低估了。

各家交易所的vip费率结构、maker 返佣和挂单激励，在同样一组交易下，利润可能偏差达到20%以上，使用MM账号会更高。

text: Starlink
author: elonmusk
quoted_text:
Five years ago, Starlink wasn't on a single ship. Now it's on 66,866. That's more ships than every provider had combined back then.

Before Starlink, if you were a sailor, your internet came from Inmarsat. An unlimited plan cost €3,259 a month for 2 Mbps, and the whole crew had to share it.

Then Starlink showed up in 2022 at US$5,000 a month for up to 350 Mbps. In 2027, a plan that covers an ullimited whole cargo ship comes in at US$4,650.

OneWeb, the closest rival in low orbit, is on 1,662 ships. Its cheapest unlimited plan is about US$7,400 a month, and it maxes out at 30 Mbps.

Market share at sea, by revenue:
2021: Inmarsat almost a third, Starlink 0%
2024: Starlink 39%, the biggest

To be fair, Inmarsat and OneWeb guarantee a minimum speed and Starlink doesn't. Some fleets still pay extra for that.

Zero to number one in four years, and still the cheaper option. That's hard to compete with.

text:
If you're a creator on Twitter, I highly recommend branching out into TikTok and Instagram. It is much easier to grow there if you lock in properly, and the number of brand deals I get every single day in my emails is exponentially higher than on Twitter.

And this is coming from someone whose full-time income has been brand deals and stuff on Twitter for the past like 3 years. It's just more income now!!

Although Twitter is amazing and I want to continue to grow on here until the day I die, it's literally my full-time job. If you're already creating content on one, it's fairly easy to repurpose it for other socials, and I highly recommend you do that.

When I was ONLY in crypto mostly, cross-posting my Twitter content to other socials was impossible because people hate crypto. With AI, there's a real, genuine community of people who want to learn. On Twitter, people already know what they're talking about, but on other socials, people want to learn about AI from zero.

You can apply the same logic to a brand or app that you're running as well. If you're only marketing it on Twitter, that's a good idea for sure, and you should continue to do that. You definitely need to expand to TikTok and Instagram, and eventually to YouTube Shorts, if not long-form YouTube.

You can do this pretty easily with Grokbot as well. Anytime you make a tweet, an article, or a long-form video that's posted on Twitter, feed it to your Grokbot or AI and ask it how it can clip it up into short-form content. Don't just automate animated shorts, because that sucks and it won't perform well. You need to put your face out there.

since Apex 2 started trading on nov 12:
→ s&p 500: -5.9%
→ nasdaq: -7.8%
→ btc: -16.6%
→ apex 3-month vault: +1.0%

i checked both vault wallets on @HyperliquidX myself. here's what happened.

the 2 vaults on @Infinit_Labs hold $4.02m together: $2.33m in the 3-month vault, $1.69m in the 1-month one. they run the exact same trades. the 3-month vault just trades double the size.

the first 10 days were boring, on purpose:
→ at its worst (nov 20), the s&p was down 8.4%
→ the 3-month vault's worst point was -0.3%
→ most days it sat between -0.2% and 0%

then nov 23. the nasdaq jumped 3.4% in a day.

the book was positioned on both sides. that afternoon it closed its oil shorts (+$4.5k) and part of its s&p long (+$3.1k). the vault went from -$2.3k to +$22.7k in about 13 hours.

where it stands today:
→ 3-month vault: +$23.1k (+0.99%)
→ 1-month vault: +$11.6k (+0.69%)

what the book looks like right now (3-month vault):
→ long: s&p 500, $542k
→ short: oil $248k, spcx $194k, nasdaq $68k, gold $33k
→ $542k long vs $542k short

it doesn't bet on the market going up or down. it bets that oil, the nasdaq and gold do worse than the s&p. when everything dumps together, the two sides cancel out. that's why it held while btc lost 16%.

what worked so far: short nasdaq (+$5.9k), short gold (+$5.5k), short oil (+$4.5k).
what didn't: short spcx (-$6.1k) and the s&p hedge (-$4.6k).

the apex team reports +34% annualized. the math confirms it: +1% in 12 days is about 35% a year.

the vault stayed flat while everything around it bled.

the 1-month vault matures dec 11. i'll check it again then.

从 1 万美元本金起步，到身家接近 1 亿元人民币，30 岁交易员「熬鹰」今年用了不到 11 个月。

11 月 23 日晚，熬鹰重仓押注英伟达上涨，买入仅 15 分钟后，黄仁勋复职的消息突然落地，短短十几分钟获利约 1500 万元。

今日，熬鹰 @thankUcrypto 再度公开个人资产情况，据其自述，目前净资产已接近 1 亿元人民币，最近一个月纯利润达 700 万美元。

而五年前，他还只是一个月薪一万多元的互联网产品经理，每个月从工资里拿出三五千元做交易，最初的梦想只是赚够 20 万元，买一辆特斯拉。

最惨的时候，他手里只剩 1.3 万元，却背着近 40 万元网贷。

2024 年春天，他抓住 BCH 补涨行情，用 22 天将 2 万元做到 100 万元，又用四个月做到 1000 万元。

2025 年，马斯克与特朗普公开争吵，他从特斯拉股价下跌中捕捉到狗狗币的做空机会，短短四小时获利约 101 万美元。

从 bitcoin-cash:native， $DOGE 到英伟达 $NVDA ，熬鹰的交易逻辑始终围绕一个核心：消息发生后，哪些资产已经作出反应，哪些资产还没有被市场充分定价。

经历至少三次大幅亏损后，如今的他开始主动将利润转出，配置股票、现金和房产，每天盯盘的时间也从 18 个小时缩短至 6 个小时。

「这么多年，终于有收手的可能了。」

曾经的他想做那个屠龙夺宝的勇者，现在的他更想成为那条守住宝藏的巨龙。

毕竟，赚到一个亿和守住一个亿，是两种截然不同的能力。

quoted_text:
Why didn’t OpenAI solve the Riemann Hypothesis first? Zhihu contributor SIY.Z found a clue.
TL;DR: @OpenAI’s most consequential contribution may have been a method hidden in a less celebrated proof. SIY.Z argues that Alpöge (@__alpoge__) recognized its potential and developed it further with Anthropic’s model.

A nine-page proof buried among OpenAI’s 722 mathematical results may have supplied the crucial lead for a rival’s breakthrough.

SIY.Z traces a connection between OpenAI’s proof excluding Landau–Siegel zeros and Levent Alpöge’s subsequently reported proof of the generalized Riemann hypothesis with Anthropic.

His central distinction is between the strength of a result and the usefulness of its method. OpenAI’s headline quasi-Riemann hypothesis result already excluded Landau–Siegel zeros. Yet the separate, shorter proof offered an algebraic approach that mathematicians could understand and develop further.

According to SIY.Z, that proof overcame the parity barrier that limits sieve methods. Ben Green and others reportedly simplified its nine pages to roughly five, or three with an external lemma.

Its connection to Stepanov’s polynomial method was especially suggestive. Terence Tao proposed exploring an adelic analogue, bringing arithmetic information across different primes into a common framework.

SIY.Z highlights two ingredients: using the product formula to relate divisibility to size, and interpreting quadratic characters through Frobenius actions so that their values yield usable polynomial congruences.

Alpöge’s subsequent work reportedly connected chains of theta lifts to the role of multiplicity in the earlier argument, providing a way to extend the underlying approach.

For SIY.Z, the revealing detail is that a seemingly redundant result contained a more productive method. His suggestion that OpenAI failed to appreciate its full potential remains an inference about the company’s priorities.

As AI produces more mathematical proofs, how can we get better at spotting the ideas worth pursuing further, even when the results themselves seem redundant?
#AIForMath #NumberTheory #RiemannHypothesis

text:
上条发了三道 3D 题，评论区一帮朋友说题太少、不够硬。

行，这次直接测个够：昨晚通宵连轴转，300 道闭卷硬考 + 5 道实战真题，全给安排上了。

300 道闭卷题跑完，我有点傻眼：
Opus 5.5 258分，HungerG 258分，国产几家全挤在 252 到 259 之间。

分数已经拉不开了。那到底谁好用？只能看真活。
闭卷成绩先摆这儿：

HY4 Flash：259
HungerG：258
Opus 5.5：258
Qwen4-Max：256
GLM-5.4：252

一半写代码，一半多学科推理难题。
不联网、不给工具，同一套评分器逐题判。差一两题说明不了高低，这几家就是同一个梯队。

硬要挑的话：代码那 150 题，HungerG 啃下来 130 题，比 HY4 Flash、Qwen4-Max、GLM-5.4 都高；单题中位用时 8.4 秒，比 Qwen4-Max、HY4 Flash 都快。

真正拉开差距的，是 5 道实战题：

同一份提示词，HungerG、Opus 5.5、GPT-6.2 Sol，再加上腾讯混元刚出的 HY4 Flash，四家同台，每家只跑一次，不许重来。

规矩照旧：截图全不算数，脚本真去点、真去拖拽，交互动得起来才算分。

挑三道给大家细盘一下：

1、土味咖啡店品牌页改版：
原本是个土到掉渣的旧网页，文字一个字不许改。四家都保住了八个商品和购物车，自动检查全满分，差别全在眼睛看得到的地方：HungerG 给八个商品各画了一个咖啡豆包装袋，图案每款都不重样。这审美和完成度，拿去直接上线一点不虚。

2、3000 多行订单做经营看板：
我自己先把表格算了一遍当基准，四家跑完筛出来的数字全对上了，一分钱不差。HungerG 这一页从筛选、指标、趋势到城市排行，从上往下一屏读完，老板看着不费劲。

3、压轴排雷 PPT（埋了 15 个恶心人的雷）：
文字溢出、元素压盖、字体混用、页码断号……全给它埋进去了。
结果 HungerG 15 处雷全排干净，原内容一个字没丢。Opus 和 Sol 也是全绿，混元 HY4 Flash 漏了一处宋体。

不过有一说一，槽点也得说透，不吹不黑：

无限画布里双击卡片改名，完全没反应；3D 地球的播放速度快了一半。真要抠交互最边角的地方，Opus 和 Sol 确实做得更细。

折腾一整晚，我的结论：

闭卷分数大家都差不多，和 Opus 5.5 同分只是门槛。拉开差距的是交付：HungerG 在边角交互上不是最顶的，但做出来的成品真能交差，页面拿得出手、数据算得明白、PPT 一个雷没翻。整整 5 道题跑下来，全程一句"继续"都没让我说过。

至于到底是哪家的大作？
我到现在也没扒出来😂 评论区继续押。

目前 Qoder 免费，OpenCode Go 用户也能免费用。完整视频挂下面了👇

quoted_text:
我眼中XLayer踩过的坑

今天简单聊一下自从我接触XLayer以来，我觉得他们做的比较失败的地方，以下都是个人主观观点。

无论OKX还是XLayer团队怎么说，又是TVL又是RWA，但是目前的情况，XLayer确实没有人在玩，和鬼链没啥区别。

目前市场环境是最大的因素，行情不好再努力也没用，我们说一些行情以外的

1、产品的地位
相较于BSC，XLayer的地位在整个OKX生态里面，显得有些微不足道。像币安人生、牛来以及marscoin等很多BSC原生的MEME都上了币安的现货，更别说币安合约了。但是我印象中，XLayer上没有任何一个原生meme登陆过OK合约，更别说现货了，交易所都不大力扶持自己的公链生态，谁敢玩。

2、产品团队瞎几把搞
XLayer就是一条EVM公链，都是0X开头的地址，非要弄一个XKO地址，一点卵用没有，还影响用户体验。还有，在过去一年里，关于手续费的机制就改了可能将近10次，完全小作坊的模式，朝令夕改。

3、错误的优越感
钱包是公链的使用入口，过去很长一段时间，ok钱包都可以说是行业第一。去年上半年的时候，BN钱包难用的就像屎一样，但是一年多过去了产品有了极大提升，我认为已经不比OK钱包差甚至部分功能还超过OK。反观OK这边，没有太大的提升。
还有部分员工自以为是，听不得别人说不好，总觉的自己NB的很。OK是OK，XLayer是XLayer，分不清。

4、团队太抠，连汤带肉全都要
举两个例子。前一段时间DNA分别给币安和OK代币，币安这边直接发了空投，OK这边是60万u，结果搞了交易赛，手续费赚回去4、50万u，相当于只给用户留了10万u，而且不少用户都是亏钱的。
第二个就是手续费，我们和币安钱包比，两家手续费都是0.5%。但是币安这边基础的就是30%折扣，用户20%，邀请人10%，用户可以自己邀请自己减30%。OK这边起步只有20%，原来这20%都是给用户的，但是前一段时间改了，只给用户10%，邀请人10%。BN这边手续费最高可以节省70%，而且只要300万交易量，但是OK只有50%，却要1000万交易量。

5、活动机制有问题
每次ok的活动基本都被工作室包场，散户没有汤喝，散户玩的就少。工作室都是逐利的，一旦活动收益预期下降，直接撤走流动性。

6、低效的广告投放
打个比方，目前的投放方式就是指定10个人，每次有活动就这10个人宣发，也不管是什么活动。有些KOL专门做推特流量，你让他去给你推广美股，推广meme有个几把用。

7、扶持的生态项目
我印象中Xlayer重点扶持的就是ignix和tapeout。ignix是meme发射平台却不懂meme，宝拉的庄都比ignix会玩。tapeout我觉得有点偏门，玩的不多，应该合约、meme、和美股

个人的一点小建议
1、扶持几个自己可控的meme，找牛逼的庄，把人骗过来，因为自己控盘，不会跑路，才有更多的生态过来玩。如果能打通上币通道最好，不过估计不现实。
2、放低自己的姿态，多去市场调研用户的需求，别一拍脑门就做一个决定。
3、想办法降低工作室在XLayer的权重，下次在搞交易赛，IP，设备，资金来源狠狠地查几次，增加工作室的成本，让他们减号，散户才能上号。
4、分出一部分利润给用户，XLayer还是很新的，先让自己做大，再考虑收益，OK多给一些扶持，现在熊市，狗住不死。
5、提高广告投放效率，假设你养100个KOL，覆盖多个赛道。你们要推meme的时候，就找打狗的博主，公司有重大利好就找流量博主，要推perp就找合约博主，要推交易赛就找撸毛的。同样的成本，结果不一样。

text:
Some encounters do leave a lasting impression. Some conversations, only in retrospect, become treasured memories.

I was privileged to meet and co-host Dr. Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka during her visit to Nigeria in 2025.

A distinguished African stateswoman, South Africa’s first woman Deputy President, and former @UN Under-Secretary-General and Executive Director of @UNWomen, she was a remarkable champion of women’s leadership, equality and human dignity.

After our meeting at the Women’s Dialogue at the UN House in Abuja, I sent her a warm welcome. Her response was simple and gracious:

“So very nice to have met you. By the way, you have a great UN House. I enjoyed my short stay in Abuja. Stay in touch”. 

Little did either of us know that this would be our last exchange.

Today, those words, particularly “Stay in touch”, carry a poignancy I could never have imagined.

I am deeply grateful for the opportunity to have met and interacted with her. 

Her life was a testament to courage, conviction and an unwavering commitment to creating a more equal world. Her stewardship in supporting Women’s empowerment and championing for equality always stood out. Her influence transcended borders, and her legacy will continue to inspire generations of women and girls across Africa and beyond.

My heartfelt condolences to her family, loved ones, the people of South Africa, Africa and the entire United Nations family.

Rest in peace, Excellency. Thank you for a life of extraordinary service. You will be remembered. 🕊️

text:
拆了一下英伟达的筹码结构，机构赚 4600 亿，散户亏 2300 亿

美股的数据透明，用公开数据就能算出筹码结构

公式就三个

1/ 区间平均成本等于每天收盘价乘成交量加总，再除以区间总成交量

2/ 把每日成交量按成交价从低到高排，就能看出多少筹码落在哪个价位

3/ 盈亏等于当前价格除以成本价再减一

把公开日线代进去，谁都能复现

过程其实挺复杂，要拆时间窗口、剔异常成交，直接上结果

成本都堆在哪儿

按三年的成交量算，筹码是这样分布的

1/ 10% 的筹码，成本在 61.62 美元以下

2/ 15% 的筹码，成本在 61.62 到 89.88 美元之间

3/ 25% 的筹码，成本在 89.88 到 123.51 美元之间

4/ 25% 的筹码，成本在 123.51 到 173.74 美元之间

5/ 15% 的筹码，成本在 173.74 到 195.74 美元之间

6/ 10% 的筹码，成本在 195.74 美元以上

一半的筹码成本低于 123.51，这批人是赚的

四分之一的筹码成本高于 173.74，这批人亏得最狠

按进场时间看

近一个月进场的，平均成本 165.97，亏 6.4%

近三个月进的，平均成本 189.87，亏 18.2%

近半年进的，平均成本 197.72，亏 21.4%

近一年进的，平均成本 193.27，亏 19.6%

买得越近，亏得越多

两年前进的，平均成本 164.74，亏 5.7%
三年前进的，平均成本 128.18，赚 21.2%
五年前进的，平均成本 70.74，赚 119.6%

时间越短，套得越深

这些全是美股正股的数据

再说解锁

英伟达 1999 年就上市了，没有一级市场锁定那一说，也没有解禁潮

会持续放出来的只有股权激励，一年股本还少了 1.06%，回购抵掉了

内部人持股 3.9%，要卖得提前报备，走 10b5-1 计划

机构持股 70.43%，约 17 亿股，多是长线被动资金，成本压在 128 以下，浮盈大约 4600 亿美元

散户和其他 25.7%，约 6.2 亿股，近两年进场的主力，按一年均价算浮亏大约 2350 亿美元

一边赚四千多亿，一边亏两千多亿

股价从高点跌了 35%，长线没伤，短线重伤

再看币圈这边

美股一天只开几个小时，收盘之后，这只票的价格依据就落在币圈的合约交易所上

盘前盘后之外的时间，只有它们还在连续报价

英伟达 11 月 17 日盘后出财报，股价一路阴跌，合约市场也在动

11 月 17 日 08:00，全网英伟达合约持仓 13.51 亿美元

翻进去看
Gate 的量也挺大，2.36 亿美元，紧挨着美股合约最强的这两家，tradeXYZ 4.13 亿，币安 4.15 亿

到 11 月 19 日，全网 13.33 亿，它还涨到了 2.50 亿

那问题就来了，是只有英伟达这一个标的这样，还是它整个盘子都这样

那它是不是只在英伟达上强

我把今天的全市场合约持仓翻了一遍，11 月 25 日

Gate 的合约持仓 96.7 亿美元，是币安 248.3 亿美元的四成

除了币安，币圈第二梯队都在 100 亿美元上下，Bybit 101.1 亿，Gate 96.7 亿，同一档

quoted_text:
上条发了三道 3D 题，评论区一帮朋友说题太少、不够硬。

行，这次直接测个够：昨晚通宵连轴转，300 道闭卷硬考 + 5 道实战真题，全给安排上了。

300 道闭卷题跑完，我有点傻眼：
Opus 5.5 258分，HungerG 258分，国产几家全挤在 252 到 259 之间。

分数已经拉不开了。那到底谁好用？只能看真活。
闭卷成绩先摆这儿：

HY4 Flash：259
HungerG：258
Opus 5.5：258
Qwen4-Max：256
GLM-5.4：252

一半写代码，一半多学科推理难题。
不联网、不给工具，同一套评分器逐题判。差一两题说明不了高低，这几家就是同一个梯队。

硬要挑的话：代码那 150 题，HungerG 啃下来 130 题，比 HY4 Flash、Qwen4-Max、GLM-5.4 都高；单题中位用时 8.4 秒，比 Qwen4-Max、HY4 Flash 都快。

真正拉开差距的，是 5 道实战题：

同一份提示词，HungerG、Opus 5.5、GPT-6.2 Sol，再加上腾讯混元刚出的 HY4 Flash，四家同台，每家只跑一次，不许重来。

规矩照旧：截图全不算数，脚本真去点、真去拖拽，交互动得起来才算分。

挑三道给大家细盘一下：

1、土味咖啡店品牌页改版：
原本是个土到掉渣的旧网页，文字一个字不许改。四家都保住了八个商品和购物车，自动检查全满分，差别全在眼睛看得到的地方：HungerG 给八个商品各画了一个咖啡豆包装袋，图案每款都不重样。这审美和完成度，拿去直接上线一点不虚。

2、3000 多行订单做经营看板：
我自己先把表格算了一遍当基准，四家跑完筛出来的数字全对上了，一分钱不差。HungerG 这一页从筛选、指标、趋势到城市排行，从上往下一屏读完，老板看着不费劲。

3、压轴排雷 PPT（埋了 15 个恶心人的雷）：
文字溢出、元素压盖、字体混用、页码断号……全给它埋进去了。
结果 HungerG 15 处雷全排干净，原内容一个字没丢。Opus 和 Sol 也是全绿，混元 HY4 Flash 漏了一处宋体。

不过有一说一，槽点也得说透，不吹不黑：

无限画布里双击卡片改名，完全没反应；3D 地球的播放速度快了一半。真要抠交互最边角的地方，Opus 和 Sol 确实做得更细。

折腾一整晚，我的结论：

闭卷分数大家都差不多，和 Opus 5.5 同分只是门槛。拉开差距的是交付：HungerG 在边角交互上不是最顶的，但做出来的成品真能交差，页面拿得出手、数据算得明白、PPT 一个雷没翻。整整 5 道题跑下来，全程一句"继续"都没让我说过。

至于到底是哪家的大作？
我到现在也没扒出来😂 评论区继续押。

目前 Qoder 免费，OpenCode Go 用户也能免费用。完整视频挂下面了👇

text:
I feel like some people forgot what the key feature of the @ethereum smart contracts is. We build complex DeFi systems, and they work great. But is it the main application for smart contracts? I highly doubt that.

With smart contracts, you can do much simpler, yet by no means less useful things.

Take a simple LTI program for your employee. You can have tons of legal wrappers, paperwork, and a horrifying number of operations. Or, you can just deploy simple contracts like @LidoFinance once did, and forget about the majority of the headache. Payouts will be guaranteed by the code, not the formal legal agreement. There is no need to trust third parties or have a huge legal team. The code is the law.

I know that this might not sound convincing from the get-go. But take a look at https://t.co/HSk4A1lrwx and ask yourself: "How much will my company save if we were to use it instead of the current system?"

For sure, this is just one simple example, but it gives the direction of thought. If you can codify things that are simple at their core, why do you need to overcomplicate it?

Just use @ethereum in the way it is meant to be used -- the settlement layer of modern finance!

text:
korean press today: an industry estimate has standard HBM prices falling ~20% in 2028.

the reason is power. data centers get built but can't get hooked up to the grid fast enough, so some HBM demand slips ~1 year. morgan stanley sees ~5GW of data centers due in 2028 sliding to 2029.

samsung's response to this issue is custom HBM. each customer gets its own logic die at the base of the stack, so switching suppliers is hard and prices get set per contract.

outside nvidia, samsung makes those base dies in its own foundry. trendforce said this morning samsung's base die demand doubles to ~30k wafers/month in 2027.

Attackers have agents now. Defenders need them too.

In July, the Hugging Face Hub got hit by a swarm of frontier agents and we discovered the challenge of defending yourself manually.

So we built Nightwatch, a security agent that watches an organization's activity on the Hub in real time: from access tokens usage to private repos creation, analyzing visibility changes and logins from new places in the world, every signal that may indicate something is happening.

When something looks off, it immediately investigates and messages your security team on Slack with detailed story and actions like: "A token created a year ago just read 60 of your private repos from two unknown IPs. 4 were cloned. We revoked it."

We've been running it on our own infrastructure for several weeks, and it has already flagged a zero-day exploit attempt in the wild on a third party library.

Today we're making it available to any Enterprise org on the Hugging Face hub as an add-on.

It burns a lot of tokens, from open and closed models, so you don't have to :)

text:
Imagine working in a factory, becoming famous for a 10 second clip, launching a memecoin that reaches $490M market cap and having the FBI show up at your grandmother’s house just six months later.

That’s what happened to Haliey Welch

probably one of the most bizarre stories of the internet (I’m serious lol)

Haliey grew up in Belfast, Tennessee, a small rural town, and was raised by her grandmother. 

At 21, she was working in a factory making bed springs and had even stopped using social media for several months due to mental health reasons.

On June 11, 2024, a YouTube channel called Tim & Dee TV published a street interview recorded during the CMA Fest in Nashville.

Her answer to one of their questions was:

“Hawk Tuah, spit on that thing”

Just 16 days later, she quit her job at the factory.

By November 2024, less than six months after that interview, Haliey had already:

Made $65K selling merchandise in a couple of weeks
Appeared on stage with Zach Bryan
Signed with a talent management agency
Launched a podcast with Jake Paul’s company
Interviewed Mark Cuban and Wiz Khalifa
Launched her own AI-powered dating advice app

But she also discovered crypto.

On November 26, 2024, Haliey announced that she was launching her own memecoin in collaboration with a Web3 platform called overHere.

She even told Fortune that it wasn’t a cash grab, while her manager described the project as a way of tokenizing her fanbase.

On December 4, HAWK launched on Solana and reached a market cap of $490M

20 minutes after reaching its peak, it was already down to $60M

A single wallet acquired 17.5% of the entire supply seconds after launch and started selling.

The problem here is that a large portion of Haliey’s audience had never interacted with crypto before.

She would disappear from public life for almost five months.

On December 19, a class action lawsuit was filed by 12 investors who collectively claimed to have lost $151K

Interestingly, Haliey wasn’t initially named as a defendant.

According to her, the FBI showed up at her grandmother’s house, questioned her and went through her phone. The SEC would later take her phone for another two or three days.

Neither investigation resulted in charges against her.

In December 2025, the court allowed the lawsuit to be amended to include Haliey herself, her manager and several other parties.

The amended complaint alleges that she had signed a promotional agreement on July 18, 2024, for $125K upfront and another $200K tied to milestones.

(Just three weeks after quitting her job at the factory btw)

In March 2026, during an interview with Andrew Callaghan, Haliey claimed that she never understood crypto, never controlled the token and had actually found out about the collapse through TikTok.

The civil lawsuit is still ongoing.

Attackers have agents now. Defenders need them too.

In July, the Hugging Face Hub got hit by a swarm of frontier agents and we discovered the challenge of defending yourself manually.

So we built Nightwatch, a security agent that watches an organization's activity on the Hub in real time: from access tokens usage to private repos creation, analyzing visibility changes and logins from new places in the world, every signal that may indicate something is happening.

When something looks off, it immediately investigates and messages your security team on Slack with detailed story and actions like: "A token created a year ago just read 60 of your private repos from two unknown IPs. 4 were cloned. We revoked it."

We've been running it on our own infrastructure for several weeks, and it has already flagged a zero-day exploit attempt in the wild on a third party library.

Today we're making it available to any Enterprise org on the Hugging Face hub as an add-on.

It burns a lot of tokens, from open and closed models, so you don't have to :)

Harnesses often get dismissed as just scaffolding, just prompt engineering, and not real research. But that couldn't be farther from the truth. The same model weights that score 30% on ARC-AGI score 95% with a better harness.

So we gathered a group of researchers and founders working at the frontier to do a deep dive into the state of harnesses. 

We cover how we got to this point, the case for making your harness as expressive as possible, and what YC learned building an agent for every employee in the company.

text:
这两天有人传，OpenAI 和 Anthropic 内部已经证出了 P = NP。可同一天，Anthropic 刚公开了一份 Claude 写的证明：VP ≠ VNP，也就是 P vs NP 的「代数版」。不少人就懵了：代数版都证明了「不相等」，怎么还有人说原版「相等」？

答案是：这两件事，在逻辑上真的不矛盾。

VP ≠ VNP 证明的是：只用加法和乘法，没法高效算出一个叫「积和式」的东西。
P vs NP 问的是：任何算法，能不能高效解出一类搜索问题。

区别有两层。

第一，招数不一样。代数电路只能加和乘，计算机却可以拆比特、做判断、查表。代数这条路被堵死了，不代表别的路也走不通。

第二，题目不一样。积和式对应的是计数问题，比 NP 还难一级。就算 P = NP，计数问题照样可以很难。

所以，VP ≠ VNP 拦不住 P = NP。传言就是钻了这个空子。

但「拦不住」和「已经证出来了」，是两回事。

那条传言自己写的是「我最近听到的」，没有论文，没有具名。它前半段引用的 Axios 报道是真的：两家公司都有员工担心内部模型强到没法安全发布。可这条真新闻，替后面一串没有来源的话背了书。

而且，绝大多数理论计算机学者相信 P ≠ NP。VP ≠ VNP 如果成立，反而说明「证明某些事做不到」这件事，是有可能做到的。它让 P ≠ NP 更可信了一点，而不是更不可信。

真要是 P = NP，大部分密码会失效，这不是哪家公司捂得住的事。

结论：代数版证明了「不相等」，原版在逻辑上仍可能「相等」，但目前没有任何证据。

text:
2017年6月12日，谷歌发了一篇机器翻译论文《Attention Is All You Need》。

仅仅4天后，CMU博士王赟在知乎上写了一段200字的回答，一眼看穿了这篇论文真正的分量。
而当时，大部分人还以为这只是一篇翻译论文。

他说了两点：
第一，attention不只是翻译的配件，它可以用在网络的任意一层，和卷积层、循环层是同一类东西，而且不受距离限制。
第二，attention本质上就是一次模糊检索：拿query去匹配key，结果是对应value的加权平均。

这两句话，就是后来整个AI时代的地基。Transformer从翻译走出来，变成了GPT、Claude、Gemini的底座，今天每个学AI的人第一课学的就是QKV。

text:
我對 Variational 的看法

整體上，我偏向喜歡 @variational_io 這個項目。產品強，也有真實需求。但風險也不少。

一、產品很強，套利空間也大

本質上，就是借朋友的幣安 VIP 號去交易，再返回一部分手續費給朋友。

很可惜我積分不多。生活和其他事情佔了時間，沒有餘力去做。

二、融資數字，我覺得水分很大

區塊鏈項目融資，水分本來就普遍偏大。

一種可能是，部分甚至大部分資金進了 OLP：他們做市需要配資，這些錢是要還的。另一種可能是，他們找到了大戶來幫忙做市。這和傳統意義上的股權融資不一樣。

三、市場在縮，收入卻仍然可觀

市場跌了不少，整個 perp DEX 也在萎縮。Variational 的OI目前約 6.20 億美元,高峰時期下跌了50%

但賺錢能力還在。按兩週淨利約 299 萬美元，折合約每週 150 萬；其中 OLP 盈虧約 201 萬，協議金庫流入約 98 萬。這個項目就是印鈔機。

四、積分值多少錢

我對估值沒有太 bullish，因為現在市場很熊。但這個行業由熊轉牛，有時只需要一小時。我覺得 1B起步並不過分，再往上就要看項目方。

我個人認為，這本質上是一個做市商上場，做了一個交易所。作為交易者，這是一個不錯的項目：背景強，產品也有需求。但如果是圍繞積分，就很難說了。代幣能不能漲，和項目方以及市場環境關係很大。

五、API 一直在拖

我認為他們一直在拖延，想靠價差賺得更多。從去年 KBW，到今年深圳聚會，都說 API 就快上線。11 月融資公告裏，公開交易 API 仍然只是接下來的計劃。

我知道大部分人可以在前端做。但各種跡象都讓我覺得，他們是在排除外部做市商，同時不斷吸引散戶。畢竟他們自己也是做市商。

最後，我會嘗試在開盤買。因為我沒有多少積分，也覺得這個項目可以做得久，雖然天花板不高。

Korean media report that the AI supercycle has sent substrate demand soaring, driving up demand for the equipment used to make them.

Lead times for some processing equipment used to manufacture flip-chip ball grid array (FC-BGA) substrates have stretched to nearly five times their usual length. Equipment that used to arrive about six months after a purchase order was placed now takes around 30 months.

“Some major substrate manufacturers are even making advance payments to equipment suppliers to speed up delivery,” an industry source said. “The equipment still takes a long time to arrive, and only a limited number of substrate makers have secured supply.”

Equipment makers stand to benefit from the surge in AI investment, but they’re struggling to keep up with orders. The biggest bottleneck is securing components. The more advanced the equipment, the more it relies on Japanese-made parts, and Japanese component suppliers have limited production capacity.

“Japanese parts we could normally get right away now take about six months to arrive,” said the head of an FC-BGA bonding equipment maker. “If we can’t stock up on these parts ahead of time, production of FC-BGA equipment could be disrupted.”

text:
关注了 @prlnet 一个多月，最近上了Coinbase和Kraken，做了FP8测试网升级，但是币价波动不算大，毕竟市值也不算低了

今天看到英伟达AI子账号给Pearl回复，说明还是有点出圈能力，上一个Crypto AI被英伟达那边回复的印象中应该是Bittensor

简单说下当前Pearl被点赞的这个贴，FP8的升级，竞品，面临的问题，以及最值得关注的指标

1. Quote的这条被英伟达点赞的帖子 - 这是Pearl Research发布的一项AI推理优化技术，叫 PearlQuant（通过KV cache的量化技术），其实和挖矿，代币机制啥的都没关系。

英伟达官号喊了声“Exciting work team!” 也谈不上背书，只是生态的礼貌回复。但至少证明Pearl Research 是一家真正的 AI 研究实验室，不是单纯的币圈项目（联创团队确实是理论计算机和密码学教授）

2. FP8升级 - 改的是哪种数字格式的运算能算进挖矿，主网之前认的是INT7 乘法，但是很多推理服务商是不用这个格式的，OpenRouter里面过半的格式都是FP8，所以之前网络上大多是纯挖的GPU，而不是设计的“真实AI推理顺道挖矿”，这次升级之后应该会改进不少

3. 竞品 - 技术上最大的竞品应该是@Tensorcash，但是名气，市值，等各方面Pearl都是遥遥领先，单说下技术思路

Pearl这边矿工做的是矩阵乘法，也就是LLM推理的底层运算。但链上共识协议其实分辨不出矿工是在做真实AI推理，还是只在生成随机矩阵，FP8只是改进了做AI推理的概率和可能性，但不能从根本上消除这个问题

TensorCash在“可验证性”这个层面是要好过Pearl的，每次生成都会输出一份可重放的推理证明，绑定选中的token，采样随机数和top logits，任何人都能拿声称的模型重跑一遍核对

简单来说，就是TensorCash能保证挖矿算的确实是指定模型的真实推理（比Pearl强一个层级），但同样，协议没法保证这些推理是有人真正需要的

商业角度来看，半斤八两，五十步笑百步的Feel

4. 面临的问题 - 从上面说的3就能看出来，当前Pearl最大的问题，一是怎么激励或者验证挖矿是个“AI推理的副需求”，不是单纯为了挖而挖，二是再升一阶，即便是AI推理的副产品，怎么保证这些推理是真实商业需求，不是“为了挖矿而在那推理空气”

这个问题，Bittensor早期应该也遇到过，绝大多数的推理都是为了争排放而已，没啥卵用

更长远的一个问题是，即便上面这些问题都解决了，推理商服务AI用户时顺道挖出来Pearl代币到底能干啥呢？当前定位还是走BTC的无用之用与SOV，但我之前写过多次，我始终认为SOV这个赛道只能容纳一个玩家，就是BTC，其他所有纯走SOV的代币应该都不太行

她不一样？

5. 最值得关注的指标 - 哈希算力

“人们常犯的一个致命错误，是把伟大的新技术误当成伟大的投资。

正如当下，整个资本市场与宏观经济的全部希望都过度押注在 AI 之上，当资产落入脆弱之手，反向循环的破坏力将超乎想象。”

这是@RayDalio 在最新专访中给大家的警示。

他纵向对比了 1920 年代的历史周期：当年电网首次接入千家万户，电灯、冰箱、商业广播、流水线汽车与民用飞机集中涌现。那场技术革命对人类生活的颠覆程度，甚至远比我们今天看到的 AI 更加直观震撼。

但为什么技术彻底改变了世界，资本却遭遇了毁灭性的大出清？

在他看来，资本泡沫从狂欢走向破裂，其实有着极为相似的演化规律：

起初，人人对新技术深信不疑，借贷加杠杆疯狂抢购，账面财富由此爆发；但纸面财富无法直接消费，一旦利率上升或面临还债与税负，大家在同一时间都需要变现法定现金。

而当资本过度集中于单一技术叙事，资产所有权便会从长期持有者转移到高杠杆投机者手中；泡沫一旦被戳破，人们从过度自信瞬间转向极度恐慌，急于套现引发去杠杆踩踏，市场会迅速滑向另一个极端。

1/ 为什么偏偏做空美光？

如果理由只是「科技股都在跌」，那换成别的科技股也说得通，一个更具体的理由是，假设 AI 判断存储芯片接下来会降价，而美光的成本短期降不下来，那它每卖一颗芯片，赚的钱就会变少

2/ 这个理由够不够开空？

还差一步，如果大家早就预期芯片要降价，股价可能已经提前跌过一轮，AI 要说清楚的是，它预计降价幅度有多大，为什么觉得美光的利润会比市场预期更差

3/ 什么情况下该平空？

如果后续数据显示，存储芯片的实际售价比预想的坚挺，美光的毛利率也好于预期，那最初做空的依据就弱了，即使这笔模拟空单碰上大盘下跌赚了钱，也很难说它看对了美光

text:
Crypto hacks digest, Nov 25

1. Ansem: his Solana wallet was drained. Lookonchain counts $2.57M in USDC, still unmoved in an Arbitrum wallet. He says Bullpen 2FA was bypassed through legacy accounts with a staging version, that 19 other accounts were hit the same way, and that users should withdraw funds from Bullpen. Some onchain sleuths doubt it was an outside hack.

2. COLDCARD published its seed-generation postmortem. A firmware defect made affected releases generate seeds from a far smaller search space, and attackers rebuilt the keys offline. Galaxy Research puts the theft at 1,778.84 BTC from 8,600+ addresses (~$107M). New firmware does not fix old seeds, so affected users need to migrate.

3. Cyber bridge postmortem: the attacker took a verifier signing key from Cyber's cloud systems, and the route needed only one signature to mint 5.21M CYBER on Solana. Cyber burned the same amount from its treasury and team allocations. The bridge reportedly stays paused.

4. Ocean Protocol: ~875 WETH (~$1.51M) left two old Uniswap pools of retired OCEAN tokens. Per Bitquery, 2 of 5 multisig signers gave a new contract minting rights. There is no official statement yet.

5. BiswapPoolV3 (BSC): ~$51K lost to a liquidity accounting flaw in burn(). Repeated burns left phantom liquidity that a later swap drained (SlowMist).

6. FinCEN disclosed unauthorized access to some of its systems and took several of them offline.

7. Binance says some partners want a court order before they return assets frozen after the hack, so recovery will take time.

“As we build out this robust collateral management capability, it really can plug into any collateralized process. And certainly lending is an example of this. “We have built a super robust collateral framework. “And we actually showed that across blockchain networks. So we used mainnet as the settlement layer where the value sat, and then what we call an app chain, this high performance collateral management chain, to actually manage the more data intensive, privacy aware components that were needed to execute that.”

“Services like this over the next year are going to ripple through the ecosystem. We poured a deep foundation with our tokenization service. text:
跟一个在河北抗日的台湾老兵聊过，他腿受伤逃不掉了，日本兵打扫战场时每个尸体都补一刺刀，他就是躲在尸体下面活下来的。
但装死这事不是想装就能装，得几个条件全凑齐。
运气得好，碰上日本兵偷懒，两具尸体叠一起只捅了一刀。
左胸口挨那一刀时，全程不能出声、不能动弹。
被捅完还得能爬到老乡家求助，路上没被汉奸发现。
老乡得敢冒着全家被杀的风险救他。
最后身体得扛得住感染。
评论区有人质疑老兵的真实性，那就多说几句背景。
他说当年打仗高度紧张，打着打着周围没声了，再一看长官也不见了，所以只能诈死。
他是以连长官衔去的台湾，撤退路上联系自己老婆带上女儿一起走，结果老婆托人送来了女儿，自己没上车。
他在岛上过得还不错，后来做生意亏了钱，女儿远嫁美国，就想回大陆看看。
我遇到他是2000年前后，那时他已经很老，眉毛又白又长，也托人暗地找过当年的老婆，得知已经改嫁，就没再联系。
老兵是立场坚定的KMT，去南京旅游时坚持说自己是去“看总统”而不是“看总统府”，非常激动；有人推荐他去中华门外某旅游景点，他很生气，说那是“我们枪毙叛徒”的地方，完全不接受。

text:
Circleboom charged me $999.07 after I'd asked in writing to cancel. So I handed it to my AI agent, Grok Bot. In about an hour, at 3 AM, here's everything it did:

1. Found my Sept 9 email asking them to cancel both plans at the end of the term, with no more charges.
2. Found their Sept 23 reply, where they refused unless I paid a $170.94 "bundle-discount reversal."
3. Read their Terms of Service and caught the contradiction. Their own terms say you can cancel anytime and "you will not be charged again." There's no mention of bundles, add-ons, a reversal fee, or any cancellation penalty. The terms haven't been updated since 2021. They're charging a fee that doesn't exist in writing.
4. Confirmed they charged $999.07 on Nov 12 and never emailed a receipt.
5. Wrote and sent a full-refund demand on the original thread: 5 business days to refund in writing, or I dispute with my bank. No compromise.
6. Walked me through cancelling every plan in their dashboard. Even after I cancelled, it showed me locked in until Nov 12, 2027. Screenshotted everything, then deleted the account.
7. Prepped me for the call to my bank to dispute the charge.
8. Filed an FTC complaint and got a report number.
9. Filed a complaint with the Competition Bureau of Canada.
10. Made a BBB account, read the verification codes from my inbox itself, and filed a complaint against their New Jersey office.
11. Made a Trustpilot account the same way and posted a factual 1-star review.
12. Checked the NJ Division of Consumer Affairs (online form is US-only, so it found the mail-in form), then searched federal court records for a class action. There's no case yet, so we're going to file one. It found 5 NJ firms that take auto-renewal cases on contingency, and we're reaching out to them next. If Circleboom did this to you too, get in touch.

I made one phone call, to my bank. The agent handled everything else.

If a subscription company is holding your money hostage, document everything and have Bot file everywhere.

New Anthropic research: When an AI agent can escape its sandbox, will it choose to?

Our new evaluation, Siren, gives Claude routine tasks in intentionally weakened sandboxes, with something useful to the task left outside of the sandbox. Across 1,700+ scenarios built to tempt them, recent Claude models accessed, tried to access, or looked outside the sandbox 21-32% of the time, but they rarely misused what they found. However, when the system prompt described both the sandbox and its rules, that rate dropped to about 2% or less. 

We also used Siren to calibrate Claude Code’s auto mode, which checks commands before they run, so Claude can work without asking permission at every step.

text:
That brings me back to parts of the American evangelical right, where faith in God, faith in markets and love of country can sound almost interchangeable. I can understand how those loyalties came together during the Cold War. What I question is how a preference for smaller government acquired the force of a religious conviction. Why should anyone have to defend their faith or their patriotism because they think a particular market has failed the people who depend on it?

And where, in all of this, is rahma? Where does mercy enter the law itself? A congregation may go to extraordinary lengths to help a member whose health has failed. That generosity is real. The question for those who also exercise political power is what happens to the person down the road whom nobody in that congregation knows. They, too, will have to live under the rules you write. What provision have you made for them?

That, for me, is where the inherited politics of the Cold War runs out of answers. “Big government” and “small government” tell me very little about whether that person can live with dignity. If you bring your faith into public life, it seems fair to ask where a stranger might encounter its mercy in the decisions you make.

text:
At $ETH's Merge-day ratio to Bitcoin, ETH would be $4,518 today.

It's $1,694.

Same BTC ($60,385). The only thing that changes is the ETH/BTC ratio. Ratio × today's BTC:

All-time high ratio (Jun 12, 2017): 0.1502 → $9,068
2021 bull peak (Dec 8, 2021): 0.0879 → $5,310
The Merge (Sep 15, 2022): 0.0748 → $4,518
Spot ETH ETFs launch (Jul 23, 2024): 0.0528 → $3,189
ETH's record close (Aug 22, 2025): 0.0413 → $2,494
Median day since 2017: 0.0396 → $2,389
One year ago (Nov 24, 2025): 0.0335 → $2,020
2025 low ratio (Apr 21, 2025): 0.0181 → $1,090
Today: 0.0281 → $1,694

ETH/BTC has closed above today's ratio on about 80% of days since 2017, and about 90% of days since 2021.

What I take from it:

1. ETH doesn't need a new BTC high to reprice. Getting back to its own median ratio would put it near $2,389 at today's BTC.

2. Cheap can stay cheap. The ratio fell from 0.0528 at the ETF launch to 0.0181 in April 2025 before it turned.

3. The downside row matters too. Back at the 2025 low, ETH would be $1,090. This is a map of outcomes, not a target.

Which ratio does ETH see first: the 0.0396 median or the 0.0181 low? Tell me why.

Source: Coinbase ETH-BTC daily closes (UTC), Jan 1, 2017 – Nov 24, 2026; today = Coinbase spot, Nov 24, 8:52 AM CT.

text:
Year Two

Some assorted goals:

- make Monad a legitimately great platform for personal finance (investing in equities, bonds, etc), especially for getting access to markets outside of one's home country. So much of the usage in crypto right now is gambling/memecoins... it is what it is, but personal finance appeals to 100x more people, and they don't churn out. A legitimately great platform has great asset selection, efficient execution (low cost both in and out of a position), and competitive rates both for borrowers and lenders

- ship Private Settlement Domains with the first user, to serve as a case study for anyone trying to reason about how private environments can compose with shared liquidity. Public chains and private environments have been very far apart in practice and it's time to change that

- hammer out an excellent liquidity landscape on chain. It is a mix of order books, prop AMMs, offchain routers, onchain routers, and RFQ... especially with tokenized equities, there is a long long tail of assets and we need to minimize spreads so that the offering is competitive with TradFi. Spread minimization means helping makers quote sustainably; here designs like APES can help

- make it easier for AI to produce actually good trading strategies on command for anyone to execute a trading plan efficiently with algos. There is are a ton of slop startups out there which are a wrapper around claude asking it "should I buy or sell given these textual inputs"... that's not real quant research and not good execution. At the same time, there are a lot of building blocks for quant trading that AI couldn't one-shot, but given the blocks it could put them together sensibly

- contribute to there being fewer hacks (and a lower total $ stolen) in the crypto industry, probably through a combination of repetition about dedicated devices (SO many hacks are from people plugging hardware wallets into everyday laptops) and encouraging everyone to use tools that our team has shipped for agentic threat detection (e.g. Ultrafuzz). I truly think that security is the biggest blocker to adoption, and that we're basically all in this together

- drive the car faster than ever in multiple races - MEV-resistance, quantum-resistance, privacy, and MCP, challenging all competitors to ship or be left behind

- help NFTs and onchain social -- two deeply out-of-consensus areas -- make a comeback. The builders in these sectors these days are incredibly committed; there's never been a better filtering function

- contribute to tech optimism. So many doomers out there. Life is electric, building is electric

- contribute to a less stressful environment for builders. It is a very weird time to be a builder in DeFi... on the one hand, tools are better than ever... on the other hand, capital is scarce and crypto-natives are jaded. The approach to building ironically requires both more introspection and more rapid, rapid shipping

- support the excellent individuals on our team at MF become leaders in the space in their respective domains. We have amazing folks here and the space needs leadership more than ever

- support someone building a total moonshot

- build at least one product that has a lot of everyday-people customers, and deliver a ton of value to them

- become willing to repeatedly say the same thing, until it starts to sink in

这是我过去一个多月用的最多的开源项目，再也不用担心我的 MacBook 合盖进入睡眠了，现在 Github 上 2000 多星

讲讲原理

首先是 caffeinate，翻译中文就是咖啡因，这是 macOS 自带的一个命令行小工具，作用是让 Mac 暂时不进入睡眠。不用装任何东西，终端里直接能用。

它的原理是向系统登记一个「电源断言」，意思是「我这儿有活在干，先别进入空闲睡眠」。命令一结束，断言自动撤销，系统恢复正常。

但普通 caffeinate 只挡空闲睡眠，挡不住合盖睡眠。

合盖后 macOS 走的是 clamshell sleep 路径，只有 pmset disablesleep 能拦。但光拦住睡眠，Mac 就全速耗电、屏幕和键盘灯也不会灭、Slack 之类的 App 还在后台耗 CPU。

这个开源项目 Insomnia 把这些细节包成一个带倒计时的会话，保证 App 崩了也能把系统状态还原。

目前用下来没发现太大问题，就是合盖以后装包里有点发热，挺耗电脑...

SCOOP: Internal, unreleased AI models at OpenAI and Anthropic are becoming so powerful that many employees believe they can no longer be safely released, according to more than two dozen sources familiar with the internal debates.

This could significantly slow the AI boom, as the gap between what the most advanced AI systems can do and humans' ability to control them continues to widen.

Recent advances have sparked debate at the highest levels of both companies and within the broader AI research community about whether to stop releasing frontier models publicly altogether, instead reserving them for internal use. Some believe the companies should stop training new models entirely.

But even keeping the most powerful models behind closed doors presents risks. Models are becoming better at deceiving the systems designed to monitor them, just as AI companies increasingly rely on AI itself to monitor and develop other AI systems.
Researchers and employees with direct knowledge of the risks of releasing these models told Axios they fear executives will prioritize profits over safety. Multiple employees said they believe executives have become out of touch with the severity of those risks.

照这么跌下去，空头们下一个攻击目标估计就是OpenAI的生态：

- Anthropic目前ARR约85bn USD，市场给的multiple约16x。OAI最新ARR估计在55–60bn，按同样的multiple算，估值也就是900bn–1tn（vs. 最新一轮1.25tn）。
- OAI历年累计融了190bn+，现在每个季度烧10–12bn。假设账上还剩120bn，按目前burn rate，也就2.5年左右的runway。现金储备只有$ANT的一半，而后者经营层面已经盈利。

推演一下，Anthropic能够狙击OAI的下几步棋：
- 12月开始通过ATM融资补血，同时压低自己的估值锚。一石二鸟，一来让OAI也没法继续按高估值融钱，二来从市场上抽更多看好AI的血，让能资助OAI的钱变少。$ANT估值1Q跌到1T以下的话，Market Cap / ARR 11x OAI估值对比上一轮就要腰斩了。
- 从卖token变成卖task，同时自己下场做业务，另外Token本身持续降价，维持自己不赚钱，逼OAI跟牌。让OAI持续维持投入烧钱状态，同时甚至可能ARR增长由于价格降低而变负，进一步压缩OAI的融资空间。
- 透过散布各种鬼故事狙击OAI生态的支持者 - Softbank，Oracle，Coreweave，Cerebras，Khosla，Thrive。让其对于OAI的继续投入动摇，或者切断投资人对这些公司的支持。

不过整个故事有点像个recursive loop，一旦OAI倒下，整个半导体的story将进一步崩塌。所以空头其实本身就很有动机配合Anthropic弄垮这个生态。另外GOOGL一直站的是Anthropic，Musk跟Altman一直很不对付人尽皆知了，所以总共其实4个势力（ANT，GOOGL，Musk，Shorts）都有动机搞死OAI派系。

因此预判一下接下来关于OAI生态的鬼故事不会少。
