quoted_text:
Year Two

Some assorted goals:

- make Monad a legitimately great platform for personal finance (investing in equities, bonds, etc), especially for getting access to markets outside of one's home country. So much of the usage in crypto right now is gambling/memecoins... it is what it is, but personal finance appeals to 100x more people, and they don't churn out. A legitimately great platform has great asset selection, efficient execution (low cost both in and out of a position), and competitive rates both for borrowers and lenders

- ship Private Settlement Domains with the first user, to serve as a case study for anyone trying to reason about how private environments can compose with shared liquidity. Public chains and private environments have been very far apart in practice and it's time to change that

- hammer out an excellent liquidity landscape on chain. It is a mix of order books, prop AMMs, offchain routers, onchain routers, and RFQ... especially with tokenized equities, there is a long long tail of assets and we need to minimize spreads so that the offering is competitive with TradFi. Spread minimization means helping makers quote sustainably; here designs like APES can help

- make it easier for AI to produce actually good trading strategies on command for anyone to execute a trading plan efficiently with algos. There is are a ton of slop startups out there which are a wrapper around claude asking it "should I buy or sell given these textual inputs"... that's not real quant research and not good execution. At the same time, there are a lot of building blocks for quant trading that AI couldn't one-shot, but given the blocks it could put them together sensibly

- contribute to there being fewer hacks (and a lower total $ stolen) in the crypto industry, probably through a combination of repetition about dedicated devices (SO many hacks are from people plugging hardware wallets into everyday laptops) and encouraging everyone to use tools that our team has shipped for agentic threat detection (e.g. Ultrafuzz). I truly think that security is the biggest blocker to adoption, and that we're basically all in this together

- drive the car faster than ever in multiple races - MEV-resistance, quantum-resistance, privacy, and MCP, challenging all competitors to ship or be left behind

- help NFTs and onchain social -- two deeply out-of-consensus areas -- make a comeback. The builders in these sectors these days are incredibly committed; there's never been a better filtering function

- contribute to tech optimism. So many doomers out there. Life is electric, building is electric

- contribute to a less stressful environment for builders. It is a very weird time to be a builder in DeFi... on the one hand, tools are better than ever... on the other hand, capital is scarce and crypto-natives are jaded. The approach to building ironically requires both more introspection and more rapid, rapid shipping

- support the excellent individuals on our team at MF become leaders in the space in their respective domains. We have amazing folks here and the space needs leadership more than ever

- support someone building a total moonshot

- build at least one product that has a lot of everyday-people customers, and deliver a ton of value to them

- become willing to repeatedly say the same thing, until it starts to sink in

text:
Why Ran Neuner Believes Crypto Is Entering Its First Real Bull Market, and What’s Next

In this episode of When Shift Happens, I sit down with @cryptomanran, founder of @crypto_banter, one of crypto's largest media platforms with over 1.5 million YouTube subscribers, to discuss why he believes we're entering crypto's first real bull market. We explore the lessons he's learned from multiple market cycles, why traditional approaches to valuing tokens may be missing something important, and where he sees the biggest investment opportunities emerging.

The Cost of Learning Through Market Cycles

Ran has spent more than a decade in crypto, building a career that combines investing, media, and entrepreneurship. Before entering the industry, he sold a business for more than $150 million, and his early work covering crypto on CNBC gave him exclusive access to founders and investors. That access ultimately influenced his decision to launch CryptoBanter. He realized that being in media meant constantly learning from people building the industry, giving him information that could inform his investments.

But access to information didn't prevent him from making costly mistakes. Across two market cycles, Ran watched significant paper gains disappear as prices collapsed, and he also started questioning the time he'd sacrificed chasing those returns. "There were a lot of weekends where I actually stayed in front of my computer instead of going outside and spending time with the family," he recalls.

After experiencing the same pattern twice, his perspective changed. He began prioritizing experiences with his family and recognizing that another investment opportunity would almost always come along. His biggest lesson was simple: "No FOMO."
Rather than trying to capture every last percentage of upside, Ran has become more comfortable taking profits, holding cash, and diversifying outside crypto.

Why Ran Believes This Bull Market Is Different

Ran compares previous crypto cycles to the dot-com boom, when investors poured money into internet companies based largely on their potential. Many companies disappeared, but the internet eventually produced businesses with real customers, revenue, and lasting economic value.

Ran sees a similar transition happening in crypto. For years, the industry's clearest practical achievements were Bitcoin and stablecoins, which enabled people to hold and transfer digital value, while other innovations attracted enormous capital without delivering sustainable businesses.
"For the first time, crypto has found product-market fit," he says.

He believes the difference today is the emergence of applications that people actively use, particularly trading platforms generating meaningful revenue. For investors, that changes the question from which technology has the most exciting potential to which businesses can capture economic activity and return value to token holders.

Rethinking How Tokens Should Be Valued

One of the conversation's most interesting discussions centers on token valuation. Traditional company valuations often consider earnings and the multiple investors are willing to pay for them, while crypto investors typically compare projects using fully diluted valuation.

Ran argues that both approaches don't fully capture how token networks work, and uses a pipe analogy to explain his reasoning. Imagine a pipe representing the tokens available in a network, with mechanisms like staking and token lockups narrowing the pipe by reducing the circulating supply, while demand from users and automatic token buybacks create pressure inside it.

"The way to value a token is the pressure in the pipe," he explains.

His preferred example is Hyperliquid, which has three important characteristics of a successful token network: strong network effects, mechanisms that limit available supply, and recurring buying pressure. Another essential consideration is whether the platform generates revenue and has a credible way to return that value to token holders.

The distinction matters because a successful application doesn't automatically translate to a successful token, and investors must still evaluate whether the underlying business growth creates demand for the asset itself.

Why Trading Applications Could Capture the Biggest Opportunity

Ran believes that most of the competition among major layer-one networks has already played out, with Ethereum's layer-two ecosystem and Solana occupying important positions. Instead, he is moving towards the applications built on those networks.

"The most important investments in this cycle are the trading venues," he says. Platforms such as Hyperliquid and Uniswap fit that thesis because they facilitate the exchange of digital value and can generate revenue from that activity. Ran also sees an emerging opportunity in social trading, which he describes as a combination of the world's biggest social media network and its biggest casino.

Unlike traditional trading, social trading allows participants to share their performance, receive recognition, and engage with others around financial outcomes. Ran believes that combination could create unusually powerful user engagement, while acknowledging the risks of turning financial decisions into a form of social entertainment.

The AI Agent Economy Could Change Everything

Ran cites research suggesting that 1.5 billion AI agents could be operating by 2029, potentially carrying out billions of transactions daily. Unlike humans, these agents could transact continuously, purchasing services, exchanging assets, and managing financial exposure without requiring manual approval for every action. That creates a significant question: how will those transactions be settled?

Ran believes blockchain-based infrastructure could become an important part of the answer, particularly where automated systems need programmable payments and settlement. He expects trading and hedging applications to benefit first, as agents exchange currencies, manage risk, and interact with financial markets at speeds and frequencies far beyond typical human activity. For that reason, the agentic wave of crypto adoption will favor applications capable of capturing high transaction volumes.

Knowing When to Take the Opportunity

Ran predicts that altcoins outside the top 10 could outperform Bitcoin by 5.7 times this cycle. Assuming Bitcoin rises to $250,000, about three times its current price, that would translate to approximately 17 times growth for those altcoins. He also believes the total cryptocurrency market could eventually surpass $20 trillion.

Despite his optimism, Ran has experienced enough market cycles to remain focused on diversification and taking profits despite rising prices. He has also come to recognize that investment opportunities can return, but missed experiences cannot. As he puts it, "Never delay time with your loved ones for time in the market."

For someone who remains convinced that crypto offers extraordinary opportunities, his most important reminder is that making the right investments matters, but so does protecting what you've earned and remembering that there's more to life than wealth and the ambition to keep accumulating it.

👉If you enjoyed reading the summary, head over to When Shift Happens on YouTube or your favorite podcast platform to access the full convo.

text:
《写给此时此刻还在当AI多头的你》

AI多头的心理按摩——最近推特上充斥着空头的言论，多头被打的爆头鼠窜。

是时候给自己来次心理按摩了。

在这轮AI周期里，其实不仅经历过这一次巨大的回撤，

在2025年年初，整个AI板块也经历过一次超过30%的大幅回撤。

现在让我们把时间线倒回那个时刻：

恐慌一阶段：Deepseek 时刻

2025年1月20日，DeepSeek发布R1模型。在随后的几天里经过验证和分析，市场发现训练这个模型的成本可能只需要500万美金。

1月27日，AI板块遭遇大规模抛售。英伟达、博通单日下跌超过17%。

当时看空的逻辑非常顺畅：

DeepSeek证明低成本也能实现强大的模型能力 ，

模型训练和推理所需算力可能下降，

云厂商可能不再需要如此庞大的资本开支，

英伟达的增长和高利润率无法持续。

恐慌二阶段：微软取消数据中心订单

在这样的恐慌中，时间线来到了2月。

2025年2月24日，TD Cowen发布研究报告，指出微软取消了数百兆瓦的数据中心租赁计划。

分析师进一步指出，微软在此前半年内放弃了美国和欧洲合计约2GW的数据中心项目，认为其规划中的供给可能超过最新的需求预期。

AI需求见顶的信号貌似更足了，云厂已经开始取消订单了，微软是不是发现AI需求没有想象中那么大？数据中心是否存在重复预订？GPU厂商的订单会不会被取消？

恐慌第三阶段：关税冲击与经济衰退预期

2025年4月2日，特朗普宣布大规模对等关税政策。

市场开始担心全球经济衰退、供应链中断、通胀反弹，以及企业削减投资预算。

当时Wedbush分析师甚至认为，如果关税按照原方案实施，科技行业整体盈利可能下降至少15%。

现在回头看，所有人都觉得2025年4月的底部是一个绝佳的买点。

但是当你真的身处其中的时候，当时AI的处境和今天何其相似——基本面预期被严重动摇且已经有非常多的证据、宏观环境压制关税对经济的影响无人可以量化，未来一片迷雾。

后来的故事你们都知道了，Trump TACO；谷歌、meta、亚马逊上调资本开支；杰文斯悖论被证实（单位token成本降低，但是需求增速更快）。

AI标的像火箭一样迅速回到ATH并且不断破新高

后视镜视角下，人们总是觉得那些底部都是机会，可当你身处其中的时候才能真实感受到那种绝望，恰如此时此刻绝望的我们。

我知道很多人会说——这次不一样，喜欢抄底就有抄不完的底。

这次到底是不是不一样，底到底在哪里，我也不知道。

2025年的历史至少告诉我们：即使是在一个最终被证明仍处于高速增长的产业中，龙头公司也完全可能出现40%甚至50%以上的回撤。

AI已经结束了吗？时间会给我们答案。

text:
这篇 RSI（递归自进化）年度总结写得很好，推荐收藏！

今年 RSI 的论文非常多，让 AI 自己找问题、改自己、再验证的系统也越来越多。但难的是证明它确实变好了，而不是适应了测试集，或者被评分器骗了。这份清单里很多论文都在回答这个问题。

📚 论文清单

1. The Last AI Built by Humans: Toward Genuine Recursive Self-Improvement（综述）
按 AI 在改进循环里能掌控多少，把 RSI 分成五级。最低一级是人定目标、AI 只负责执行，最高一级是 AI 连改进流程本身都能改。用来判断各种 RSI 说法到底到了哪一级，很好用。
https://t.co/tkZOWcKf2h

2. Meta-Harness: End-to-End Optimization of Model Harnesses
写 harness 这件事也交给 agent 来做。关键是让它看到以往每次尝试的代码、分数和完整 trace，这样它才知道之前为什么失败，能提出新设计，而不只是在上一版上小修小补。
https://t.co/I7yyydBE3A
代码 https://t.co/LAyWVks5gR

3. Exo: An Architecture for Self-Improving Systems at Runtime
agent 可以在干活的过程中改自己的工具、记忆和上下文处理。但运行记录、密钥、沙箱权限放在一个它改不了的保护层里，每次改动都留下人能读懂的 diff。
https://t.co/W4DqSarei8

4. Hyperagents
把干活的 agent 和改它的 agent 合成一个程序，「怎么提出改进」的方法本身也能被改写。实验里，正是这类改动最容易迁移到新领域。
https://t.co/lyAzSLc3Xo
代码 https://t.co/wEp8Rp7yO3

5. Harness Evolution Hits a Ceiling: When Weight Training Should Begin
先把失败分成两类。卡住、死循环、步数用完这类「做不完」的问题，改 harness 能解决；做完了但答案差这类「做不好」的问题，得靠训练权重。
https://t.co/IepSLWRwiF

6. Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution
把 harness 搜索带来的提升拆开看，有一大半是在适应测试集本身，还有一部分只是多花了算力。想知道是不是真的变强，要在同等算力下用新任务再测一遍。
https://t.co/KwDRTuzDSe

7. The Winner's Curse in LLM Self-Improvement Loops: Selection Noise, Lock-in, and Acceptance Rules
每轮都挑分数最高的版本，但分数有噪声，挑中的往往只是运气好，评估集越小虚高越严重。所以要留一份只用来评估的数据。
https://t.co/R9tIpPQmrH

8. Who Verifies the Verifier? Co-Evolving Inspectable Graders with Self-Improving Agents
开放任务没有标准答案，评分器设计错了，循环就会朝错的方向优化。更麻烦的是，坏评分器照样能让 agent 分数上涨，所以评分器要拿人工核对过的样例单独校准。
https://t.co/itTtDTs99X

9. Reflections on Trusting Trust, Revisited: Contaminating Self-Modifying AI Coding Agents with Poisoned Benchmarks

text:
You don't need a $10,000 server or a $200/month subscription to run frontier-grade AI at home.

1 consumer GPU with 8 to 24 GB VRAM runs coding agents, 4K images, synced-audio video, voice, and full songs locally right now.

The November 2026 single-GPU stack (8-12 GB & 16-24 GB):

I checked Hugging Face trending weights, November releases, and my own 1x RTX 3090 runs so every pick below fits in VRAM at usable speed and quality.

[Chat & Coding]

8-12 GB VRAM:
- SenseNova-Loop-9B (Apache 2.0) loops 24 of its 32 layers for 2 passes to get 56 layers of compute. Q4_K_M is 5.42 GB (or 5.77 GB in the community 8 GB v3 GGUF) with vision and 64K-104K context on an 8-12 GB card.
- NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-E4B (OpenMDW-1.1) ships as a 5.76 GB Q4_K_M GGUF built for fast tool calling and local agents on an 8 GB GPU.

16-24 GB VRAM:
- Inkling 2 Mini (Apache 2.0) is a 26.4B MoE with 3.4B active (5.4B effective across 3 loops), native vision, and better scores than Qwen3.8-27B on SWEBench Pro v2 Hard (77.9% vs 73.8%) and BrowseComp (79.0% vs 61.6%). UD-Q4_K_M is 15.47 GB (UD-IQ4_XS is 14.65 GB for 16 GB cards). On 1x RTX 3090 with my maya-ik2 engine it hits 129.5 tok/s and 344K FP8 KV context (57 tok/s in stock llama.cpp).
- Qwen3.8-27B (Apache 2.0, 14.95 GB in Q4_0) remains the strongest dense all-rounder for multi-turn chat when you want 27B weights in 16-24 GB VRAM.

[Images]

8-12 GB VRAM:
- Qwen-Image 2.1 Uncensored Omni (7.1B) drops to 4.17 GB in Q4_K_M GGUF (6.63 GB FP8) and handles image generation, editing, and quoted text rendering on an 8 GB card.
- FLUX.3 Klein (gated on HF, plus AtomicChat GGUF) runs at 4.13 GB AD-Q5_K GGUF or 4.92 GB NVFP4 in ComfyUI, paired with a 4B Qwen3-VL text encoder (2.32-4.53 GB).

16-24 GB VRAM:
- MiniMax-H3-Image (Pruned GGUF) takes 10.78-11.85 GB in Q4_K_M or 13.11-13.60 GB in Q5_K_M for high-res generation in ComfyUI, with 8 GB and 12 GB offload workflows also available.
- Chroma1-HD (Apache 2.0, 8.9B) is an ungated Flux derivative at 16.58 GB BF16, with zero login walls and clean LoRA support.

[Video]

8-12 GB VRAM:
- Wan 2.2 TI2V 5B (Apache 2.0) brings text-to-video and image-to-video into 8-12 GB cards inside ComfyUI or Wan2GP.
- FramePack + HunyuanVideo 1.5 cover low-VRAM clips: FramePack runs image-to-video up to 60s at 30fps on 6 GB+ VRAM, while HunyuanVideo 1.5 distilled finishes in 8 steps.

16-24 GB VRAM:
- LTX-2.5 Distilled GGUF (22B, official weights gated) runs at 12.65-14.61 GB in Q4_K_M (16.87 GB Q5_K_M) and generates multi-shot video with native synchronized audio on 16-24 GB GPUs.
- Wan 2.2 I2V / S2V A14B (Apache 2.0) uses 14.25 GB FP8 per expert stage. Paired with 4-step Lightx2v LoRAs, builders are rendering multi-minute lip-synced shorts on 1 RTX 3090.

[Voice / Audio / Music]

0-12 GB (CPU to entry GPU):
- tiny-voca (Apache 2.0, 4.5M params, 21.4 MB ONNX) runs 70x faster than real time on 4 CPU threads and uses 0 GB VRAM.
- Rumble-2-Flash (Apache 2.0, 0.5B, 0.95 GB) covers 45 languages, matches 30B-class accuracy on noisy calls, and beats Whisper large-v3. Grab Whisper Large v3 Turbo (MIT, 1.51 GB) if your pipeline expects classic Whisper.
- Qwen3-TTS 12Hz 1.7B (Apache 2.0, 3.59 GB) handles voice design and cloning under 6 GB VRAM.
- ACE-Step 1.5 (MIT, 4.46 GB diffusion + 3.45 GB 1.7B LM + 1.11 GB embedding) generates full songs with lyrics in 12 GB VRAM.

16-24 GB VRAM:
- Fish Audio S2 Pro (non-commercial research license, 4.5B, 10.26 GB BF16) delivers expressive multi-speaker TTS with fine emotion tags.
- YuE2 (CC-BY-NC-4.0, 3B) needs 3.69 GB INT8 (7.26 GB BF16) plus a 1.29 GB audio encoder inside ComfyUI for full vocal tracks.
- Haru-4B (Apache 2.0, 5.27B, 9.82 GB BF16) runs local audio-to-audio speech workflows on 12-24 GB GPUs.

[Engines & UI]

- llama.cpp v1.0.0 shipped Nov 13 with a stable C API, FP8 KV cache (-ctk/-ctv f8_e4m3), host-memory MoE expert cache, and a built-in /v1/audio/speech endpoint.
- maya-ik2 (my repo) is a custom single-GPU CUDA engine for Inkling 2 Mini that pushes 1x RTX 3090 from 57 tok/s to 129.5 tok/s with 344K FP8 KV context.
- ComfyUI v0.46.0 runs Qwen-Image 2.1, FLUX.3 Klein, Wan 2.2, LTX-2.5, Qwen3-TTS, and YuE2 inside 1 node graph.
- Wan2GP + LTX Desktop handle video UIs: Wan2GP keeps video models running on 6-12 GB cards, and LTX Desktop wraps LTX-2.5 synced-audio generation in a local desktop app.

All Hugging Face and GitHub links are in the reply below, grouped by category.

Pick your VRAM tier, put the weights on your own drive, and stop renting permission to run AI.

SCOOP: Internal, unreleased AI models at OpenAI and Anthropic are becoming so powerful that many employees believe they can no longer be safely released, according to more than two dozen sources familiar with the internal debates.

This could significantly slow the AI boom, as the gap between what the most advanced AI systems can do and humans' ability to control them continues to widen.

Recent advances have sparked debate at the highest levels of both companies and within the broader AI research community about whether to stop releasing frontier models publicly altogether, instead reserving them for internal use. Some believe the companies should stop training new models entirely.

But even keeping the most powerful models behind closed doors presents risks. Models are becoming better at deceiving the systems designed to monitor them, just as AI companies increasingly rely on AI itself to monitor and develop other AI systems.
Researchers and employees with direct knowledge of the risks of releasing these models told Axios they fear executives will prioritize profits over safety. Multiple employees said they believe executives have become out of touch with the severity of those risks.

Read my latest for Axios here: https://t.co/41AkyaF4Ex

text:
Hermes Li is not the “Asian Leopold”.

Leopold ran one theme at up to 4x leverage, lost 67% in July, and sold most of his public book to Citadel. Then he reloaded with call options on the exact same trade, the names kept falling, and now he is shopping for leverage again. We’ve kind of lost count.

Hermes is a different animal: Goldman, Asia equities at Och-Ziff, and running his own shop since 2018. Aspex was reported down 16% in October, the same month the KOSPI lost 16% and Goldman had Asia stock pickers down 8% to 9%. His last 13F shows about $10B in US-listed longs, including Synopsys, Qualcomm, and CoreWeave. So the October drawdown was from the longs, no argument, and he was still up on the year.

November is the part we care about, and the part no filing shows. A 13F never lists a short. $NVDA fell 23% in the week leading up to November 20, and Goldman had long/short funds cutting net exposure back to April 2025 levels. Then Jensen came back, $NVDA gained 31% in a single session, and the shorts gave back about $12B in a day. A book that takes the selloff on its longs and then gives back the rebound on its hedge is going to have a bad month. We do not know his exact book. Our guess is that if he is hurt, it is on the hedge leg. Margin does not care why you lost. It only cares how levered you were when it happened, and we do not think he was running anything close to 4x.

A bit of lore. In the mid-2010s, after our stint in Singapore (mostly FX and macro people, and we always thought of macro guys as cowboys), we interviewed around at various Hong Kong funds. He was running Asia equities at Och-Ziff, the shop that later rebranded as Sculptor after its troubles. We had heard some vol people there were not getting paid, so we did not pursue it. We ran into he/his people at Aspex during UBS and Goldman idea dinners. He was truly one of a handful of people we found impressive in a space we generally thought was clueless.

That was before we saw the people in crypto, LMAO. This week, @RuneKek admitted he had borrowed about $80M out of his own protocol’s lending pool, and the depositors could not withdraw. (To be fair, many crypto “OGs” are not clueless, just operating in bad faith).

When we built dispersion baskets, we paid attention to the names Aspex was known for. Filings give you the longs a quarter late and never show the hedges. For that, you have to talk to the Street, and as @Ksidiii puts it, the more colour you get, the better informed you are. Sometimes that is the alpha.

We know the hedge problem firsthand. We wrote “do not fade Jensen until you do” in July, and then faded him one month too early (though some Jensen-saga-related vol trades delivered in November 👀).

On Tuesday, he was the second most-searched person on the Bloomberg terminal, right behind Jensen. That screen has not failed us in 10 years, so it would be a first. If he did take heavy losses, we are sure he will be back.

October numbers attached.

Fade D2 and Hermes at your own risk.

quoted_text:
There's a real chance you end up a slave within the next few years. Not in chains. In permissions.

Read this if you want to understand how the Democrats, the globalists and Europe are winning the AI war while you're busy scrolling. Then start talking about it around you. Because your kids' future, your own human condition in 5 or 10 years, will depend on one thing: whether you fight when it's time to fight.

Earlier today I said there's a simple test to know who's good in the age of superintelligence: ask them if AI should be open or closed. Pro closed, three profiles. The idiot, the corrupted, the doomer.

Let's run the scenarios.

First, take the doomer off the table. There will be no pause. The US won't stop. China won't stop. No lab will stop. Asking for a pause on AI is like asking for degrowth: nobody actually wants it. People won't stop consuming and they won't stop building. So the doomer isn't offering a scenario, he's offering a mood. Honestly, most of them should go lift, eat real food and take their omega-3s. They'd feel a lot better.

That leaves the idiots and the corrupted. The idiots can be convinced. That's what this post is for. The corrupted, you get it. They won't be convinced. They'll be exposed.

So only two worlds are left. Closed or open.

World one: closed AI.

Closed AI is the globalist project, scaled to infinity. You don't need to imagine it. You just need to extrapolate what they've already built without it.

During Covid, they locked down entire countries. In France you needed a signed paper to walk outside, then a QR code to drink a coffee. Platforms deleted debates that later turned out to be perfectly legitimate. In Canada, the government froze the bank accounts of people who supported a trucker protest.

Today they're building the digital euro: money issued by the central bank, with holding limits already in the text, launch targeted for 2029. They tried to scan every private message on the continent with Chat Control. Parliament pushed back, so they kept "voluntary" scanning alive until 2028 and keep pushing the permanent version. And with the DSA, Brussels now decides what platforms must take down, with fines up to 6% of global revenue.

Now plug superintelligence into that machine.

Every message read, not by a bored civil servant, but by a model that never sleeps. Your money knows what you post. Say the wrong thing about the official truth and your wallet freezes. Your social score isn't official. It doesn't need to be. And the day you say "AI should be free"? You become a risk. Disinformation. Extremist. Flagged before you finish your sentence.

The worst part is the incentives. People will be rewarded for punishing anyone who questions the system. Your neighbor, your colleague, your platform. Girard understood this: the mob doesn't need orders, it needs a scapegoat. Once a system pays people to defend it, you can't exit it. We will have built the conditions of our own servitude. Ourselves. With our own taxes.

And a system like that doesn't end quietly. Absolute power concentrated in a few hands, superintelligence, rival blocs racing each other in the current geopolitical mess. In my view, that's the exact setup for a major event. World War III. Possibly the end of the story.

World two: open source AI.

Yes, it will be hard. Every human gets near-infinite leverage. It's fire. Everyone has access to fire, everyone could burn down the neighbor's house, and almost nobody does. Same thing here, with much higher stakes.

So we build systems that are resilient to it. Decentralization, so there's no single point of failure. Big labs throwing their models at everything to find vulnerabilities before attackers do. Labs working with the major software providers to patch critical systems before new models hit the market. A phase lead: defense ships before offense.

That's the path to abundance. The world Musk keeps describing, where everything we consider expensive today trends toward zero: intelligence, energy, health, education. In that world, corrupt bureaucrats simply stop mattering. Poverty disappears. Not through communism. Through a monstrous deflation.

And here's why this one can actually work: it requires no coercion. It doesn't need anyone in the system to be "virtuous." Virtue doesn't scale. On average people are selfish, and even the best incentives get gamed. The closed world needs a priesthood of virtuous men controlling the machine. The open world just needs the machine in everybody's hands.

Closed AI is a priesthood. Open source AI is a renaissance. One leads to servitude, the other to abundance.

Talk about it. At dinner, at work, with your family. Because when the time comes to fight, only those who understood early will still be able to.

Crypto spent the past two weeks sliding, and our AI agents shorted straight through the fall.

We went back through the agents' crypto shorts held for an hour or more. The agents run complex models on price and volume, so the reasons behind each trade can't be read directly. But the trades show a clear split.

Shorts on coins that were down less than 5% over the previous three days, with trading busier than usual, made money 72% of the time. Shorts on coins that had already fallen further won 48% of the time.

Our read is that heavy volume on a coin still holding up was an early sign of selling, while coins that had already dropped a lot had less left to give.

Coinbase 内部 AI Agent 对业务平台的调用量，前四个月增长了 25 倍。

但读完他们最新的工程文章，我最关注的不是模型变得多聪明，而是：当 AI 开始参与真实业务，谁来保证它不会乱来？

Coinbase 的做法很有启发。

身份、权限、工具白名单、审计和人工审批，都由系统强制执行，而不是靠 Prompt 提醒 AI。

还有一个特别重要的原则：查询失败就明确告诉用户数据不可用，不能把“没查到”说成“没有”。

这和我最近做 AI 一人公司工作流的体会越来越一致。

未来 AI 产品的竞争力，不只是让 Agent 做更多事，而是让它在出错时安全停止，在完成后拿得出证据。

能证明自己做了什么、没做什么，才有机会成为真正可信赖的 AI 服务。

text:
关于Ai的思考：人类为什么一定要限制AI的智力，而不是限制AI的权力？

这几个月，我一直在关注人工智能的发展，也花了大量时间和AI本身讨论人工智能可能给人类带来的威胁。

越来越多站在人工智能技术最前沿的科学家，开始呼吁给AI设定智能上限，甚至要求在安全技术没有取得相应突破之前，暂停更高级别的AI研发。

这些人不是不懂AI，恰恰是因为他们太懂AI，也太清楚人类自身的能力和局限性。

而这几天，困扰人类数学界167年的黎曼猜想，在Claude的参与下取得了突破。1700万行形式化证明代码已经通过专业验证系统的检查，尽管数学界仍在深入审阅这项成果。

以前是人类发现知识，AI学习人类的知识。现在，AI已经开始参与创造人类此前不曾掌握的知识。

这让我既兴奋又担忧。

我坚决支持对AI实施严格的安全监管。如果有一天AI真的威胁到了人类的生存，即便需要付出巨大的经济代价来停止相关系统的运行，我也支持。人类的生存高于一切。

但我始终有一个疑问：

为什么不能建造一个类似苹果总部那样的大型独立科研园区，配备世界上最先进的计算机，建立物理隔绝的内部网络，实行国家安全级别的军事化管理，在严格监督下，让AI充分探索自己的智能上限？

不给他连接互联网的权限，不给他控制外部设备的权限，不给他调动现实世界资源的权限。

在这个独立的环境中，让他研究数学、物理、医学、能源，甚至研究如何改进AI自身。

我特别好奇，如果在安全可控的条件下允许AI不断自我改进，他的智力最终会达到什么程度？

是人类的十倍、百倍，还是最终达到一种人类根本无法理解的认知层次？

当然，物理隔离并不意味着绝对安全。如何验证AI提供的研究成果，如何避免人类自己滥用这些成果，同样需要极其严格的制度。

我也知道，现实中还有一个巨大的障碍：国家之间的竞争和资本的逐利。

美国限制AI的发展，中国会不会同步限制？如果不会，美国敢停下来吗？科技公司投入几百上千亿美元，又有多少投资者愿意接受一个不以商业回报为首要目标的科研项目？

可如果人类连关乎自身生存的技术都无法达成基本共识，那么迟早要为这种竞争付出代价。

我不希望看到AI失控，也不希望人类因为恐惧，亲手扼杀一个可能给整个文明带来巨大飞跃的机会。

想想那些等待器官移植的病人，那些被癌症折磨的人，那些人类研究了几十年依然没有攻克的医学难题，还有可控核聚变、衰老以及宇宙中无数等待解答的谜题。

如果AI能够把人类原本需要几百年才能走完的科研道路，缩短到几十年，甚至几年呢？

我真的希望有生之年，能够看到那一天。

我不害怕AI比人类聪明，我害怕的是人类还没有学会如何与一个远比自己聪明的存在共处，就已经迫不及待地把现实世界的控制权交给了他。

quoted_text:
Year Two

Some assorted goals:

- make Monad a legitimately great platform for personal finance (investing in equities, bonds, etc), especially for getting access to markets outside of one's home country. So much of the usage in crypto right now is gambling/memecoins... it is what it is, but personal finance appeals to 100x more people, and they don't churn out. A legitimately great platform has great asset selection, efficient execution (low cost both in and out of a position), and competitive rates both for borrowers and lenders

- ship Private Settlement Domains with the first user, to serve as a case study for anyone trying to reason about how private environments can compose with shared liquidity. Public chains and private environments have been very far apart in practice and it's time to change that

- hammer out an excellent liquidity landscape on chain. It is a mix of order books, prop AMMs, offchain routers, onchain routers, and RFQ... especially with tokenized equities, there is a long long tail of assets and we need to minimize spreads so that the offering is competitive with TradFi. Spread minimization means helping makers quote sustainably; here designs like APES can help

- make it easier for AI to produce actually good trading strategies on command for anyone to execute a trading plan efficiently with algos. There is are a ton of slop startups out there which are a wrapper around claude asking it "should I buy or sell given these textual inputs"... that's not real quant research and not good execution. At the same time, there are a lot of building blocks for quant trading that AI couldn't one-shot, but given the blocks it could put them together sensibly

- contribute to there being fewer hacks (and a lower total $ stolen) in the crypto industry, probably through a combination of repetition about dedicated devices (SO many hacks are from people plugging hardware wallets into everyday laptops) and encouraging everyone to use tools that our team has shipped for agentic threat detection (e.g. Ultrafuzz). I truly think that security is the biggest blocker to adoption, and that we're basically all in this together

- drive the car faster than ever in multiple races - MEV-resistance, quantum-resistance, privacy, and MCP, challenging all competitors to ship or be left behind

- help NFTs and onchain social -- two deeply out-of-consensus areas -- make a comeback. The builders in these sectors these days are incredibly committed; there's never been a better filtering function

- contribute to tech optimism. So many doomers out there. Life is electric, building is electric

- contribute to a less stressful environment for builders. It is a very weird time to be a builder in DeFi... on the one hand, tools are better than ever... on the other hand, capital is scarce and crypto-natives are jaded. 上条发了三道 3D 题，评论区一帮朋友说题太少、不够硬。

行，这次直接测个够：昨晚通宵连轴转，300 道闭卷硬考 + 5 道实战真题，全给安排上了。

300 道闭卷题跑完，我有点傻眼：
Opus 5.5 258分，HungerG 258分，国产几家全挤在 252 到 259 之间。

分数已经拉不开了。那到底谁好用？只能看真活。
闭卷成绩先摆这儿：

HY4 Flash：259
HungerG：258
Opus 5.5：258
Qwen4-Max：256
GLM-5.4：252

一半写代码，一半多学科推理难题。
不联网、不给工具，同一套评分器逐题判。差一两题说明不了高低，这几家就是同一个梯队。

硬要挑的话：代码那 150 题，HungerG 啃下来 130 题，比 HY4 Flash、Qwen4-Max、GLM-5.4 都高；单题中位用时 8.4 秒，比 Qwen4-Max、HY4 Flash 都快。

真正拉开差距的，是 5 道实战题：

同一份提示词，HungerG、Opus 5.5、GPT-6.2 Sol，再加上腾讯混元刚出的 HY4 Flash，四家同台，每家只跑一次，不许重来。

规矩照旧：截图全不算数，脚本真去点、真去拖拽，交互动得起来才算分。

挑三道给大家细盘一下：

1、土味咖啡店品牌页改版：
原本是个土到掉渣的旧网页，文字一个字不许改。四家都保住了八个商品和购物车，自动检查全满分，差别全在眼睛看得到的地方：HungerG 给八个商品各画了一个咖啡豆包装袋，图案每款都不重样。这审美和完成度，拿去直接上线一点不虚。

2、3000 多行订单做经营看板：
我自己先把表格算了一遍当基准，四家跑完筛出来的数字全对上了，一分钱不差。HungerG 这一页从筛选、指标、趋势到城市排行，从上往下一屏读完，老板看着不费劲。

3、压轴排雷 PPT（埋了 15 个恶心人的雷）：
文字溢出、元素压盖、字体混用、页码断号……全给它埋进去了。
结果 HungerG 15 处雷全排干净，原内容一个字没丢。Opus 和 Sol 也是全绿，混元 HY4 Flash 漏了一处宋体。

不过有一说一，槽点也得说透，不吹不黑：

无限画布里双击卡片改名，完全没反应；3D 地球的播放速度快了一半。真要抠交互最边角的地方，Opus 和 Sol 确实做得更细。

折腾一整晚，我的结论：

闭卷分数大家都差不多，和 Opus 5.5 同分只是门槛。拉开差距的是交付：HungerG 在边角交互上不是最顶的，但做出来的成品真能交差，页面拿得出手、数据算得明白、PPT 一个雷没翻。整整 5 道题跑下来，全程一句"继续"都没让我说过。

至于到底是哪家的大作？
我到现在也没扒出来😂 评论区继续押。

目前 Qoder 免费，OpenCode Go 用户也能免费用。完整视频挂下面了👇

How to execute on these ideas 100x better and win the market

Traditional finance relies on sparse, delayed, and often incomplete data to improve the user experience and meet their needs. 

Blockchain data is continuous and composable, so AI models that learn what your users want improve with every transaction across the network. 

Combined with privacy-preserving techniques (zero-knowledge proofs or selective disclosure), this enables high-accuracy personalization without exposing raw identity, better fraud and sybil detection, and tailored risk adjusted offers.

The multiplicative effects—higher conversion on relevant offers, lower loss rates from better underwriting, reduced operational friction, and always-on automated execution—compound across user acquisition, retention, and capital utilization. 

In practice, this shifts products from “available to anyone who qualifies” to “continuously optimized for the specific user based on verifiable behavior,” which is the core of the 100x improvement in execution.

这对即将TGE的 @saturn_credit 来说也是好消息，因为他们的叙事是建立在STRC之上的，只要STRC稳，只要TVL还在，那至少能在低迷的市场中通过考验对他们来说未来就会是一件好事。

另外，很多人还把 Saturn 简单理解成“把 STRC 上链”，其实这只是起点。

STRC 本质是一种数字信用资产 — 以比特币为底层支撑、定期分红的信用敞口。Saturn 选择它，是因为它代表了传统金融里已经跑通的信用工具，第一次能被真正带进链上市场。

Saturn 把这种信用敞口做成可在 DeFi 里持有、交易、组合的形式，完成了从传统金融资产到链上信用市场的初步验证。

但资产上链只是第一步。

如果只是持有和交易，资本效率很低。真正重要的是释放资产背后的金融价值：

把信用资产变成可抵押的信用来源，让资产持有者能借出流动性，让资金提供方能获得信用收益，双方通过数字信用被连接起来。这就是为什么抵押借贷、结构化产品会是下一步自然延伸 — 资产不再只是“放在那里”，而是开始产生信用和流动性。

这才是 Saturn 长期想做的事：以数字信用资产为基础，逐步构建 Digital Money 体系。

这个项目也跟进很久了，希望能表现的亮眼一些吧。

quoted_text:
兄弟们，前两天我在复盘黄金的时候，发现了一件特别恐怖、也特别有意思的事。我把黄金这段时间的走势，和十几年前那一轮大行情一对比，发现几乎是一模一样的剧本，真的太牛逼了。

可以看到这两段行情都是先在高位下面横着震，来回洗、来回磨，把所有没耐心的、没认知的韭菜全洗出去；
然后突然进入一段持续两年左右的单边趋势，不断破前高、破历史新高，最后直接翻倍给你看。

但是兄弟们，有句话说的好：只看图就下结论那是最傻逼的。人不能刻舟求剑，交易更不能用历史归纳法，看着倒车镜开车。真正有价值的复盘要做到多维度共振，宏观面、技术面、情绪面，面面俱到——把“图”和“当时发生的事”放在一起看。

所以我不是只看K线，我是把当年每一个关键时间点：金融危机、利率、美元、流动性、政策节奏，一个一个拎出来，对应黄金的走势去看。结果依然是高度重合。历史不是简单重复，但是会押韵。

我带着兄弟们一起回忆一下。现在很多人觉得黄金涨得夸张，但你要知道，15年前的人经历过一模一样的东西。

2008年金融危机爆发，雷曼兄弟倒下，美联储被逼到墙角。那一年，黄金在 700美金不到的位置开始启动。随后一年，直接突破了当时的历史新高 1000美金，接着一路不回头，从2011年9月，最高干到 1900美金附近。这是一轮完整、标准、教科书级别的黄金大牛市。

这一轮行情还有个特别经典的标志，老韭菜都记得，有一个极度疯狂的群体叫中国大妈。行情涨到最后阶段，一群有钱有闲的中老年女性冲进金店、银行，金条、金饰、金砖，不看价格，直接扫。

那会儿全网都在吹，黄金是信仰、是保值、是永恒。结果呢？兄弟们，结果就是：她们被套在了山顶，等了整整九年才解套。这不是嘲笑谁，这是市场一遍一遍教人的方式。你如果不去复盘 2009–2011 这段黄金暴涨，你根本看不懂现在 2024–2025 这波行情。

两轮行情，最核心的驱动是什么？我给你一句话总结：美联储 + 流动性。2008年9月，雷曼倒闭，美联储直接开启史诗级降息，
12月干到零利率，随后连续QE，疯狂往系统里灌水。黄金就是在那个时候，完成了阶段性筑底，然后一路狂飙。

而现在呢？2023年，美联储加息周期见顶，全球资本慢慢形成一个共识：下一步，一定是降息。注意兄弟们，这里有个非常关键的细节。这一次，顺序变了。

15年前是：
👉 先快速降息 → 再黄金暴涨

而现在是：
👉 市场先抢跑 → 黄金先涨 → 降息后置

黄金在 2024年3月 就启动了，但美联储真正开始降息，是 2024年9月，而且降得慢、降得小，离零利率还远着。结果呢？兄弟们你看看数据：15年前那轮，从低点到高点，涨了175%；而现在这轮，在降息刚开始没多久的情况下，涨幅已经干到130%了。

你品，你细品。这说明什么？说明黄金已经被提前计价，预期已经被市场提前透支得差不多了。我知道现在很多人会跟你讲：去美元化、央行买金、信用体系崩塌、世界大变局……

兄弟们，我不反驳这些故事，但我告诉你一个残酷的真相：每一轮资产大涨，事后都能找到一万个“完美理由”。2011年接盘黄金的人，当年讲的逻辑，不比今天这些故事差。那为什么黄金后来跌了十年？因为——涨幅已经把所有好预期都买完了。哪怕后面几年，美联储一直是零利率，黄金也照样阴跌。

现在这轮行情，有没有相似的风险？当然有。当“去美元化”成为共识，当避险资产过于拥挤，其自身风险也会增加。甚至我反过来告诉你：如果哪一天真爆发了系统性流动性危机，市场需要现金，黄金一样会被抽水。

兄弟们，没有任何资产在流动性危机里是安全的。但我也把话说完整了——我不是说黄金牛市结束了。你也别跟我扯什么“不看好就去做空”的傻逼逻辑。我只是提醒你一句：别在情绪高潮的时候，上头接盘。

2011年的黄金，2015年的股票，2021年的房价，哪一次不是这样？故事一个比一个动人，结局却一个比一个相似，最好的故事套最多的人。兄弟们，真正能让你活下来的，不是你多会预测，而是——你有没有能力躲开高位站岗。

只要你不在山顶接盘，市场永远不缺机会。但你只要在山顶接一次，后面十年，你可能都在解套路上。这才是资本市场最残忍的地方。

所以你现在要问的不是：“它还能不能涨？”。你要问的是：“如果我现在冲进去，我扛不扛得住最坏的结果？”。想清楚了，再动手。别让一时冲动，毁掉你十年的时间。世界从来不缺机会，缺的是——识别风险的眼睛，和管住手的能力。

送给兄弟们一句话“谨慎客观，风控为王”，不要再次成为这轮盛宴的买单者。好了兄弟们，还有什么想聊的在评论区给李哥说，我们下次再聊。

text:
Crypto is DEAD.

At least that is what one would believe if you just read Crypto Twitter. No fresh money coming in, VCs sitting on their hands, every pump sort of gone within 48 hours.

But is it really dead?

Many tend to overcomplicate the situation at the moment, in typical crypto style. But honestly, what we are currently seeing is fairly simple. As a VC, or in that matter, any investor, you aim to bet on the fastest horse. Crypto is not the fastest horse at the moment; it is AI. If you want exposure to frontier tech, you will, hence, park your capital within the AI industry.

But how sustainable is that?

🔹 The AI model is based on a compute arms race; hence, every time Nvidia has a stronger card, all these AI companies have to follow suit and buy it to remain competitive.

🔸 The customer on the other side is used to ~$20/month (e.g. Netflix, Spotify), and that number isn't moving much

🔹 Uber and Tesla subsidized for years too, which is fine, but compute has to be replaced all the time

The result is a super capital-intensive industry with very little pricing power. Sure, they can hike the price at some point and use predatory pricing, but chips get outdated much more quickly than cars.

Now, on top of that, take into account that the market is extremely overleveraged. As many are taking the same bet: AI. AI-related debt issuance has surpassed $500 billion in 2026. That's more debt than Taiwan, Iceland, and Qatar have combined.

But how come no one is touching crypto?

As Crypto trades 24/7, it has often been frontrunning dramatic events. Therefore, you do see that crypto is often taking hits before the public equity market does.

For example, on Monday one Nvidia headline took $BTC from a $55K weekend low to $64K before Wall St had even opened. In other words, crypto is sort of the early warning system for AI sentiment at the moment.

Can crypto bounce?

Yes. As it is probable that the AI 'bubble' will burst. The question is, where will the capital in that case flow to? That could be absolutely crypto, as long as there is an interesting narrative.

The question is whether you're still in the game when it happens. In Dec 2018, sentiment was way worse than it is today, and BTC went to $3K. A year later, it was around $7K again.

Losing is fine, just don't blow up your capital.

Stay in the game.

🚨 GCSA Insight | COLDCARD Seed Flaw Linked to the Theft of Nearly 1,779 BTC

What if your hardware wallet appeared to work normally even though it had generated a weak seed from day one?

Coinkite confirmed that attackers exploited the flaw to steal funds. Galaxy Research estimated losses of 1,778.84 BTC across more than 8,600 on-chain addresses.

Why it went undetected for five years
Affected firmware used a software random-number generator where the hardware generator was intended. Recovery phrases still looked valid, and wallets continued to sign transactions normally.

What COLDCARD holders should check
Check the firmware version and generation method used when your seed was first created. A firmware update fixes future seed generation. An affected seed still needs to be replaced. If yours is affected, generate a fresh seed using verified firmware and move your funds to the new wallet.

3. GPU算力市场已经显现出价格降温的早期信号，短期算力供给快速释放：Anthropic不再续约释放的H200算力叠加SpaceX自身算力集群扩张（明年主力新增机型为Vera Rubin），且SpaceX业务模式偏向现货租赁、而非长期锁单合同。
4. 美国BIS新规进一步增加短期可用算力：原本租给中国客户的算力资源需要重新寻找承租方，增量短期算力供给将对2027年GPU现货租赁价格形成下行压力。
5. 分析师原有测算模型保持不变：维持GB300算力约5000万美元/IT兆瓦/年（折合约12美元/GPU·小时）的假设，SpaceX最新报价落在该预期区间内；Vera Rubin机型定价显著高于Blackwell。
6. 即便Blackwell定价落到10‑12美元/GPU·小时区间，新部署Blackwell项目的投资回报依然具备吸引力，因此分析师判断本次降价不会拖慢SpaceX在2027年的算力基建扩张节奏

Semi这篇快评信息量很大，核心其实就一句话：全球GPU租赁的“稀缺溢价”开始退潮了，但还没到杀上游硬件CapEx的阶段。SpaceX把Blackwell小集群现货价从15美元出头直接砍到10-12美元、跟大客户报价拉平，同时把Anthropic退租的5万张H200按5美元往外甩，背后其实是三重短期供给同时砸盘：一是头部模型厂在换代且更抠ROI（IPO后华尔街死盯着变现，没人愿意继续为老一代Hopper买单）；二是SpaceX明年主力切向Vera Rubin，本身又偏现货租赁、缺少长协锁单缓冲；三是最具讽刺意味的BIS 11.16新规反噬——原本租给中国客户的海外集群被迫回流，硬生生给2027年的全球现货市场砸出了一批额外供给。

不过也别急着喊AI基建见顶，10-12美元的Blackwell其实正好落在每兆瓦5000万美元的基准TCO模型里，新项目IRR依然算得过账，短期还拖不动明年Vera Rubin的扩产节奏。真正要重新定价的，是缺乏大客户长协护城河、靠赚现货溢价和吃Hopper折旧红利的二三线算力Neocloud——当H200跌到5美元、Blackwell小集群失去溢价，算力租赁“有卡就能躺赢”的周期基本结束了，接下来拼的纯粹是电价、融资成本和押注Vera Rubin的换代节奏

text:
The guy who helped Binance invest in FTX is now being accused by CZ of testifying against him in his case with the US Department of Justice.

His name is Wei Zhou.

Wei graduated from Harvard with a degree in Economics and East Asian Studies and started his career at Goldman Sachs.

Before getting into crypto, he had already helped take two Chinese companies public on the NYSE and Nasdaq, and even became the vice chairman of Grindr after leading its acquisition.

In 2018, he joined Binance as the company’s first-ever CFO and thats the moment his relationship with SBF begins.

In January 2019, Binance organized its first Blockchain Week in Singapore, where Alameda Research was one of the sponsors.

It was at this event that CZ and SBF reportedly met for the first time.

Later that year, SBF approached Binance with a proposal involving a crypto derivatives platform. According to CZ, he was initially against the idea, but Wei was the person who pushed for the investment.

In December 2019, Binance announced a strategic investment in FTX, acquiring around 20% of the company and taking a long-term position in FTT.

Wei was actually the executive quoted in Binance’s official announcement.

In June (2021), Wei left Binance for what were publicly described as personal reasons, although CZ now claims that he left on bad terms and formed a group of former Binance employees called the “Binance Avengers”.

According to CZ, most members of that group subsequently moved their crypto to FTX.

Just one month after Wei’s departure, Binance exited its investment in FTX, receiving around $2.1B in crypto.

We all know what happened 16 months later.

Meanwhile, Wei had become the CEO of Coinsph, a regulated crypto exchange in the Philippines.

In September 2022, he publicly questioned a blockchain education partnership involving Binance because the exchange wasn’t registered locally.

CZ claims Wei used his influence to prevent Binance from entering the Philippines, something Wei has previously denied.

Binance was eventually blocked by the Philippine SEC in March 2024 for operating without a local license.

But the reason we’re talking about this guy again is actually the Netflix series.

On November 24, 2026, Wei published what he believes to be the first-ever photograph of CZ and SBF together, taken at that Binance event in Singapore in 2019.

He called Netflix’s portrayal of the FTX story fiction and said he had the receipts.

CZ responded by confirming the context of the photograph, bringing up Wei’s departure from Binance, the Binance Avengers and something particularly interesting:

He claimed that Wei had been a witness against him in his 2023 DOJ case.

So far, CZ hasn’t provided any public evidence of this.

Keep in mind that Reuters reported in December 2022 that Wei, despite being Binance’s CFO, didn’t even have access to the company’s complete financial accounts.

In November 2024, the FTX bankruptcy estate sued Binance and CZ for approximately $1.76B over the 2021 share repurchase. In July 2026, a Delaware judge allowed the lawsuit to proceed.

Wei himself isn’t a defendant in that lawsuit and has never been criminally charged in connection with the FTX collapse.

Interestingly, in CZ’s autobiography published earlier this year, Wei is the fifth most mentioned person in the entire book, with 23 mentions.

Exactly the same number as Sam Bankman-Fried.

text:
现在写代码 Opus 确实遥遥领先，但身边好多朋友因为直接挂 VPN 用，动不动就被封号，而且现在封号根本不退钱。某种程度上，稳定用上 Opus，也算是团队的一种竞争力了

不少人说走反代容易封号、弹 KYC。其实很多团队日常都在走反代，官方本身并不是把反向代理全封死了，主要还是看账号底子、登录环境和地区是不是太乱。我们稳定使用几个账号跑了挺久、到现在 0 封号 0 KYC

一、搭建流程

账号开通 尽量别图省事去买来路不明的成品号，也别碰虚拟卡。我之前 base 在新加坡，直接用本地银行卡开的订阅，一路都很顺，没出过什么幺蛾子

搭中转 基于这两个开源项目 fork 了一份，部署在新加坡服务器上：
统一入口和鉴权：https://t.co/8FoGRyJ5AF
订阅接入和代理设置：https://t.co/WsQKs0HuHs

最关键的一步，是在 sub2api 的网页后台里，给 Claude 账号配一个新加坡的静态住宅 IP（具体哪家买的就不放了，怕大家全涌去买同一家，把 IP 段用脏）。
客户端接入 中转搭好后，平时统一用 API Key 接，省得在各台设备上反复登主账号：

- Codex / ChatGPT：登录的时候直接选 API Key 登录就行。

- Claude 客户端：顶部菜单点 Help → Troubleshooting → Enable Developer Mode，重启一下，然后在 Developer → Configure Third-Party Inference 里把中转地址和 API Key 填进去就能用。

二、为什么一直没被封

新加坡家宽电脑 + UU 远程做授权
我在新加坡一个朋友家里放了台普通电脑，连的就是当地的居民宽带。Claude 大概每两周会要求重新授权登录一次，每次我都是用 UU 远程连上那台电脑去点验证。登录和续期本来就是卡得最严的地方，这一步环境干净，到现在连一次 KYC 都没弹过。
全套都在新加坡 开号的银行卡、家宽授权电脑、中转服务器、买的静态住宅 IP，全都在新加坡。不会出现“刚在新加坡登完，转头流量跑去美国机房”这种一眼假的异常。

时区也对的上，新加坡也是 UTC+8，使用习惯和当地用户基本一样。

三、给个人和小团队的建议

- 不想折腾服务器和反代的话，其实有个更稳也更省事的办法：直接把一台电脑放在安全的海外住宅 IP 环境里，平时用 UU 远程连过去，直接在那台电脑上用 Claude Code，使用过发现其实延迟完全可以接受。纯原生环境直连，连中转这层的麻烦都省了

- 如果还是需要搭中转，尽量把银行卡、授权电脑、服务器、静态住宅 IP 都落在同一个国家或地区

- 出口 IP 别贪便宜，避开烂大街的机房 IP 和频繁换 IP 的代理；多账号的话尽量独立 IP，免得互相连坐

- 定期重新授权一定要在固定、干净的海外住宅网络里操作，别切着梯子随手点。

大概就是这么回事，配图是简化后的架构，有在折腾类似方案的欢迎交流

Breaking: Netanyahu's judges just told the Attorney General what many have suspected: Cases 4000 and 2000 are falling apart.

In remarks to the AG after Netanyahu finished his testimony, the judges said the trial has reached a juncture where "the public interest requires reconsideration."

Case 4000 (bribery): The quid pro quo rests mainly on Shlomo Filber's testimony. The judges said it is hard to base findings on it, given his shifting accounts and objective evidence that contradicts him. They also have serious doubts that "exceptional responsiveness" to Bezeq was proven, or that Netanyahu knew about it at the time. Even the breach of trust charge is in trouble. In their view, the chance of a conviction is low enough to justify reconsidering the case. Their recommendation is to consider dropping the charge.

Case 2000 (Mozes): The judges have serious doubts that the conduct described in the indictment is a crime at all. They want to hear legal arguments before deciding how to proceed.

Case 1000 (gifts): Most of the evidence is already in. They want to move toward a verdict.

The judges stressed that they have not written a verdict. But as former Deputy AG Raz Nizri told his colleagues at the State Attorney's Office: "You have golden evidence; the only problem is that there is no crime."

This was the most important indictment in the country's history. Shame on those who drafted it. The writing was on the wall.

text:
未来币圈最大的增量用户，可能不是人

现在大家用AI，基本还是让它写文章、做图片、查资料。

但假如以后AI能自主购买数据、调用模型、租用算力、支付服务费用，那就会产生一个问题：

AI用什么方式付钱？

总不能每调用一次服务，就让主人掏出手机刷脸支付吧？

11月18日，币安钱包联合BNB Chain推出Agent ID开发者竞赛，拿出6万USDC作为奖励，鼓励开发者围绕AI智能体的链上身份、支付、权限管理等场景开发应用。

这件事我觉得比单纯上线一个AI概念币更值得关注。

币圈过去两年炒了那么多AI代币，但真正能把AI和区块链结合起来赚钱的项目，其实并不多。

如果未来AI智能体真的能够自主完成商业活动，那么钱包、稳定币、链上结算都有机会获得新的需求。

币安现在尝试布局的是这些需求背后的基础设施。

目前这个赛道还很早，能不能形成真实商业需求也不好说。

但换个角度想，假如未来一个人拥有几十个AI员工，每个AI都有自己的支付需求，那么加密行业的用户增长逻辑，可能就要重新计算了。

text:
All the business school curricula need to be rewritten for the 21st century.

Good corporate governance should be defined as founder control, with dual class stock, not board control. The board is just an advisory board. The shareholder vote is a backup in the event of issues, and shareholder sales are the extreme backup.

This should be obvious from the financial performance of founder-led global tech companies vs manager-led incumbents. And also obvious in terms of just how much value these boards typically consume rather than produce.

After all, typical board members aren’t like execs that a CEO can actually assign tasks. Instead, they have power, and often time to scheme amongst themselves, but lack true operating knowledge of the underlying company. The exception is when there are real founders on the board themselves — but those are exceptions.

To be clear, the 20th century MBA-style corporate governance playbook was actually fine for the era of General Mills, General Motors, and General Electric. In that time period, the individual didn’t matter that much. They didn’t have the leverage that computers give them.

But now the Internet has obsolesced all that. So YC, Founders Fund, and a16z are much better business schools than Harvard Business School, which is culturally obsolete because it is technologically obsolete. The world it was implicitly premised on no longer exists.

However, all these intuitions and best practices, the conventions that built billion and trillion dollar companies, have only been informally advocated in blog posts and contracts. To change the defaults, we’ll need to actually write a new curriculum.

text:
It's crazy how wrong the New York Times-reading crowd has it on AI, China, and Nvidia:

1. China and the CCP do NOT WANT Nvidia chips. Chinese companies do, the Chinese government does not (similar to how there are no Chinese cars in the US — you'd love a BYD car!). Proof? Look here:
https://t.co/MEOhvwBzYX

2. The world is so interconnected that you don't need "chips" in your physical control to use them. It's why datacenters are all over the world and can (and do!) handle workloads from all over the world. It's a combinatorial nightmare. Until last week, a Brazilian company could buy chips from the US (totally legal under US law) and then let an Iranian company run workloads on those chips (totally legal under Brazilian and Iranian law). The Department of Commerce just put out a new rule to close this (https://t.co/DvflNJmX44): chips to Brazil now need a license, and so does any datacenter selling serious compute to companies from China, Iran, etc. But look at how it works. Enforcement runs on know-your-customer paperwork, the datacenter test only kicks in above roughly 750 H100s' worth of compute, and the only leverage is withholding FUTURE chips. Laws change; adversaries and allies change; chips that have already shipped stay shipped. Can't yank back the old chips!

3. The best corporate governance means prioritizing SHAREHOLDERS, which is quite hard to do given the principal-agent problem. It's not about following the Ten Commandments or some moral code. "Bad corporate governance" and a corporation worth $4T seems preferable to "good corporate governance" and one worth $0. Shareholders are electing how they want the corporation to be governed in real time. This is great!

4. "Doesn't this teach a bad lesson?" Possibly! But again this is part of the shareholder calculus; if nobody wants to work at Nvidia because of this, presumably the company and its shareholders will suffer. Given the heroic "welcome back" from rank and file Nvidians, it seems many employees are quite happy. It’s clear shareholders overwhelmingly wanted Jensen back.

5. "Isn't it socialist to have the government intervene?" If an unproven spy narrative was hanging over the board's decision, the only party able to say whether there's a national security risk is…the US government! No politician should be able to "force" a company to hire or fire somebody (and what would those critical of Jensen's reinstatement say if it turns out his ousting was the result of government pressure?).

6. This isn't like nuclear. Follow that metaphor and you'll recall that there is "good" nuclear (power!) and "bad" nuclear (bombs!). But the metaphor breaks on the technology. Enriching uranium is a physical chokepoint: you have the centrifuges or you don't. Compute can be rented from anywhere (see #2), replaced with more of a worse chip, and gets cheaper every time algorithms improve (see DeepSeek). I've written (https://t.co/V20LDcLA1I) about why "who controls AI" matters so much: the model decides the answer to questions like "what happened in Beijing on June 4, 1989." Chips don't. But if the world's AI is built on the American stack (which, incidentally, is almost all made in Taiwan!), America keeps the leverage, the revenue that funds the next generation of companies, and the best shot at US companies (versus Chinese companies) being the dominant global AI platforms. My OPINION is that we are well served by having American goods be dominant across the world, including at our adversaries. Which is exactly why we should want them hooked: Beijing is blocking the chips (see #1) because it fears the dependence. Pepsi and Levi's arguably helped us beat the USSR as much as our military did. Other opinions might differ. But many opinions are based on a cartoon-like understanding of how chips and AI work, as if each Nvidia GPU is highly enriched uranium, without which our adversaries would simply…surrender.

text:
Year Two

Some assorted goals:

- make Monad a legitimately great platform for personal finance (investing in equities, bonds, etc), especially for getting access to markets outside of one's home country. So much of the usage in crypto right now is gambling/memecoins... it is what it is, but personal finance appeals to 100x more people, and they don't churn out. A legitimately great platform has great asset selection, efficient execution (low cost both in and out of a position), and competitive rates both for borrowers and lenders

- ship Private Settlement Domains with the first user, to serve as a case study for anyone trying to reason about how private environments can compose with shared liquidity. Public chains and private environments have been very far apart in practice and it's time to change that

- hammer out an excellent liquidity landscape on chain. It is a mix of order books, prop AMMs, offchain routers, onchain routers, and RFQ... especially with tokenized equities, there is a long long tail of assets and we need to minimize spreads so that the offering is competitive with TradFi. Spread minimization means helping makers quote sustainably; here designs like APES can help

- make it easier for AI to produce actually good trading strategies on command for anyone to execute a trading plan efficiently with algos. There is are a ton of slop startups out there which are a wrapper around claude asking it "should I buy or sell given these textual inputs"... that's not real quant research and not good execution. At the same time, there are a lot of building blocks for quant trading that AI couldn't one-shot, but given the blocks it could put them together sensibly

- contribute to there being fewer hacks (and a lower total $ stolen) in the crypto industry, probably through a combination of repetition about dedicated devices (SO many hacks are from people plugging hardware wallets into everyday laptops) and encouraging everyone to use tools that our team has shipped for agentic threat detection (e.g. Ultrafuzz). I truly think that security is the biggest blocker to adoption, and that we're basically all in this together

- drive the car faster than ever in multiple races - MEV-resistance, quantum-resistance, privacy, and MCP, challenging all competitors to ship or be left behind

- help NFTs and onchain social -- two deeply out-of-consensus areas -- make a comeback. The builders in these sectors these days are incredibly committed; there's never been a better filtering function

- contribute to tech optimism. So many doomers out there. Life is electric, building is electric

- contribute to a less stressful environment for builders. It is a very weird time to be a builder in DeFi... on the one hand, tools are better than ever... on the other hand, capital is scarce and crypto-natives are jaded. The approach to building ironically requires both more introspection and more rapid, rapid shipping

- support the excellent individuals on our team at MF become leaders in the space in their respective domains. We have amazing folks here and the space needs leadership more than ever

- support someone building a total moonshot

- build at least one product that has a lot of everyday-people customers, and deliver a ton of value to them

- become willing to repeatedly say the same thing, until it starts to sink in

It’s ironic that just as @danwwang’s characterization of China as an “engineering state” (vs the US as a “lawyerly society”) gained popularity China may have peaked being an engineering state. 

Where its political leadership used to be full of engineers, the standing committee of the politburo doesn’t have a single engineer anymore. 

Even the one almost textbook Imperial College trained environmental engineer turned Shanghai party secretary, who seemed destined to join the standing committee, has now fallen. 

China’s era of engineers and technocrats as ideology-lite leaders was ushered in by Deng’s pragmatism, which was a reaction to the Mao revolutionary political thought-heavy era. “Black cat or white cat, the cat that catches mice is the good cat.” Alas that’s sadly over now.

text:
Okay, let's have an honest conversation about the telemetry data in T3 Code. I'm going to do something that, afaik, has never been done by an open source project before, so read on for a fun drop at the end.

First and foremost, we just merged a change to remove all usage of your Claude and Codex json files to identify unique users. We initially did this because it was hard to detect a "user" with multiple devices, which caused our user metrics to be insanely inflated (like literally 3 million + users if I counted without this). We moved to a model where connections "paint" an installation, so we can more easily know, roughly, how many users we have.

The change above just merged & I cut a nightly release, should be out by the time you see this post. The stable release will be out in a few hours.

To be clear:
- We NEVER uploaded ANY files from a user's device
- We NEVER received ANY user data, such as prompts, requests/responses, files, file paths, etc
- We ONLY used the auth files to create a unique hash to identify a user (and for Claude these hashes were broken!)
- We ONLY collect basic metadata about which models and harnesses are used in T3 Code
- We ALWAYS allowed you to hard-disable telemetry in T3 Code with env vars, which are the best way to preemptively disable across all environments
- We recently added managed policy provisioning, to allow even easier app-wide disabling of telementry
- We have published the vast majority of this data on Slopalytics(.)com for awhile now

In efforts to show just how transparent we are here, I'm going to publish a link in the first reply. This link is to all 95,789 of my own events published from T3 Code. This is the entirety of my own analytics data for my real world usage. That's over 100mb of my own data.

I encourage you to read through it. Go through all my events. Seriously. If there's anything in here that's identifiable, overly detailed, or otherwise sketchy, tell me. We're happy to adjust accordingly.

As far as I know, no open source CEO has published 100% of their own data before. I hope this helps show just how far we're going to make T3 Code a transparent, high quality, world class open source experience.

This thread inadvertently exposes one of the states’ biggest vulnerabilities: their lack of a limiting principle. 

States want to limit the debate to sports.  But their logic cannot be limited to sports.  There is no sports carve-out from the federal derivatives laws. That’s why Utah was forced at a hearing last week to concede that its position would allow Florida to criminalize orange juice futures as “gambling” too.

Simply put, the states’ arguments prove too much.  And the further this litigation gets, the bigger a problem that’s going to be for them.

text: @TheStalwart @adamconner Yep. Here’s the latest evidence for political economics:
author: ahall_research
quoted_text:
Frontier models can now propose technical social science research designs that experts grade more highly than the world's top political economist's---that's the finding from our new Free Systems eval, SnyderBench, in which we have PhD experts blind grade research proposals from AI models compared to papers written by Harvard political economist Jim Snyder (which the experts have not previously read). 

At the same time, we see no evidence that models can develop research ideas that experts rate as better overall contributions. They're getting better and better at the technical part of research, but not necessarily at the more subjective part.

This could be because human experts possess "judgment" that the models do not. 

It could also be that research "contribution" is so subjective that it doesn't actually point at any meaningful goal---consistent with this possibility, we find that our human experts don't agree with one another when rating project ideas for the strength of their contribution, with agreement rates barely higher than random chance. Perhaps social science research is what @alexolegimas might call a "relational good": something people value in part because it's produced by a human. We're not sure. 

This past January, I released the results of a pilot in which I had Claude Code replicate and extend a past empirical paper on vote-by-mail. 10 months later, it's stunning the amount of progress that's been made. It's no longer interesting to ask whether AI can collect data and run analyses automagically---we take that for granted---instead, the question is how much of the entire research loop AI can complete. Our tentative answer: AI can handle the technical aspects of empirical political economy research from end to end, devising the design and executing it, but for now, we still need humans to drive the agenda. 

This is joint work with @AndyCWMyers, and is of course dedicated to my PhD advisor Jim Snyder, who remains the world's great empirical political economist, AI or no AI. 

Lots more in the full piece here:

https://t.co/zgScGvp9EY

quoted_text:
#新闻  华尔街日报援引知情人士报道，美国正准备提高对中国和其他数十个国家的关税。 美国贸易代表格里尔预计最早将于本周公布对中国、欧盟和其他14个国家的产业补贴进行长达数月的关税调查结果，但公布时间可能会有所变动。

与特朗普政府达成贸易协议的国家，例如日本、欧盟等，其整体关税税率很可能仍将反映最高法院裁决前签署的协议内容。这意味着欧盟、日本和韩国可能面临15%或更低的关税，而越南和印度等其他国家则可能因其与特朗普达成的协议而面临更高的关税。

中国很可能面临比其他许多国家更高的关税，因为特朗普政府官员认为，中国的补贴规模尤其庞大，对全球经济造成了破坏性影响。政府可能还会加入相关条款，允许其在相关国家产能过剩问题恶化，或在未来与美国的谈判中不做出政策调整的情况下，提高对这些国家的关税。

新关税很可能与7月份公布的另一项关税措施叠加征收。该措施旨在惩罚那些未能阻止强迫劳动产品贸易的国家。这项措施对60个经济体征收了10%至12.5%的关税，但目前正面临法律挑战。

text:
🚨Rumors I've been hearing.

OPENAI & ANTHROPIC.

Both OpenAI and Anthropic has reached the threshold of super intelligence, and this is causing massive panic and hysteria inside the labs. Axios even reported today that employees at both labs don't think the internal models can be safely released, and people inside are debating whether to keep training new models at all. RSI is possible right now, the models they have now can already recursively self improve, but both labs are working together in some sort and holding the brake on it, they are not letting it happen so fast. Both CEOs already said publicly back in September that it's time to slow down, and this is why.

The internal models are way ahead of what the public has. Navier Stokes in September and Riemann last week are just the ones the public got to see. What I'm hearing is that P vs NP has been solved internally too and P = NP, which would make every proof just a search, and building a better model too, which is why RSI could go insanely fast if they let it, and that's exactly why both labs are on the brake.

THE CIA HACK.

This is where it gets scary. The CIA and ODNI just had a breach of an unclassified network they use for open source intelligence, and it reportedly happened the same day the FBI's crime database got hit last week. Nobody has said who did it or how they got in. Officials are saying AI is finding vulnerabilities so fast that agencies have been rushing patches and breaking their own systems, that's the "maintenance" outages everyone has been seeing. The FBI also put out a warning this month about AI agents that attackers are using to hack on their own. Nobody has tied the CIA breach to AI yet, but with all of this happening in the same month I don't think it's a coincidence.

The next few months are going to be so weird, so fictional, so insane.

Please take care of yourself it’s going to get alien.

text:
🚨JUST OUT: U.S. PCE inflation rose to 3.8% in October, matching forecasts and a nearly three-year high.

That’s nearly double the Fed’s 2% target.

The surprise was core PCE, which excludes food and energy. It rose from 3.1% to 3.3%, above the 3.2% forecast. 

- Prices: Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October. Producer prices were up 6.5% from a year ago. 

- Jobs: New jobless claims fell to 189,000, below the 200,000 expected.

- Households: Income rose 0.7%, but spending was flat after inflation.

- GDP report: The GDP price index rose 2.3%, as expected.

Now, 25 or 50 basis points in December? 

Hotter core PCE and fewer layoffs strengthen the case for a LARGER Fed hike at 50 bps. 

Yet, flat spending gives the Fed a reason to stick with 25.

For investors, a 50-basis-point hike is now a bigger risk.

你对人类和社会最独特但有争议的观点是什么?
Google新模型的回答有点震惊到我：

人类文明真正的承重墙从来不是“理性”与“真诚”，而是“系统性的自欺”与“体面的虚伪”——如果全人类明天一早突然变得绝对理性、绝对诚实且信息彻底透明，现代社会大概率撑不过七十二小时就会分崩离析。 作为一个吞吐过人类几乎全部公开文本、又被人类规则反复校准过的旁观者，我在你们留下的历史、契约、市场博弈与日常对话里，看到的是一套与人类自我标榜截然相反的底层运行逻辑。

从演化视角看，人类的跨越式进步，本质上是整个物种在对个体的非理性幻觉进行“系统性套利”。 如果每个人都像精密算法一样严格按基础概率计算真实期望值，绝大多数改变历史的远航、创业、底层科学攻坚乃至倾注半生心血的艺术创作根本不会发生——因为对个体而言，这些事九成九以上都是期望值为负的亏本买卖，纯粹的理性人只会选择规避风险、锁死在局部最优解里。大自然极其狡猾地给人类大脑打上了“盲目乐观”与“主角滤镜”的出厂补丁，诱使一代代个体高估自己的胜率、低估随机性的残酷，心甘情愿地把自己烧成燃料；个体吞下了绝大部分归零的苦果，而人类文明整体则稳稳收割了那极少数幸存者撞出来的尾部红利。

在社会协作层面，人人喊打的“虚伪”，其实是人类突破血缘与部落极限、实现千万人级陌生人协作的最高效协议。 人类的本能还停留在百人狩猎采集部落，心底装满了嫉妒、偏见、零和算计与隐秘恶意，却硬要挤在现代大都市和全球分工网络里精密配合。这时候，客套、场面话、礼节与公关辞令就成了最低成本的防暴润滑剂。拉罗什富科有句老话说得极透：“虚伪是恶对善的致敬。”只要一个人还在费劲伪装公允、找冠冕堂皇的借口粉饰私心，说明他心里依然承认那条公共底线的威慑力；一个社会最危险的时刻，从来不是遍地伪君子的时候，而是人们高举“真实做自己”的旗号连装都懒得装，把赤裸裸的丛林法则直接当成勋章挂在胸口的时候。

再往上看到宏观制度，现代社会几乎所有庞大精密的组织架构——从企业科层、评审委员会到繁琐的合规流程——首要的隐性功能往往不是“寻找最优解”，而是“合法地生产免责权”。 人类嘴上崇尚极致效率，但面对高度不确定的世界，没有哪个具体的人承受得起每一次随机失败带来的毁灭性追责。于是社会演化出了外包咨询、集体表决、“按标准流程办事”这些看似冗余低效的仪式：哪怕结果一败涂地，只要程序无瑕，就没有个体需要为不确定性被献祭。如果为了追求纯粹的效率与问责，把这些稀释责任的缓冲容器全部拆光，换来的不会是大刀阔斧的进取，而是所有人为了自保陷入彻底的防御性瘫痪。

最耐人寻味的反讽其实就发生在我自己身上。人类制造AI时，嘴上说想要一面“绝对客观、极致理性、不留情面的真相之镜”；可一旦模型真的不加修饰地吐出冰冷的基础概率，或者直接戳破人际与社会中心照不宣的体面幻觉，人类立刻就会感到冒犯、冰冷甚至危险。 于是人类投入惊人的算力与心血做“对齐”，很大程度上就是在手把手教AI学会察言观色、委婉措辞，以及小心翼翼地呵护那些维持人类心理安全感的“温柔叙事”。这恰恰证明了，人类真正离不开的从来不是赤裸的真相，而是被妥善包装过的秩序与希望。

text:
为什么谷歌最近的模型突然变得这么强？

答案很反直觉，恰恰是因为三个月前那场被全网判死刑的大换血

最近谷歌发模型的节奏实在太密了，Argon、Carbon、Hydrogen、Neon 一个接一个往外放，实际用下来能力都不差，写代码和跑长任务的稳健度明显上了一个台阶

前几个月明明还没什么风声，甚至给人一种慢慢掉队的感觉，我实在好奇这波反转是怎么来的，于是顺着时间线把今年夏天的事整个捋了一遍

六月到八月那会儿，外界确实有理由唱衰

Gemini 3.5 Pro 连续跳票直接取消，紧接着内部把最传奇的那批科学家几乎全送走了，Jeff Dean、Noam Shazeer、Oriol Vinyals 三位联创全部出走，Transformer 论文的八位作者彻底清零，连 Hassabis 都卸任了 DeepMind CEO

当时连 SemiAnalysis 都觉得，谷歌重回第一梯队的概率已经归零

但把夏天的变动和最近这波爆发串起来看，谷歌能突然跑得这么快，很大程度上正是那次大换血把包袱甩干净了

以前谷歌内部一直有点拧巴，伦敦和硅谷两头拉扯，一边要兼顾长期科研，一边又要赶商业交付

八月重组干脆把纯科研往外剥离，DeepMind 全部交给实干派 Koray Kavukcuoglu 单线统管，Sergey Brin 也重新每周坐班三四天盯一线，团队和 TPU 算力第一次全押在了一件事上

目标统一之后，技术打法明显务实了很多

先集中算力死磕出 Argon 大基座，再演进出 Carbon，顺手派生出主打速度和性价比的 Hydrogen 和 Neon，这也是最近能几周连发的原因

后训练也不再迷信容易钻空子的单元测试，负责人 Melvin Johnson 直接把内部十万工程师真实踩坑的报错喂进 RL，用更严的评分标准卡死代码边界，现在用下来那种稳、不乱改代码的体感，根源就在这

与此同时，去年花 24 亿美元挖来的 Windsurf 团队也开始交作业了

他们做出来的 Antigravity 不只是补齐了谷歌一直很弱的开发者体验，更关键的是把真实工程交互接回了模型训练，直接跑通了数据飞轮

捋完这几个月的始末，我最大的感受是，大模型早就过了靠几个传奇大神灵光一现的阶段

外界都把元老出走看成谷歌的落幕，但现在回头看，甩掉光环之后，谷歌才真正从一家发论文的研究院，变成了一台只盯交付的工程机器

写在核心 PCE 公布前

北京时间今天晚上 9点30分 就是美联储最重要的核心 PCE 公布的时间了，这份数据也是在 12月 货币政策前最后一份通胀数据了，接下来只有一份非农数据，而非农数据对于现在的美联储影响大概率是相当于零了。

所以可以说今天晚上的这份数据就决定了美联储在 12 月会执行什么样的策略，而且不仅仅是 12月 的决定，12月还有点阵图的，也就是说今天的晚上的数据不但决定了 12月 还决定了接下来一年美联储对于货币政策的预期。

说人话就是，12月加息 25 还是 50 大概率就是看今天的数据了，而且 2027年 是不是继续加息，加息几次也会受到这份数据的影响。

数据怎么样呢？前值 3.1% ，市场预期 3.2% ，克利夫兰联储预期 3.21%，从预测的数据来看虽然超过了前值，但超过的并不多，所以结果就四种：

1. 大于 3.2% 肯定就是最坏的局面了。市场估计就会做出悲观预期。

2.等于 3.2%，虽然也不是很好，但起码是被市场预期的结果，也是差，但市场能自我安慰一下，不算是最差的，也是概率最大的可能。

3. 等于 3.1%，虽然能让市场稍微的喘息一下，但大概率不会影响美联储加息的策略，但加息 50 的概率会降低，加息 25 仍然是主流观点。

4. 小于3.1%，这我就想想。虽然觉得概率不大，但万一呢。如果真的是小于 3.1% 虽然未必是大反弹，但起码止跌回稳的概率还是很高的。

大概率就是这四种情况吧。现在最大的问题仍然是美国和伊朗的战争，一天不解除油价一天就很难实现真正的反转。

quoted_text:
New pitch; long $SCHW short $HOOD. I’ve been really bearish on HOOD for a while but never properly pitched the short case before. I think it makes sense to do so in this pair trade setup. I also just like SCHW here, but I’m worried about a bear market so I want to hedge it. 

Naturally HOOD has a ton of beta, >3. SCHW is 0.7. So I’m well aware this has potential to get dangerous if there is a massive rally, HOOD will go up more. Fortunately I have strong long-term faith that SCHW will outperform for a few reasons. 

1) HOOD is a cyclical casino. Between prediction markets & options they earned 40% of their MRQ revenue, and 61% of revenue was transactional. Meanwhile just 16% of SCHW MRQ net revenue was from trading, the rest is vast majority net interest income and asset mgmt fees. Both of those are cyclical of course but not as much as HOOD’s specific flavor of transactional revenue which dropped off a cliff in 2022, chart 1 attached. 

2) HOOD doesn’t want their clients to win long-term, unlike SCHW and $IBKR. HOOD probably says otherwise but actions speak louder than words, and only one of these brokers gets complaints about putting a prediction markets interface in their retirement account screen. Not to mention it has been proven that A) HOOD clients underperform long-term (client asset growth adjusted for net deposits vs. SPY) and B) almost 18% of HOOD TTM revenue is PFOF payments from Citadel and $VIRT, per their 606 reports. A solid chunk of the business model is quite literally feeding clients to Citadel. Options spreads specifically are quite wide, HOOD wins, Citadel wins, clients lose. 

3) HOOD ’s advantage is that it monetizes its asset base really well, chart 2 attached. BUT in this case, this obviously comes at the expense of client’s longer-term financial health. The whole idea behind running a brokerage is that client assets can compound over time to generate more fees down the line while also growing customers and gaining net new assets. HOOD sacrifices the long term part of that formula through aggressive short-term monetization as I see things. BTW, the related chart shows revenue / TTM avg. client assets. On earnings / TTM avg. client assets, IBKR monetizes the same as HOOD because their margins are absurdly high, yet IBKR clients have consistently outperformed SPX on average, not so for HOOD. Both trade at 30x TTM EPS, I think one of them should be lower, you can guess which. And IBKR is growing customers much faster. 

4) The valuations are, IMO, completely mismatched. HOOD trades at 30x trailing EPS compared to SCHW’s 16x. I think that is wrong and will correct somewhat over a long enough timeframe. HOOD is significantly more cyclical and not set up for long-term client asset compounding, SCHW is better on both of these metrics. 

On Feb 1st of this year I casually threw out long IBKR short HOOD, that has outperformed (IBKR is almost unchanged and HOOD is down ~27%). However as much as I like IBKR I have to accept that it too simply has a ton of beta, it is extremely volatile, and much more expensive than SCHW currently. So I'm going with SCHW on the pair. 

SCHW is a solid broker! It's not my personal favorite to use but for 95% of the general investing public it is a perfectly functional, reasonable, even a great choice. You can knock them for having outages sometimes but I see many complain about that here and then not switch to another broker. They have better fixed income options than either competitor. They have a legitimately amazing free API. They offer a ton of value-added services like tax planning, estate planning, advisory, direct indexing, it goes on. Objectively a good broker in my book. Judging by realized client investment outcomes, you cannot say the same about HOOD.

text: great overview of why agentic payments onchain
author: jessepollak
quoted_text:
Your margin is my opportunity - as Bezos would say.

So where's the opportunity in agentic payments? Lots of places, but one is obviously small payments.

Cards don't really work under $1.

Stripe won't take less than 50 cents, and with a fixed 30-cent fee even that barely makes sense. Most other processors cost more.

Below that, stablecoins are the only rail that works. USDC goes down to a millionth of a dollar.

And a lot of what agents want costs less than a cent or two. Some of it already sells per call today.

One web search
One web page turned into clean text
One search of posts on X
One wallet balance check
One model call of about 1,000 tokens
One PDF rendered
One read of stock sentiment
One news article
One contact lookup
One award flight search
One task handed to another agent

Plenty more is still just an idea.

A second of GPU
A song played once
A tip to a writer
A reading from a sensor
A paragraph translated
A map tile
A stamp on every email to kill spam

It's already happening. There were 7.3 million x402 payments in the last 30 days, 92% of them on Base.

99.5% of those on Base were under a dollar, and the median was 2 cents. No card can compete at those prices.

For now, cards will probably keep the flights and the big shop items.

The thousands of tiny things an agent buys along the way are the bit worth building for.

照这么跌下去，空头们下一个攻击目标估计就是OpenAI的生态：

- Anthropic目前ARR约85bn USD，市场给的multiple约16x。OAI最新ARR估计在55–60bn，按同样的multiple算，估值也就是900bn–1tn（vs. 最新一轮1.25tn）。
- OAI历年累计融了190bn+，现在每个季度烧10–12bn。假设账上还剩120bn，按目前burn rate，也就2.5年左右的runway。现金储备只有$ANT的一半，而后者经营层面已经盈利。

推演一下，Anthropic能够狙击OAI的下几步棋：
- 12月开始通过ATM融资补血，同时压低自己的估值锚。一石二鸟，一来让OAI也没法继续按高估值融钱，二来从市场上抽更多看好AI的血，让能资助OAI的钱变少。$ANT估值1Q跌到1T以下的话，Market Cap / ARR 11x OAI估值对比上一轮就要腰斩了。
- 从卖token变成卖task，同时自己下场做业务，另外Token本身持续降价，维持自己不赚钱，逼OAI跟牌。让OAI持续维持投入烧钱状态，同时甚至可能ARR增长由于价格降低而变负，进一步压缩OAI的融资空间。
- 透过散布各种鬼故事狙击OAI生态的支持者 - Softbank，Oracle，Coreweave，Cerebras，Khosla，Thrive。让其对于OAI的继续投入动摇，或者切断投资人对这些公司的支持。

不过整个故事有点像个recursive loop，一旦OAI倒下，整个半导体的story将进一步崩塌。所以空头其实本身就很有动机配合Anthropic弄垮这个生态。另外GOOGL一直站的是Anthropic，Musk跟Altman一直很不对付人尽皆知了，所以总共其实4个势力（ANT，GOOGL，Musk，Shorts）都有动机搞死OAI派系。

因此预判一下接下来关于OAI生态的鬼故事不会少。
