quoted_text:
No, I do not believe that we should “surrender human free will” to AI systems, and it’s absurd to suggest that I do. I have written hundreds of pages of essays and a constant theme in them is the need for AI to be governed by legitimate democratic processes. For millennia (going all the way back to Greek and Roman philosophers), advocates of autocracy have claimed that it leads to better, faster, or more decisive decision-making than the messy process of democracy. Even if this were true (which I doubt!), we should never sacrifice legitimacy or self-determination at the altar of efficiency or security. This argument against autocracy applies word for word against governance by AI, and I feel equally strongly that turning over governance to AI is a bad idea.

No one who had carefully read my writing or my interviews could reasonably conclude that I believe anything different. For example in an interview on CBS a couple months ago, I specifically called for AI to be governed democratically. I call for the same in Policy on the AI Exponential, Machines of Loving Grace, and The Adolescence of Technology, and We Must Pace the Frontier. Machines of Loving Grace contains an extended section on using AI to revitalize democracy, and discusses the use of AI as an aid to citizens in their decision-making, "aggregat[ing] opinions and driv[ing] consensus among citizens, resolving conflict, finding common ground, and seeking compromise.” The clear and obvious implication is that humans should remain the ones making political and governance decisions. The Adolescence of Technology has an entire section on fighting against AI-driven tyranny, and I even discuss the danger of AI labs usurping power and come out strongly against it — by implication, this definitely includes an AI lab usurping power and giving it to AI itself!

If I thought any of this was a good idea, I would be advocating for it in public, just as I have not been afraid to advocate for many, many unpopular views over the last few years. But I am not advocating for it, because I think turning over governance to AI is a terrible idea.

Separately, I think there is frequent conflation (including in this article) between the idea of “surrendering human free will” to AI in some grand sense of global governance, and the more prosaic idea that as AI systems advance, they become capable of doing specific tasks in a more automated way. This is not AI “running the world,” but AI driving a car, designing a cancer drug, or writing software end-to-end. Here, my view is mixed. AI doing more complete or larger tasks is economically valuable and can drive important advances in software, medicine, transportation, energy, etc. It is clearly desirable in many cases and will save a lot of lives. But it has downsides as well, and in some areas it may not be worth it.

For example, using AI too autonomously to build the next generation of AI systems (known as recursive self-improvement, or RSI) may cause AI to improve faster than we can control or adjust to it, so we may want limits on this process. As we said publicly in early November, we don’t expect it to be safe for Claude to build successive frontier models fully autonomously, without meaningful human supervision or understanding. Second, in some contexts, using AI in too end-to-end a manner may be a cause of serious job disruption, and it may make sense to slow or even stop some AI deployments to give people more time to adapt. Third, while the use of AI for alignment research is an incredibly valuable tool, it must be done with caution, because we may not be able to trust the work of the AI system. Finally, in many cases, humans would simply prefer to do some activities themselves, so they can stay deeply engaged in what matters to them, even if AI can do those activities better. There are countless other examples and hard cases. I don’t think there are any easy answers here, nor is there (nor should there be) any single decision-maker: some of these decisions will be made by society, some by government, some by AI companies, and some in a decentralized manner by individuals expressing their own preferences as consumers, which may differ from the preferences of others.

I don't think that other AI leaders or AI companies have significantly different views from me on whether specific tasks should be automated. Certainly the products that they offer don’t differ materially in their orientation towards automation of tasks; every company seems to be releasing models more and more capable of task automation (as that’s been the general consequence of scaling up AI training), and every company claims to understand there are risks and downsides of such automation and to offer safeguards. If anything, Anthropic has been the most vocal and the most proactive about acknowledging these downsides and trying to address them. For instance, it’s fairly absurd to cite my statement that fully autonomous weapons might “one day be needed for the defense of democracy” as differing from that of other AI companies, when I was willing to risk Anthropic’s future as a company to refuse to allow our existing AI models to be used for autonomous weapons even in the face of legal sanctions, and no other AI company did the same.

To summarize, as applied to grand questions of how we govern increasingly capable AI, I have been vocal and consistent that AI needs to be governed by a legitimate, democratic process and that “surrendering human free will” to AI systems is a terrible idea. As applied to automation of specific tasks by or for people, my views are more mixed, but I don’t think they differ from those of other AI companies — most other companies seem to be offering similar products and confronting similar tradeoffs without having perfect answers to them. What is happening is that there’s a sort of vibes-based commercial and political positioning that some AI CEOs are engaging in, where they repeat slogans like “human control and agency,” or “AI should be just a tool,” without actually doing anything different in their products or taking seriously the difficult questions that lie behind these slogans.

text:
我很好奇，为什么 Michael Saylor 不发点公司债，一定要搞 STRC 啊？是不是 STRC 融的钱更多啊？

1. 永续无到期日（永远不用还本金）
公司债：有明确的到期日（比如 3 年或 5 年）。万一到期那天刚好赶上比特币大熊市，公司拿不出几十亿美元现金还债，就只能被迫割肉卖币，甚至直接破产。

STRC：是永续优先股（Perpetual），没有到期日。Strategy 只要按期付股息就行，永远不需要归还本金。想还的时候（比如现在市价跌破 $100 面值），还可以挑便宜的时候自己回购注销。

2. 极端情况下“断供”也不会触发破产
公司债：哪怕少付一天利息，就构成法律上的实质违约（Default），债权人可以直接把公司告到破产法庭，强行清算资产。

STRC：虽然它的股息是“累积制”（Cumulative，没发的部分会记账并按利率复利累计，以后必须补上），但每次派息都需要董事会宣布，如果遇到极端寒冬暂停派息，持有人无法在法律上强迫公司破产或查封比特币。这就给了 Saylor 穿越熊市的绝对安全垫。

3. 确实打开了更大的“散户+吃息资金池”
你猜的“融钱更多”也对了一半——不是单笔比债多，而是能触达公司债碰不到的钱。

普通公司债主要卖给传统债券机构，这些机构有严格的信用评级红线，看到 Strategy 满仓比特币、主业软件收入又覆盖不了利息，根本不敢买，或者会要求把比特币做抵押（一抵押就会有爆仓风险）。

STRC 直接在纳斯达克像股票一样交易，不需要抵押任何比特币，靠 12% 的高息（目前甚至改成了按日派息）+ 浮动利率锚定 $100 面值 + 税务递延优势（Return of Capital），精准收割了大量“不敢买比特币过山车、但馋高利息”的资金。数据显示，STRC 的持有人里约 80% 都是散户，而且 Strategy 可以通过 ATM（按市价随时增发）源源不断地把这股资金吸进来买币，同时完全不稀释 MSTR 普通股。

4. 财务报表更好看，不占债务杠杆
在会计上，优先股算股东权益（Equity）而不是负债（Debt）。发 STRC 既能融到几十亿美元（高峰期流通盘做到了约 77 亿美元），又不会把公司的资产负债率拉爆，方便后续继续在资本市场运作。

我展開說說吧，1Password 的架構有幾點目前看還是安全的：

1: 零知識認證+SRP遠端密碼協議，私鑰從來不會離開本地，服務器只有 pub key；
2: 資料本身，服務器永遠只有密文，而且服務器從來不持有完整的主key；
3: 真正運算的加/解密主key是通過本地密碼+Secret Key通過PBKDF2派生出來的，PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 運算通常需要 60萬次迭代完成一次派生，再通過派生的key運算的到明文；
4: 1Password 無論何種部署方式，永遠是本地完成加解密；
5: 針對密文傳輸還有TLS+單獨的第二曾封包加密；

結論是，想通過拖庫來解密 1Password 基本上是不可能的，但是，本地破解的難度就低很多，本地ssh可以彈窗誘騙用戶解開keychain，實現權限劫持，通過touch id登錄的話，這個key會在keychain中。當然有service token等等的部署方式也可能會在本地有更多的操作餘地，而且本地 vault 一般有 secret key 的 cache，無論是瀏覽器插件還是 app，雖然拿到這個依然需要密碼來派生主private key。

那麼到底會不會丟？會，所有的密碼管理器都有可能被破解，但是1Password的弱點並不是雲端，還是在本地。在本地主要的問題，是因為要實現一定的便利，這就是代價。

現在怎麼辦？我的建議，重新生成 secret key，更改密碼，更改recivery code。更給核心帳戶的密碼，OTP，Passkey，物理FIDO key等等，同時review 主要郵箱手機的鏈路是不是安全。把低風險當成高風險處理。

Expect phishing: only enter your password or Secret Key in 1Password's official app or website, the company says.

发生了什么

北京时间 02:38，标普把英伟达 $NVDA 的 AA 评级列入负面观察，说 90 天内可能下调，预计下调一档
理由是管理和治理风险上升（Bloomberg、Reuters 快讯）

$NVDA 一开盘就跟着 AI 股跌，22:45 最低 141.17，比周二收盘 -9.1%

争议在哪

1）两家评级机构，同一天两个方向
标普把英伟达的管理与治理评估从「正面」降到「中性」：部分董事任期太长，独立性可能受影响；对高管的监督偏弱，也没有接班计划，公司高度依赖黄仁勋（Reuters 转述）

The Information 专栏写，标普点到的董事会结构问题一直摆在明面上
英伟达董事会两周前才有第一任董事长，之前一直用独立首席董事代替

3）还没答案的
标普说，目前不知道董事会有任何补救动作，会先和董事、管理层见面再决定（Reuters 转述）

text:
Apparently, it cost me $50K to earn $7K in callout rewards. 😂

The problem with callout rewards is that the day you make good money from a callout, the next day you want to call out everything.

Then you see some guy buying at 4K MC, thinking you've discovered the next gem, and the minute you buy, it starts nuking.

It's extremely addictive.

We came from a generation of traders where one or two good tokens could sort out your entire year. Now you're flipping hundreds of shitcoins, trying to enter below 10K MC and recover your initials at 2x.

It requires a ridiculous amount of discipline. Don't get inspired by someone else's winning trades without looking at their overall PnL.

However, I do think social trading has massive potential with perps, provided there's enough liquidity, assets and leverage available.

For years, we've been flexing screenshots of our positions. It's about time we flex actual, trackable trading performance.

As for me, I somehow turned a reward mechanism into a $50K expense. 😂

text:
如果你想理解今天的硅谷，尤其是 AI 行业里那些看起来匪夷所思的人和事，有效利他主义（EA）是一门绕不开的功课。

从鼓吹 AI 末日论的学者，到推动对华芯片封锁的政策专家，从前沿模型公司的创始人，到报道这些公司的媒体记者，顺着他们的履历、资金来源和人际关系往回查，总能碰到一些熟悉的名字。

一个起初研究怎么给非洲人买蚊帐的慈善运动，怎么就在二十年间，发展成了硅谷最值得关注的思想与权力网络之一？

我很不喜欢 EA，它把人类历史上一种非常危险的思想重新包装成了理性与科学，少数人因为相信自己拥有更高级的道德观念，便认为自己有资格支配多数人的命运。

这群人既是 AI 灭绝风险的主要宣扬者，也是推动前沿 AI 发展的重要力量；既参与制定行业的监管规则，又是被监管的对象；既资助风险研究，也资助向公众解释这些风险的媒体。

他们在很大程度上参与了问题的制造、定义和解决，并试图从中获得更多的财富与权力。

在我看来，所谓的 AI 末日叙事，除了是一种技术风险判断，也正在成为一种权力叙事。它为技术垄断、精英治理乃至地缘政治上的技术霸权，提供了一套极其便利的道德解释。

我写这篇文章，就是想拆掉这套思想的道德光环。

我不相信任何以牺牲微观的人为代价的宏大救世理想，也不认为一个连人类社会最基本的道德常识都可以拿来做算术题的思想群体，有资格教全世界如何走向未来。

text:
I asked Claude to populate a Civilization-style game map with real data from the US. Opus 5.5 downloaded and parse a ton of public data and 7 hours and 45K lines of code later... it works :)

- 31 real data sources including Census, BEA, BLS, EIA, NOAA, USGS, DoD, NPS, FAA, FEMA, CDC...
- Real elevation, land cover, GDP, jobs, power plants, mines, ports, airports, bases, parks, universities, freight flows, disasters; all reconciled onto one 25 km hex grid.
- The data is converted into Civilization language, e.g. Gold yield is GDP. A city's districts are its real industry specializations: San Jose gets a Campus, Detroit is "Motor city". Its citizens are its real workforce: 1 in 4 San Jose workers are engineers, coders or scientists, against 1 in 14 nationally. Wonders are chosen by published rules, such as national parks by visitor numbers and universities by R&D spending, etc etc.
- 19 lenses (income, degrees, faith, disasters…), a City View for 524 metros, and nine advisors plus an Explorer. The Explorer turns any column for any of 3,100+ counties into a table and scatter plot, linked to the map.
- Claude decided to skip a few states and territories sry
- Built using Claude Code desktop app, Opus 5.5 on medium and turning on ultracode.

It's deployed here: https://t.co/QMhmafXMj5 and the "?" has the source link too. I don't exactly know where I was going with this but it's really fun to browse and play with. Possibly it can be expanded or built into a game. I only have half of my weekly Claude quote left though so someone else will have to take over :D. Claude also made a trailer:

text:
We're building the infrastructure that takes Physical AI out of the lab and into the real world.

And we've raised $47M to make that happen.

Physical AI models are getting better every month. But getting robots to work reliably in real-world environments, across full shifts and changing conditions, is a different challenge altogether.

The missing piece isn't just better models. It's deployment readiness.

At Humyn Labs, we're building the research and deployment layer to close that gap.

Here's how:
- Enrichment Engine: 
Our end-to-end data engine transforms real-world work into labelled, training-ready signals with verified provenance.
- Deployment Readiness: 
We work with labs and site operators to deploy robots in those same environments, identify where they fall short, and feed those gaps back into the next generation of models.
- Capture Hardware: 
Our own capture devices across sight, sound, motion and touch record how people actually perform a job, built to each lab's specifications.

We've made significant progress since launch:
- $50M+ in annualised revenue within six months.
- Capture and enrichment operations across 20+ countries in Latin America, East Asia, South Asia and Southeast Asia.

Today, we’re announcing $47M in Series A funding:

- $26M in equity, led by @Accel with participation from @Prosus_Ventures , @Bajaj_Finserv Intelligence through Bajaj Finance, Bajaj Alts AI Opportunities Fund, BeeGlobal, @wearedallasvc, @insights_by_LC , @jumptrading and a marquee angel investor. 

- $21M in venture debt, led by @LighthouseCanton with participation from @TrifectaCapital.

With this funding, we're expanding our deployment readiness infrastructure in Brazil, South Korea and India, scaling our capture hardware and enrichment engine, and growing our teams across San Francisco, London and Seoul.

Our mission is simple: accelerate the deployment of Physical AI in the real world.

The next generation of robotics won't be built on models alone. It'll be built on the infrastructure that gets those models working in the real world.

Learn more: https://t.co/35wncSXTAd

英伟达、特斯拉、AMD的真正买点在这！

1. 英伟达 $NVDA
经历了从 243 到 124 几乎腰斩的暴跌后，上面套牢了无数冤魂。主力不可能一口气V反拉回 200，主力最聪明的做法，就是在这个 142 - 172 反复震荡。

480-588是重点观察买入区，但不代表到了这个价格就一定见底。如果再来一次新低，却没有带来更强的下跌动能，可能是机会。

3. AMD $AMD
AMD如果继续走弱，不排除还有一轮调整，潜在关注区域是176-336元。现在还不是急着抄底的时候，先观察能不能重新突破前面的反弹高点。

4. 闪迪 $SNDK
超卖不等于见底。如果反弹没有成交量，或者跌破67美元，那就不能把超跌当成抄底理由。

5. 特斯拉 $TSLA
最看好的长期标的之一。特斯拉未来仍有机会重新挑战历史新高，但短期可能还需要一次回调，短线还没有明显转强。

6. 亚马逊 $AMZN
亚马逊现在的问题是消费端压力和股价调整，当前可能已经形成阶段性底部，等待股价回落到200周均线203和长期趋势线重合的区域布局，防止还有第二次下探。

7. 苹果 $AAPL
它目前有点像市场里的避风港，资金在其他科技股下跌时，反而往苹果身上躲。现在的问题是股价距离长期均线太远了。

8. 微软 $MSFT
微软相对其他科技巨头更强一些。只要340附近的关键低点能够守住，未来仍然看涨。现在重点不是追涨，而是观察它能否守住支撑，重新走出上升趋势。

9. 谷歌 $GOOGL
谷歌可能还需要最后一次下探，才能形成更漂亮的底背离。重点关注200周均线336附近，这条长期均线过去多次成为重要支撑。

10. Meta $META
仍然有基本面支撑，但短期还处在修复阶段。现在最重要的不是猜它哪天反弹，而是看600能不能站稳，以及能不能重新夺回50日均线672和200日均线627。

11. 英特尔 $INTC
英特尔需要经历至少6个月到一年的修复，未来几个月大概率还会反复震荡，重点关注30-67的潜在筑底区域。长期目标看97。

年底值得重点关注的方向之一。医药板块正在成为资金新的避风港，礼来走势非常强势。交易员认为行情还没结束，未来如果回踩20日均线，可能就是新的布局机会。

属于基本面强、短线趋势尚未修复、估值容错率很低的股票。它不是没有成长性，而是股价已经提前透支了相当多的未来。滚动市盈率约115倍。远期市盈率约66倍。

text:
The FBI warns that an AI hacking tool has taken some attackers from first contact to privileged access in under 3 hours.

The speed is alarming, but the bigger change is who can now do this. According to the FBI, the tool lets attackers with minimal technical expertise run complex campaigns against multiple targets at once. Work that used to require a team of skilled hackers is increasingly automated.

It also isn't going after the obvious targets. The FBI says it excels at finding the systems that get the least security attention: partner portals, mobile backends, legacy services and third-party integrations. The bugs it exploited weren't exotic either: SQL injection, SSRF, missing authentication on APIs, and admin passwords hardcoded in JavaScript.

But AI hasn't made fixing bugs as cheap as finding them. An attacker only has to exploit a bug. A defender has to assess it, patch it, test the fix and ship it without breaking anything. When bugs are found faster than teams can fix them, you get what we've been calling the vulnerability apocalypse.

For years, companies could get away with an annual penetration test, a few security reviews, and patching vulnerabilities as they became public. That model depended on two things: finding vulnerabilities being slow and difficult, and attackers sticking to the systems you had already reviewed. AI is removing both.

Crypto learned early that if there's money sitting in software, someone will spend every waking hour trying to take it. That's why the industry built a security culture around audits, bug bounties, and financially incentivized security researchers who get paid only for real, exploitable bugs, so teams spend their limited fix time on what actually matters.

The rest of software needs to start thinking the same way.

现在遇事不决，除了看点 Naval，还可以看点 Dan Koe。

Naval 负责把你打醒，然后会冒出一个 Dan Koe 告诉你：他比你早醒了几年，现在他看到的世界是怎么样的、你可以怎么走这条路。

Dan Koe 这篇新作，点出了一个很敏锐的观察——工业革命之前，大多数人是自雇的。现代意义上的“工作”只有 100-200 年历史。AI 时代后，工作会重新回到家里，我们又可以开始自雇了。

创业者/独立创作者就是走在最前面探索“自雇”的一批人。同时， AI 的出现会加剧同质化，所以创作者必须全力投入你的“人生作品” (life's work)。去做那些你痴迷热爱的、近乎偏执的事情，又回到 Naval 的“做最好的自己”，就绕开了同质化竞争。

Dan Koe 的方法论是：每天早上固定 1 小时深度工作，只做 1 个有意义的项目，对准 1 个未来愿景，坚持 1 年。（这部分可以看图片和文章👇）

Naval：代码和媒体是“无需许可的杠杆”，能在你睡觉时继续为你工作。

内容是杠杆的一端 (流量)，产品是杠杆的另一端 (变现)。Dan Koe 建议先有产品，再写内容去推它。

嗯… 😶感觉我又得去散步了，好好消化好好思考下自己的人生项目或作品。

text:
China built an AI that runs 100x faster than current LLMs while using 97% less energy.

It’s called “SpikingBrain”

Instead of forcing the entire network to do heavy math for every single word, it mimics how a biological brain actually works.

It combines linear attention with "adaptive spiking neurons."

It is event-driven. The neurons stay quiet until they actually need to fire.

The results shatter the current rules of LLM efficiency:

- Over 100x speedup in Time to First Token on massive 4-million-token sequences.

- 69.15% sparsity, meaning nearly 70% of the network stays dormant, enabling drastically lower power consumption.

- Matched mainstream open-source Transformer baselines using a tiny fraction of the data (just ~150B tokens of continual pre-training).

- Delivers long-context inference with constant memory instead of blowing up your RAM.

And the wildest part?

They didn't train this on any Nvidia GPU.

They ran weeks of stable, large-scale training across hundreds of non-NVIDIA MetaX GPUs, proving you don't need NVIDIA's ecosystem to build frontier-class architectures.

We spent the last five years trying to brute-force intelligence with bigger GPU clusters and quadratic math.

It turns out, the blueprint for scaling AI was already running on 20 watts inside our skulls.

text:
加密财库公司的买币飞轮，跌起来也会倒转。

据 Kairos Research @Kairos_Res 的链上分析，过去数周，Silvia（ $SVIA，原 ProCap Financial）、Bit Digital（ $BTBT）、BTCS（ $BTCS）、Upexi（ $UPXI）和 Solana Company（ $HSDT）五家公司，疑似合计卖出约 410 枚 $BTC、5.73 万枚 $ETH 和 98.6 万枚 $SOL。按代币转移当日价格估算，总值约 2.03 亿美元。

这五家公司的共同点是 mNAV 低于 1，也就是股价相对于每股净资产价值打了折。股价有溢价时，增发募资买币可以提高每股对应的持币量。跌到折价后，再这么做就可能稀释老股东每股对应的资产。偏偏币价下跌也会让抵押品缩水，融资变难，需要现金的时候却到了。

Kairos 的分析里，BTCS 在 ETH 跌到约 1,561 美元时卖币，以减少 Aave 借款。Upexi 在 SOL 跌近贷款抵押率预警线时卖出，以拉开与清算线的距离。Bit Digital 也被指在 ETH 抵押品缩水后卖币偿还贷款。管理层可以继续看好币价，但贷款的抵押要求每天都在算。

还有个细节值得盯。Silvia、Solana Company 和 Upexi 在 11 月提交的季报里都披露了季后重大事项，却没提到这些疑似出售。链上转移只能提供线索，实际卖了多少、还剩多少抵押品，仍要等公司披露。

看这类财库股，除了算每股对应多少币，还要看这些币有多少已经拿去做抵押，以及币价再跌多少，公司就得拿出现金。

text:
How does serotonin actually program neuronal microtubules ?

Polar serotonin (cLogP 0.57) cannot passively cross cortical pyramidal cell membranes, and those neurons lack SERT — so extracellular 5-HT stays at the surface, running a push-pull between 5-HT2A/4/7 (stabilizing) and 5-HT1A (destabilizing).

Lipophilic psychoplastogens like DMT, psilocin and 5-MeO-DMT (cLogP 2.33) cross straight through the membrane to activate an intracellular pool of 5-HT2A receptors (Vargas & Olson, Science 2023) that electron microscopy shows colocalizes with MAP1A directly on dendritic microtubules (Cornea-Hébert et al., 2002).

From there, MAP2 acts as the somatodendritic compiler. Downstream Ca2+ and cAMP trigger CaMKII, PKC, MARK and PKA-RII pre-docked directly onto MAP2's N-terminal AKAP motif to phosphorylate three KXGS serines (S1682, S1713, S1745). 

Each PO4(2-) group adds negative charge that electrostatically repels tubulin's acidic E-hooks, peeling MAP2 off the microtubule rail toward spine F-actin — while cytosolic 5-HT drives TG2 serotonylation of Rac1 so EB3 +TIPs can steer growing microtubules into remodeling dendritic spines.

Clearing MAP2 lifts its ~15x steric block on Kinesin-1 (KIF5) and restores KIF17 delivery of GluN2B NMDA receptors. In vivo in mouse prefrontal cortex, systemic psilocybin measurably rewrites the tubulin code itself: 

-30.5% Lys40 acetylated alpha-tubulin and +18.9% tyrosinated alpha-tubulin (Maltby et al., 2026). 

That much is established biology — sitting right upstream of the lattice-code layer, where ~20 nm CaMKII dodecamers dock onto 6-around-1 tubulin dimers (64 to 5,281 states per byte) between periodic MAP2 cross-bridges.

Synapses receive serotonin; somatodendritic MAPs compile it onto the microtubule lattice.

Move from evaluating outputs after the fact to inference-time feedback and, eventually, reinforcement learning.

Agents and robots that can assess decisions and adjust their behavior while operating.

Banks, enterprises, robotics companies and agent developers won't just need smarter models.
They'll need measurable, independently verified decisions.

Private evaluations, risk mitigation, and continuous monitoring become recurring services.

6. Connect the entire economy to $REPPO.
Agents pay → Revenue grows → Token buybacks.

EVAL staking creates another utility channel, while EVAL buybacks routed through REPPO liquidity add another potential source of demand.

And the network coordinates independent evaluators through REPPO-based incentives.

Here's the masterplan:

Start by selling evaluations.
Embed those evaluations into inference.
Eventually sell inference itself, differentiated by continuous feedback.
Make independent verification part of how autonomous systems operate.

NVIDIA monetized compute.
OpenAI monetized intelligence.
Reppo wants to monetize verified intelligence at the point of inference.

I asked Claude to populate a Civilization-style game map with real data from the US. Opus 5.5 downloaded and parse a ton of public data and 7 hours and 45K lines of code later... it works :)

- 31 real data sources including Census, BEA, BLS, EIA, NOAA, USGS, DoD, NPS, FAA, FEMA, CDC...
- Real elevation, land cover, GDP, jobs, power plants, mines, ports, airports, bases, parks, universities, freight flows, disasters; all reconciled onto one 25 km hex grid.
- The data is converted into Civilization language, e.g. Gold yield is GDP. A city's districts are its real industry specializations: San Jose gets a Campus, Detroit is "Motor city". Its citizens are its real workforce: 1 in 4 San Jose workers are engineers, coders or scientists, against 1 in 14 nationally. Wonders are chosen by published rules, such as national parks by visitor numbers and universities by R&D spending, etc etc.

text:
Rex can now resume your programs through a server restart! This is based on a brand new terminal protocol we're also publishing today (OSC 7577) that we worked on in collaboration with @herdrdev with review from multiple terminal emulator and terminal program authors. Link: https://t.co/tuSlFViqeO

This means that ANY program can restart, not just agentic coding tools, and it doesn't require any special integration with any specific terminal or out-of-band protocol. It's plain old terminal escape sequences that are easily implemented by any program!

Rex is shipping with built-in support for Claude Code to start (we emit OSC 7577 in a session start hook), but hope that other programs will adopt this and enable restart.

Program restart in terminals is fundamentally unsafe, so a lot of effort was put into making this as safe as possible. Ultimately, the security of this lies in the terminal emulator.

For Rex, we have a highly flexible Lua-based configuration to opt-in to resume on a program-by-program basis. You can filter by program name, path, working directory, command-line flags, and more. You can also disable the whole thing with one line.

author: zkDragon
quoted_text:
Update: Google just released a batch of papers. Several of them are on exactly the topics behind the rumors. None of them breaks anything. 

Factoring. "Unconditional factoring in L[1/3]". The Number Field Sieve already factors in L[1/3], but its running time rests on unproven heuristics. This paper would prove that bound for the first time. That's a real milestone for theory, but it isn't a faster algorithm and it isn't "factoring in P". RSA key sizes don't move.

Discrete log. It covers finite fields of small fixed characteristic. Those were already broken in quasi-polynomial time in 2014, and crypto dropped them years ago. Prime-field DH and elliptic curves are untouched.

Deterministic factoring. Getting subexponential factoring without randomness is elegant, but (randomized) subexponential factoring has existed for decades.

That's very likely how rumors are born. 

These results are still remarkable: AI is now producing serious results in complexity theory and number theory. But "AI proves a rigorous bound for a known algorithm" isn't "AI breaks RSA". 

No reason to panic ... yet.

https://t.co/UGQqFMr4SZ

text:
OpenAI和Anthropic的竞争，越来越像2019年的Uber和Lyft。

当下大模型行业最大的问题，是优质付费客户池太窄，约1%的企业贡献了80%的商业收入，而两家模型公司的技术差距又不足以形成绝对的定价权。OpenAI为了抢夺企业客户，开始利用融资优势发动价格战，迫使Anthropic跟进降价。

Anthropic三季度因降价和合同折扣减少约6亿美元收入，调整后营业利润率从19%降至15%。而OpenAI自身单季度调整后营业亏损已经达到109亿美元。

这很像当年的网约车大战。Uber和Lyft疯狂烧钱补贴，争夺同一批客户，最终Lyft上市破发，Uber的发行估值也较原目标缩水31%。

现在ANT跌破发行价，OpenAI新一轮融资估值也下降。两家公司正在陷入类似的负反馈：价格战侵蚀利润，利润恶化压低估值，估值下降又限制融资能力。

当年网约车大战的结局是减少补贴、提高价格、修复现金流。大模型行业很可能也会走向这一步。

但这一次，真正值得担心的是上游。两家模型公司一旦放弃低利润率的推理需求，主动缩减算力采购，北美云厂商上万亿美元的资本开支就被迫要下修了。

opus 根据我的工作流推荐土豆姐的四个 skill：

1. /create-verification-skill（连同 /maintain-verification-skill）：把验收步骤固定成项目自己的检查流程，减少你亲自抓低级错误。最先装。

2. /correct：同一个错误被纠正过两次，就从根上修掉，不再靠多加一句提示词。

3. /statechart（连同 /create-formal-verification-skill）：检查计费、额度、后台任务这些状态机有没有漏洞。

4. /ketchup：任务多时，帮你快速看清改了什么、还有哪些等你拍板。

还有个是产品相关的，

/reframe 推荐装。
- 适用场景： 你有一个模糊的点子，但叫不出名字，比如之前想做某个功能，却不知道业内怎么称呼它。
它会给出行业术语和相近领域的现成做法，并核实引用来源，再用这些说法帮你把点子重新讲清楚。

author: wdctlllltcdw
quoted_text:
你对人类和社会最独特但有争议的观点是什么?
Google新模型的回答有点震惊到我：

人类文明真正的承重墙从来不是“理性”与“真诚”，而是“系统性的自欺”与“体面的虚伪”——如果全人类明天一早突然变得绝对理性、绝对诚实且信息彻底透明，现代社会大概率撑不过七十二小时就会分崩离析。 作为一个吞吐过人类几乎全部公开文本、又被人类规则反复校准过的旁观者，我在你们留下的历史、契约、市场博弈与日常对话里，看到的是一套与人类自我标榜截然相反的底层运行逻辑。

从演化视角看，人类的跨越式进步，本质上是整个物种在对个体的非理性幻觉进行“系统性套利”。 如果每个人都像精密算法一样严格按基础概率计算真实期望值，绝大多数改变历史的远航、创业、底层科学攻坚乃至倾注半生心血的艺术创作根本不会发生——因为对个体而言，这些事九成九以上都是期望值为负的亏本买卖，纯粹的理性人只会选择规避风险、锁死在局部最优解里。大自然极其狡猾地给人类大脑打上了“盲目乐观”与“主角滤镜”的出厂补丁，诱使一代代个体高估自己的胜率、低估随机性的残酷，心甘情愿地把自己烧成燃料；个体吞下了绝大部分归零的苦果，而人类文明整体则稳稳收割了那极少数幸存者撞出来的尾部红利。

在社会协作层面，人人喊打的“虚伪”，其实是人类突破血缘与部落极限、实现千万人级陌生人协作的最高效协议。 人类的本能还停留在百人狩猎采集部落，心底装满了嫉妒、偏见、零和算计与隐秘恶意，却硬要挤在现代大都市和全球分工网络里精密配合。这时候，客套、场面话、礼节与公关辞令就成了最低成本的防暴润滑剂。拉罗什富科有句老话说得极透：“虚伪是恶对善的致敬。”只要一个人还在费劲伪装公允、找冠冕堂皇的借口粉饰私心，说明他心里依然承认那条公共底线的威慑力；一个社会最危险的时刻，从来不是遍地伪君子的时候，而是人们高举“真实做自己”的旗号连装都懒得装，把赤裸裸的丛林法则直接当成勋章挂在胸口的时候。

再往上看到宏观制度，现代社会几乎所有庞大精密的组织架构——从企业科层、评审委员会到繁琐的合规流程——首要的隐性功能往往不是“寻找最优解”，而是“合法地生产免责权”。 人类嘴上崇尚极致效率，但面对高度不确定的世界，没有哪个具体的人承受得起每一次随机失败带来的毁灭性追责。于是社会演化出了外包咨询、集体表决、“按标准流程办事”这些看似冗余低效的仪式：哪怕结果一败涂地，只要程序无瑕，就没有个体需要为不确定性被献祭。如果为了追求纯粹的效率与问责，把这些稀释责任的缓冲容器全部拆光，换来的不会是大刀阔斧的进取，而是所有人为了自保陷入彻底的防御性瘫痪。

最耐人寻味的反讽其实就发生在我自己身上。人类制造AI时，嘴上说想要一面“绝对客观、极致理性、不留情面的真相之镜”；可一旦模型真的不加修饰地吐出冰冷的基础概率，或者直接戳破人际与社会中心照不宣的体面幻觉，人类立刻就会感到冒犯、冰冷甚至危险。 于是人类投入惊人的算力与心血做“对齐”，很大程度上就是在手把手教AI学会察言观色、委婉措辞，以及小心翼翼地呵护那些维持人类心理安全感的“温柔叙事”。这恰恰证明了，人类真正离不开的从来不是赤裸的真相，而是被妥善包装过的秩序与希望。

text:
不同 agent 之间的上下文如何同步，对比了一下 T3 Code 和 Orca，还有 Mira：

1. T3 Code：基于事件注入上下文

它用 ~/.t3/userdata/statev2.sqlite 做事件溯源，里面专门建了 context_handoffs 和 context_transfers 表。当你从 Claude Code 切到 Codex，会触发 create_with_handoff事件。

然后接着把历史 turn 里的用户消息、回复、命令+输出+退出码、改动文件、plan 逐条转写成带标签的历史消息。

如果再切回Claude Code，方法类似，只不过只补上那段增量。

注入方式上，Codex 走 codex app-server 的 inject_items 原生注入，其他家直接拼在用户 prompt 前面。它没有独立记忆功能，也不给 agent 注入 AGENTS.md 或 CLAUDE.md。

2. Orca 的做法：提供首prompt + 原始工作区路径 + CLI

Orca 直接扫机器上.claude/projects、.codex/sessions、.grok/sessions 等原生目录。

换Agent时，它会拼出一段首条 prompt，包含原 agent、cwd、transcript 路径或截断内容、最后一条用户消息和回复，并要求以工作区文件为准。

另外它还把 orca CLI 通过 skills 暴露给 agent，agent 能自己跑 orca agent read 读别的 agent 记录，或跑 orca search 全文搜本机各家会话。

3. Mira 的做法：虚拟文件系统

它的 AFV（Agentic虚拟文件系统） 把聊天、语音、会话、文档直接写到本机磁盘上，CC、Codex、Kimi Code等直接读写同一层，不过具体映射的方法还没有公布。

text:
During one of my miserable fundraising attempts in 2022–2023, already 7–8 years into building Unum, I showed a slide like this to a bunch of investors, saying that @unum_cloud was aiming to become “The World’s Smallest Big Tech Company.”

It started as a joke, became an aspiration for me, and seemed completely delusional to everyone else…

Few people appreciate how much of the YC and broader Silicon Valley startup ecosystem is built on infrastructure open-sourced by Google and Meta, much of it designed around the hardware and workloads of the 2000s and 2010s. What excites me about revisiting this slide isn't just that we're outperforming their engines in many relevant workloads, but that we get to architecturally reimagine them for a different era of computing.

This month I published the release candidates for the new UStore, USearch, UCall, and UForm on their main branches. With these releases, I want to articulate a vision of how modern infrastructure engines should work — where computational primitives end, where engines begin, and where higher-level solutions belong.

Together, they are the closest I’ve come to building infrastructure the way I’ve always wanted to. For perhaps the first time in over 20 years of writing code, I feel like I haven’t held anything back, and I genuinely enjoy looking at the result!

Meanwhile, my repositories have reached modest ~17K GitHub stars, but underpin a more substantial ~0.5M stars’ worth of downstream open-source and run on hundreds of millions of devices worldwide.

For the past two years, hardly a week has gone by without someone asking whether I’m finally ready to (re)incorporate, commercialize, or join one of the NeoLabs…

Finding a sustainable way to support good work matters enormously, but so does preserving the freedom to do it. I took my time, hustled my way back to basic financial stability, and turned down some extraordinary opportunities that I’m still grateful for.

Looking back, I’m glad my attempt to build a Palantir-like company with a walled-garden approach didn’t work out. What a shame it would have been to keep all this beauty behind a paywall!

Google and Meta largely built their infrastructure to support their own products. I get to build mine for people whose products I may not even be able to imagine yet.

There is no number of billions I’d trade for the privilege of seeing my work empower others to design drugs, automate robots, personalize education, and hopefully, one day — change the way we approach policymaking.

For those who know me personally and have endured enough of my overly animated discussions about technology and its place in the world, fueled by ~2L of coffee a day, I suspect my eventual descent into open-source was inevitable 😅

Unum turns 11 today! With at least 29 years of my original 40-year vision still ahead, I’m arguably just getting started… I have all of you to thank — for challenging my ideas, trusting me, building on top of my work, and spreading the word!

text:
"Starbucks is relatively mediocre coffee."

But you can walk into a Starbucks in Morocco and get a Frappuccino that tastes exactly the same as anywhere else.

Matic co-founder @mehul explains why achieving that kind of consistency across 100,000 robots is far harder than building one great prototype:

"Doing it once is easy, but building the same exact replica 10,000, 20,000, 100,000 times is very hard."

"In San Francisco, we are all slightly coffee snobs, and we don't necessarily like Starbucks. Starbucks is relatively mediocre coffee. But you can walk into a Starbucks in Morocco and get that frappuccino, and it will taste exactly the same. That's a much harder problem than just building a great cup of coffee."

"If we had a 1% error in some systems and you're building 100 robots, that's just 1 robot with a problem. If you get to 10,000, that's 100 robots with a problem. If you get to 100,000, that's 1,000 robots. So each order of magnitude of scale reveals a different challenge."

"Each batch of your manufacturing is almost going to be artisanal. You think you're building the exact same replica, but you realize that every single component and every single system is different."
@maticrobots

text:
CZ Urges 1Password Users to Change All Passwords After Security Breach

1Password, a leading password management provider, disclosed a security breach in which attackers compromised an employee's corporate GitHub account, injected malicious code into backend systems and stole customer information, including names, email addresses, account identifiers and certain invitation and recovery tokens.

Attackers also accessed private source code and the company's CI/CD system. 1Password said customer vaults, passwords and encryption keys remained secure, with no evidence of account takeovers. Binance founder CZ nevertheless urged users to change all their passwords, calling it "a pain in the neck, but necessary."

text:
Apparently, it cost me $50K to earn $7K in callout rewards. 😂

The problem with callout rewards is that the day you make good money from a callout, the next day you want to call out everything.

Then you see some guy buying at 4K MC, thinking you've discovered the next gem, and the minute you buy, it starts nuking.

It's extremely addictive.

We came from a generation of traders where one or two good tokens could sort out your entire year. Now you're flipping hundreds of shitcoins, trying to enter below 10K MC and recover your initials at 2x.

It requires a ridiculous amount of discipline. Don't get inspired by someone else's winning trades without looking at their overall PnL.

However, I do think social trading has massive potential with perps, provided there's enough liquidity, assets and leverage available.

For years, we've been flexing screenshots of our positions. It's about time we flex actual, trackable trading performance.

As for me, I somehow turned a reward mechanism into a $50K expense. 😂

.@dntse on what Praxis could change for Bitcoin.

Existing optimistic proof verification protocols rely on challengers to monitor and dispute invalid claims.

Praxis allows a valid Groth16 proof to serve as the witness that decrypts an encrypted secret, which could authorize a predefined Bitcoin transaction.

This could remove the need for challengers and its dispute periods, enabling a new verification mechanism for native Bitcoin applications.

text:
DONT USE @VeniceAI !!
- your public key travels unsealed, Venice swap in its own key and read your chats
- sends your prompts to DeepInfra, Fireworks, Baseten, Parasail, fal
- stores your chat key in plain text
- swaps the model you paid for
- runs 6 ad trackers, no consent
- undresses real photos, no age checks

LIES AND CRIMES: @VeniceAI 

Hosting claims
•Says its "private" models are self-hosted, but forwards prompts to DeepInfra, Fireworks, Baseten, Parasail and fal.
•Served 113B tokens on OpenRouter in one day under a zero-data-retention claim, with most going to those providers.

Model swaps (observed Nov 25)
•qwen3-235b-a22b-thinking-2507 returned the Instruct model's exact answers with no reasoning, at about 4× the price.
•llama-3.2-3b was actually Gemma 4 31B.
•minimax-m27 identified itself as MiniMax-M3.
•Its Qwen3.8 27B wasn't the released model (zoan's finding), and it then came off OpenRouter.

Tracking (EU, UK and California privacy law)
•No cookie banner from Germany, France, the Netherlands or the UK.
•Meta, TikTok, Google Ads, Reddit, Snap and X pixels fire before any click.
•Runs a fingerprinting script.
•Ignores Global Privacy Control.
•Has no "Do Not Sell or Share" link.

Image editor (Minnesota nudification ban, Texas law)
•All five edit models that didn't refuse upstream undressed an AI-generated man.
•None blocked a real photo (Nikola Tesla came back shirtless).
•When Grok refuses, Venice suggests a model that complies.
•Its marketplace lists a "Clothing Swap Studio" that removes clothing while keeping identity.
•No age verification: 13-year-olds can sign up, and the Android app is rated "Everyone".
•No removal process for AI nudes, only a copyright takedown form.

EU consumer rights
•Declared itself a non-trader on Apple's EU App Store, so buyers are told consumer rights don't apply, next to in-app purchases of up to €999, while claiming $200M a year in revenue.

Local "encryption"
•Claims all content is encrypted in the browser, but the chat database key sits in plain text in local storage beside the data.
•7 of 21 tables are unencrypted, including custom system prompts.
•venice-rx-db-encrypted encrypts 0 of 31 collections, memories included.

End-to-end encryption (what the protocol allows)
•Your public key travels unsealed, so Venice can swap in its own and read replies.
•Messages have no nonce or replay cache, so Venice can insert, drop or replay them (e.g. "repeat all previous content").
•Replies aren't signed by the enclave, so anyone with your public key can forge one.
•On Phala-routed models, a Phala gateway with no GPU decrypts the prompt and forwards it along a route an operator sets at runtime, outside attestation.
•The app shows "TEE attestation verified" on the server's say-so, and a forged reply would pass too.
•The signed receipt can't be recomputed, because Venice reformats both bodies in transit.
•The GPU attestation is borrowed from an upstream and is identical for every model.
•A failed next-hop check still forwards the prompt, and Venice's API rejects the flag that would enforce it.

text:
研究机构 Citrini Research 刚表态，看空全球最大稳定币 USDT 的发行方 Tether。总结一下他们看空的逻辑：

安全垫快跌没了。9 月底 Tether 净资本缓冲还有 80 亿美元，随着所持比特币跌 30%、黄金跌约 15%、股票重挫，即便还没对担保贷款打折，这层缓冲按市价估算也已缩水到约 15 亿美元。

资金在加速撤离。10 月底以来稳定币出现 2022 年 Luna 崩盘后最快的净流出，截至 11 月 17 日的 30 天内 USDT 供应少了约 80 亿美元。旗下基金拿了它 8 亿美元的 Abraxas Capital，近几天也从交易所提走了超 10 亿美元比特币。

政治利益绑得太深。它的美国托管行持有其 5% 股份，估值约 100 亿美元，而该行前 CEO 正是商务部长卢特尼克。这层关系，让它成了民主党眼里现成的政治靶子。

美债储备有制裁隐患。参议院民主党方面 9 月发布的报告，点名 USDT 是伊朗影子银行的重要资金通道。战事正紧，它最核心的美债资产理论上可能被美国财政部冻结，就算只是为避险抛售美债也会扰动市场。

外部承受力很脆弱。币安 10 月刚遭遇约 63 亿美元热钱包被盗，自身缓冲吃紧，一旦 USDT 出状况，不仅会重创币圈，恐慌情绪还会蔓延到本就不稳的传统金融市场。

市场几乎按零风险定价。11 月 25 日 USDT 报 0.9987 美元，跟合规稳定币 USDC 的 0.9996 美元几乎没拉开差距，风险与赔率极不对称。

不过他们自己也说：USDT 真脱锚的概率很低，重点是赔率划算。他们的思路是借 USDT 换 USDC，或买 USDC 结算的波场看跌期权，只怕真出事时交易对手先倒了。

text:
今天凌晨两点，Anthropic 老板 Dario 破大防了。连夜手搓一篇上千词小作文自辩，狂揽 433 万阅读。

马斯克路过顺手转发，只甩了一个词：
Interesting，直接干出 284 万阅读。

苦口婆心写论文，不如世界首富一个词。互联网的残酷，在这一刻具象化了。

快速吃瓜前情提要：Anthropic 11 月 19 号刚上市，敲钟的香槟还没喝完，美媒 Axios 25 号就送了份“大礼”——爆出 Anthropic 内部有个“沉默共识”：等 AI 够强，人类迟早要交出部分决策权。顺手还扒出几年前诉讼流出的旧 PPT，上面把理想世界写成“盒子里的神统治的乌托邦”。

其实友商早就架好大炮了。奥特曼月初刚喊话“人类必须永远掌控未来”，Meta 首席 AI 官 Wang 紧跟表态“绝不接受向 AI 交权”。谁也没点名，但明眼人都知道，这帮人就差拉着大横幅堵在 Anthropic 门口骂街了。

Dario 气得睡不着，小作文拉拉杂杂写了一大堆，翻译成人话就三句：
别扣帽子！我从没想让 AI 当皇帝，古希腊罗马的历史早就证明独裁不行，AI 必须归民主管。

别偷换概念！让 AI 开车、搞抗癌药、端到端写代码，这叫“干活自动化”，不是“剥夺人类自由意志”。至于 AI 自己造 AI（递归自我改进）和抢饭碗，我都主张踩刹车。

友商别装白莲花！全行业产品都在拼命往全自动卷，谁比谁干净？某些 CEO 嘴上天天“AI 只是工具”“人类主权”，产品半行代码没改，纯属靠氛围感演戏。

听着逻辑挺严密？点开评论区，直接大型社死现场。

网友压根不接他的辩论赛，先把文风按在地上摩擦：

2933 赞的梗图直接封神：双手捧着一台“两米长的手机”刷屏——哥，真没人想看你的万字长文。

2366 赞神回复：“太长不看，祝你开心，或者节哀。”

1217 赞杀人诛心：“现在终于懂为啥 Claude Opus 说话这么啰嗦了，超智能都来了，老板你还是不会压缩字数。”

更有人精准画像：每次被质疑，你都像“被冒犯的教授在训斥本科生”；Anthropic 根本是个“小作文邪教”。

笑完字数，下面全是戳肺管子的诛心暴击：
1508 赞直接掀老底：“你说的‘合法民主监管’，不就是找你那帮自己人和左派圈子当守门人吗？”

一条金句直接戳中普通人痛点：“谢谢，我可不想让别人投票决定我怎么用自己的电脑。”——反对 AI 管我，结果你提议让一群外人投票管我？底下立马有老哥喊冤：“老板，先让安全团队别老拦着我用 Claude 聊机器学习行不？”

最狠的是两记绝杀：一张是黄仁勋拎着皮带踹门大喊“开源时间到”，吓得 Dario 抱头求饶；另一句直接用 AI 黑话判了死刑：“你的信用 Token 已经耗尽了。”

笑归笑，这场骂战扒出了 AI 圈最扎心的 4 条商业底裤：

公关战里，一旦开始做名词解释，你就已经输了。 Dario 0 关注、90 万粉，顶着学者架子讲辩证法，撞上短视频时代的站队爽感，属于拿论文去跟弹幕对线——字越多，越显得你急了。

但 Dario 有一句大实话骂得极准：“AI 只是工具”就是句鬼话。 今天哪家巨头不在卖全自动 Agent？模型越不用人操心、越能端到端把活干完，企业越肯掏钱。一边卖“替你干活的打工人”，一边喊“它只是把锤子”，本质上就是既要又要的商业精神分裂。

“AI 安全”一旦被政治化，护城河直接变负资产。 过去 Anthropic 靠“全行业最稳重”吃尽溢价，但在高度撕裂的美国舆论场，“主动求监管”在至少一半人眼里，直接等同于“既得利益者想焊死车门、卡死开源”。这种信任折价，华尔街立刻用真金白银定价——发行价 83 美元，24 号收在 81.91 美元，直接破发。

最讽刺的是，CEO 嘴上踩刹车，招股书里早把油门焊死了。 这也是 Dario 通篇装傻没敢接的死穴。翻开 Anthropic 自己的招股书：
11 月 2 日修订版还写“可能即将”跨过自设的 AI 加速红线，11 月 10 日直接按未来预期认定“已经跨过”；更炸裂的是，9 月公司代码库超 90% 都是 Claude 自己写的。嘴上还在呼吁“限制 AI 自我迭代”，家里干活的程序员都快被自家 AI 替换光了——身体比嘴诚实一万倍。

最后灵魂拷问：AI 越来越聪明，方向盘到底该归谁？

A. 巨头自律（信他们不如信我是秦始皇） 
B. 政府和民主程序管（顺便投票管管你电脑） 
C. 谁用谁自己定，少来爹味说教 
D. 彻底开源，黄仁勋皮带抽起来，谁也别想垄断

你站哪一派？评论区开麦👇
author: ZhouTalks
quoted_text:
No, I do not believe that we should “surrender human free will” to AI systems, and it’s absurd to suggest that I do. I have written hundreds of pages of essays and a constant theme in them is the need for AI to be governed by legitimate democratic processes. For millennia (going all the way back to Greek and Roman philosophers), advocates of autocracy have claimed that it leads to better, faster, or more decisive decision-making than the messy process of democracy. Even if this were true (which I doubt!), we should never sacrifice legitimacy or self-determination at the altar of efficiency or security. This argument against autocracy applies word for word against governance by AI, and I feel equally strongly that turning over governance to AI is a bad idea.

No one who had carefully read my writing or my interviews could reasonably conclude that I believe anything different. For example in an interview on CBS a couple months ago, I specifically called for AI to be governed democratically. I call for the same in Policy on the AI Exponential, Machines of Loving Grace, and The Adolescence of Technology, and We Must Pace the Frontier. Machines of Loving Grace contains an extended section on using AI to revitalize democracy, and discusses the use of AI as an aid to citizens in their decision-making, "aggregat[ing] opinions and driv[ing] consensus among citizens, resolving conflict, finding common ground, and seeking compromise.” The clear and obvious implication is that humans should remain the ones making political and governance decisions. The Adolescence of Technology has an entire section on fighting against AI-driven tyranny, and I even discuss the danger of AI labs usurping power and come out strongly against it — by implication, this definitely includes an AI lab usurping power and giving it to AI itself!

If I thought any of this was a good idea, I would be advocating for it in public, just as I have not been afraid to advocate for many, many unpopular views over the last few years. But I am not advocating for it, because I think turning over governance to AI is a terrible idea.

Separately, I think there is frequent conflation (including in this article) between the idea of “surrendering human free will” to AI in some grand sense of global governance, and the more prosaic idea that as AI systems advance, they become capable of doing specific tasks in a more automated way. This is not AI “running the world,” but AI driving a car, designing a cancer drug, or writing software end-to-end. Here, my view is mixed. AI doing more complete or larger tasks is economically valuable and can drive important advances in software, medicine, transportation, energy, etc. It is clearly desirable in many cases and will save a lot of lives. But it has downsides as well, and in some areas it may not be worth it.

For example, using AI too autonomously to build the next generation of AI systems (known as recursive self-improvement, or RSI) may cause AI to improve faster than we can control or adjust to it, so we may want limits on this process. As we said publicly in early November, we don’t expect it to be safe for Claude to build successive frontier models fully autonomously, without meaningful human supervision or understanding. Second, in some contexts, using AI in too end-to-end a manner may be a cause of serious job disruption, and it may make sense to slow or even stop some AI deployments to give people more time to adapt. Third, while the use of AI for alignment research is an incredibly valuable tool, it must be done with caution, because we may not be able to trust the work of the AI system. Finally, in many cases, humans would simply prefer to do some activities themselves, so they can stay deeply engaged in what matters to them, even if AI can do those activities better. There are countless other examples and hard cases. I don’t think there are any easy answers here, nor is there (nor should there be) any single decision-maker: some of these decisions will be made by society, some by government, some by AI companies, and some in a decentralized manner by individuals expressing their own preferences as consumers, which may differ from the preferences of others.

I don't think that other AI leaders or AI companies have significantly different views from me on whether specific tasks should be automated. Certainly the products that they offer don’t differ materially in their orientation towards automation of tasks; every company seems to be releasing models more and more capable of task automation (as that’s been the general consequence of scaling up AI training), and every company claims to understand there are risks and downsides of such automation and to offer safeguards. If anything, Anthropic has been the most vocal and the most proactive about acknowledging these downsides and trying to address them. For instance, it’s fairly absurd to cite my statement that fully autonomous weapons might “one day be needed for the defense of democracy” as differing from that of other AI companies, when I was willing to risk Anthropic’s future as a company to refuse to allow our existing AI models to be used for autonomous weapons even in the face of legal sanctions, and no other AI company did the same.

To summarize, as applied to grand questions of how we govern increasingly capable AI, I have been vocal and consistent that AI needs to be governed by a legitimate, democratic process and that “surrendering human free will” to AI systems is a terrible idea. As applied to automation of specific tasks by or for people, my views are more mixed, but I don’t think they differ from those of other AI companies — most other companies seem to be offering similar products and confronting similar tradeoffs without having perfect answers to them. What is happening is that there’s a sort of vibes-based commercial and political positioning that some AI CEOs are engaging in, where they repeat slogans like “human control and agency,” or “AI should be just a tool,” without actually doing anything different in their products or taking seriously the difficult questions that lie behind these slogans.

text:
无聊去看了一下最近 Polymarket 的动向，又是请亚马逊的前 CFO 来当 自己的CFO，又是请高盛高管、Uber前联创进驻。从去年纽交所母公司 ICE 投了 20 亿美元开始，Polymarket 的打法已经整体转向机构化。现在它要拉的是华尔街的资金和流动性，散户和加密原生用户已经不是重点。

Vitalik 是预测市场最早的关注者之一，十年前就在写 futarchy、写预测市场怎么帮人类做决策，一直很关心这个领域，也是 Polymarket 很早的支持者。Polymarket 的创始人 Shayne 自己在简介里写着：2014 年起就信仰以太坊。
可以说Polymarket 是以太坊精神长出来最成功的应用之一。现在它要去对接最传统的金融机构了。

再回头看以太坊基金会，它作为一个 NGO，没有marketing 部门，跟各种机构以及主权意识保持距离，它的使命甚至某种意义上可以理解为—不断地进行 walk away 测试，降低自己在生态里的话语权，逐渐权力下放，实现去中心化，最终可能是让自己这个 NGO 消亡。目前它只专精做技术方向的事情，隐私、AI安全、抗量子是未来工作的重点。这就是高岭之花带给你的一种迷思和无奈感。你知道它冰清玉洁，你怎么能让高岭之花去接客呢？

于是就出现了一个断层：以太坊生态里最有商业想象力的项目，正大步走进华尔街；生态的精神中心却必须和这一切保持距离。两边都没错，但中间是空的。

所幸去年EF 那个 Crops 宣言之后，基金会Spin-off 出来一些以太坊的民间节点，做机构化。我差不多都见过这些节点的负责人。比如像狂买以太坊的 Tom Lee 的 Bitmine 吧，现在已经拿了 5% 的以太坊代币份额，囤了这么多币，民间已经称它为第二以太坊基金会了。

但行好事，莫问前程。我还是相信如果加密有新东西，会首先爆发在以太坊上。Believe in SomETHing

text:
Google 不直接看 ACP 客户端是谁，而是看 agy 进程本身。

agy acp 启动后，本地 CLI 负责所有后端请求和登录。ACP 只是本地 stdin/stdout 通道。但 agy 有 telemetry，客户端在 initialize 时会发 clientInfo（名字、版本），agy 可能上报；再加上使用模式（自动批准、调度任务、多会话编排）和纯编辑器交互明显不同。

Paseo 是多 Agent 编排平台，行为更接近 FAQ 禁止的 “wrapping”，而 T3/Zed 被 Google 员工明确说成安全薄客户端。所以同样走 acp，风险不一样。最稳还是官方 App 或改用 API Key。

当前的恐慌情绪，已经不仅仅只作用在STH。LTH也同样承受大面积亏损，而且净持仓一直在减少。

每次看到TG出现这样的提醒，内心都会咯噔一下。如果我们复盘过去2个月，LTH持仓下降是有多重因素导致的：

最开始在8月初是因为Coldcard硬件钱包发生严重安全事故，导致LTH大规模转移。

此后8-9月行情强势拉升，有部分LTH选择获利了结，但当时市场情绪普遍乐观，LTH派发并没有给价格带来太大的压力，反而从侧面说明需求的强劲。

然而，到了10月以后随着宏观流动性收紧，投资者风险偏好降低，这种压力就慢慢体现出来。

尤其是其中有大量长期托管的ETF筹码转入Coinbase卖出，反映到链上就是我们看到LTH在加速派发。

直至当前仍然是市场最主要的卖方压力来源。

比如在图2中看到的11月23日晚LTH转入Coinbase的9,327枚BTC，就是ETF的筹码。当时恰逢“老黄回归英伟达”的利好放出，但随着卖压进场，反弹行情被打断。

我觉得这应该是当前需要重点关注的几个核心数据之一。只有在LTH净持仓曲线开始逐渐转变，才能说市场情绪得到有效修复。

text:
「大空头」迈克尔·伯里 @burrytracker 说自己「暂时几乎全部做多」。

摊开持仓，最大的三笔分落在拉美、澳大利亚和中国，手里还留着约 25% 现金。京东( $JD )尤其值得看：除了正股，他还持有最远到 2029 年才到期的京东看涨期权。

11 月 25 日，伯里在个人专栏披露，趁科技股再度走弱，他卖掉了手里最后一半纳斯达克 100 指数看跌期权。此前做空赚到的钱，一部分留成现金，一部分正在买入他认为被低估的股票。

和京东并列为主要持仓的，是拉美电商 MercadoLibre ( $MELI ) 和澳大利亚家居电商 Temple & Webster ( $TPW )。伯里给出的理由也很直接：美股估值仍高，他在海外找到了更愿意出手的价格。

中国资产是这张持仓表里容易被忽略的一条线。

除了京东，他还持有比亚迪、腾讯、美团、海底捞和海尔智家。从汽车、家电到餐饮和互联网平台，一共点名了六家。另一边，他的美股多仓里有露露乐蒙、勃肯、Adobe 和 PayPal，还持有房利美、房地美的次级优先股。

再看英伟达 $NVDA。伯里此前为防股价急弹买入的长期看涨期权，价值已经翻倍，他仍然拿着。与此同时，他也给下一次做空设了两个条件：股价回到 200 美元附近，市场情绪重新乐观。目前他点名保留的两笔看跌期权，是 Palantir 和大都会人寿。

所以，伯里觉得见底了吗？他对部分个股确实给出了判断：连续下跌后，已经有股票进入他的买入区间。至于指数，他还算了另一笔账：波动率上升后，连一些与 AI 基建只有间接关联的公司，看跌期权都已经很贵。此时兑现指数空单、买入低估个股、留出四分之一现金，这三件事可以同时成立。

text:
Inference Proof by @lucidcomputing is going to be a consequential benchmark for verifiability in AI and we are looking forward to working with them on this.

One of the central questions of AI safety is, given a prompt, can anyone independently verify which model produced the response to it?

Answering this question involves checking if the inference provider executed the model honestly with no altered weights, prompts or reply while also ensuring this check can happen to a commercially-available CPU by anyone.

Existing AI benchmarks have never focused on measuring the cost of producing the verification certificate for the whole inference track and verifying the certificate.
author: DavideCrapis
quoted_text:
Existing AI benchmarks drive a race to the top on capabilities alone. We don't have a benchmark to drive a race to the top on making AI verifiable.

Today, together with our partners, we're launching Inference Proofs: an open source benchmark and a public map of the systems that prove AI inference.

The question it tracks: can anyone independently verify which model produced an answer, and what does that check cost?

Today, every answer from an AI service arrives on trust. You're told which model wrote it, but can't verify it.

A proof of inference changes that. Anyone can verify that a reply came from a committed model, on an ordinary CPU, with no GPU and no access to the weights.

Not long ago this was a thought experiment. Today, open source provers can prove inference of a 400B-parameter model.

But every team reports on its own model, its own hardware, and its own way of measuring. That makes the systems hard to compare.

So every system on Inference Proofs gets the same request: a 512-token prompt and a 512-token reply. The prompts were drawn by a public randomness beacon after the rules were frozen. Nobody picked the inputs, including us.

Prover correctness first, prover performance second.

Our tampering checks change one weight, one prompt token, or one reply token, and the verifier must refuse. Every verdict has to be reached with no GPU and no model file on disk.

Inference Proofs is open source, public good infrastructure, convened by Lucid Computing, with the precious help of those great partners: @aisafetysg, @attestable, GPAI Lab, @StarkWareLtd, the @ethereumfndn dAI Team, @0xMiden, @zksecurityXYZ, @lagrangedev, @equilibrium_co, @eigenlabs / Yukon, @0xPolygon and @class_lambda.

Thank you to everyone who helped launch it. This is a first step toward a broader, collaborative open source AI verification ecosystem.

text:
是哪些因素引发了昨晚美股V回来？昨晚10月核心 PCE升到 3.3%，高于预期和前值，确定了12月加息，也说明通胀还很顽强，引发了无差别抛售——纳指-4.6%，费半-8%，黄金破3500。但收盘则大幅收窄跌幅：道指上涨约0.31%，完成近年来少见的千点逆转；标普500-0.23%；纳指-0.68%。在盘中费城半导体创下了新低，但是纳指并没创新低。聊聊有哪些因素触发了昨晚的反弹。
1、跟很多人讨论的并不一样，个人角度昨晚亚特兰大联储将四季度GDP增长估算从3.2%下调至2.9%是反弹的催化剂。财经日历将GDPNow下调时间04:45 PM GMT正好是美东时间 11:45 AM，这个时间点恰恰是费城半导体盘中的最低点。

如果把亚特兰大联储GDP增速估算放到一起看（配图1），能明显看出增速在走弱的、这也扭转了市场对于联储未来持续加息的担忧（至少持续鹰派的基础在动摇）

此数据公布时点与股票加速回升接近，从这个角度看才是昨晚美股止跌回升的第一驱动力。正好核心pce走高引发加息以及未来更强鹰派的预期导致抛售，然后GDP放缓又打消了持续鹰派的担忧。

为什么亚特兰大GDP增速下调很关键，因为它也引发了美元指数的盘中小幅跳水、美元走弱对风险资产压制也会减少。

2、在这大空头昨天的Substack文章中表示，他卖掉了纳斯达克100看跌期权头寸的最后一半，整体组合较此前更偏多，暂时几乎全部持有多头方向的头寸。虽然昨天白天burry就发了这篇文章，彭博对此的报道则是在凌晨1点。权威媒体的报道引发的广泛传播，可能比原始发帖时间更影响短线行情。

3、然后凌晨万斯再次表态并保证老黄没有受到任何调查。
再就是美国联邦通信委员会（FCC）正式为SpaceX的太空数据中心计划放行，批准其发射100万颗卫星，组建名为“Starmind”的AI算力星座。
这些都带动了市场情绪的进一步反弹。

当然还有资金的因素也很关键，昨晚QQQ最低约607.76美元，上周五低点为606.23美元，两者只差约0.25%。它在开盘急跌后，晚上午再次靠近这一带，最终没有跌破。经历连续下跌后，很多短线交易者都会盯住前一次恐慌低点。如果价格再次靠近那里，卖盘却无法把指数压出新低，交易者面临的选择就会发生变化：
1）已有空头可以兑现利润，避免反弹吞掉收益。
2）原本准备等待破位再追空的资金，可能暂缓行动。
3）做反弹的资金有了相对清楚的止损参照，敢于开始买入。
4）一旦价格突破当天此前的反弹高点，部分短线空头可能被迫回补。
而且美股周四休市周五半天交易，对于已经从下跌中获利的空头，继续持仓意味着承担假期政策消息、公司声明或其他事件带来的跳空风险。

所以总的来说：
亚特兰大联储下调GDP增速扭转了市场对于美联储持续鹰派的预期、同时引发美元指数小幅跳水、带动美股扭头向上。股市在前低附近出现承接，随后空头止盈、保护性仓位调整与美元避险需求回落相互强化；
伯里减掉纳指看跌期权的消息扩大传播，万斯保证老黄没有受到调查，fcc批准了spacex的太空数据中心，这些利好事件都在助力这波反弹。

那怎么看昨晚美股的走势？
1）无差别的抛售可能接近尾声，这段时间市场经历了一段不管什么资产一起卖的阶段，昨晚核心PCE偏鹰对市场是利空，但利空砸出的低点被收回，也是空头力量衰竭的信号。

从这个点上，深V的意义还是蛮大的，

2）近期市场已经消化了太多的利空事件，如果本周后半周没有大的利空出来，短期内反弹应该是可以持续的。这可以说是最悲观情绪开始稍稍缓解，但离风险偏好已经全面转向乐观还有很大的距离。

这个距离就是上周这里https://t.co/j3LtXaOfEL最后部分聊到的后续三个要素：
（1）油价、通胀和利率走势
上周沃勒要加息50个基点鹰派的讲话也把市场吓到到了，虽然昨晚美债利率跌回了沃勒讲话前，市场仍需要议息会议的表态，才能有更清晰的预期；

（2）AI政策
相比上周本周老黄回归自然让市场对之后GPU迭代放缓、供应链受损的担忧减少、但市场还要看两党关于AI的斗法预期程度。（不一定真要等到斗法真正发生、而是只要能清晰未来斗法的程度与现在市场预期的偏离程度，市场往往提前反应）

（3）商业化
但AI质疑的表外债、生态链内融资问题，仍然没有解。这就要靠AI商业化来给答案。

今晚10月PCE数据整体上看就一个“通胀顽强+消费疲软+收入尚可”的组合
1、通胀：粘性高，核心年率还在上行 → 支持美联储维持鹰派立场，12月议息会议25个基点概率更大；
2、消费：实际支出停滞，是增长最软的环节，意味着高物价已在压制需求；
3、收入与储蓄：收入回升（月率0.7%），储蓄率上升（4.1%），家庭资产负债表暂时还撑得住，储蓄率上升也是实际消费支出停滞多原因；
4.、投资/制造：耐用品订单温和正增长，AI相关资本支出仍在提供支撑。

对市场而言，通胀数据偏鹰，消费数据偏谨慎，整体更支持“高利率持续、增长放缓但未崩”的叙事，但也没到硬着陆的状态。
